title: GPT-6 Astra Day-1 support
body:
## Summary

Add day-one GPT-6 Astra support to Codex, OpenAI API, and GitHub Copilot. Codex now identifies as client 0.153.4, resolving Astra's older-client rejection; Astra effort aliases preserve native max reasoning and parallel tool calls. Register provider-specific limits and pricing, including Codex Fast's 2.5x multiplier.

Curate GitHub Copilot to the agreed 14 models, with GPT-6 Astra first. Refresh verified Copilot capabilities, derive the fallback catalog from the same registry, and keep announced retirements and explicitly removed models out of live discovery and saved model catalogs. Local removals are documented separately from GitHub's upstream deprecations.

Two commits:
1. Codex/OpenAI Astra support, client identity, pricing, and regression coverage.
2. Copilot Astra support, the 14-model catalog, and discovery/cache regression coverage.

⚠️ base-red inherited: #12732

## Validation

- [x] Change type: provider
- [x] Focused Astra/Codex/OpenAI tests: 89 passing; provider translate-path golden tests: 3 passing after updating only Codex 0.149.0 → 0.153.4 headers.
- [x] After the urgent 0.153.4 update: 80 Astra/identity/discovery/executor/golden tests passing.
- [x] Copilot catalog/discovery/DB/executor regressions: 114 passing (117 with the provider golden suite).
- [x] `npm run typecheck:core`
- [x] `npm run check:provider-consistency` and `npm run check:provider-assets`
- [x] `npm run gen:provider-reference` and `npm run check:docs-all`
- [x] `npm run lint -- --pass-on-unpruned-suppressions`; plain lint reports existing unused suppression entries. No lint rules or suppression files were changed.
- [x] Pre-commit formatting/ESLint, documentation sync, any-budget and tracked-artifact checks. Stash backup disabled to comply with repository rules.
- [x] Based on the current upstream `release/v3.8.51` (`c3945a724`); no merge commit.
- [x] Production changes include automated regression coverage.
- [x] CI follow-up: refreshed the remaining catalog-dependent fixtures across 9 test files; all 184 tests in those files pass locally using the repository polyfill and isolated-data preload.
- [x] Reproduced the failing CI files against both the PR and unchanged base c3945a724: the 15 remaining local failures are in the same inherited error-handling suites. API typecheck (glm.ts TS2554) and malformed reset-aware-model-family changelog fragment also fail on the base.
- [x] Latest-head CI rerun (49ca57e35) inspected: all four unit shards now contain only the 15 baseline-reproduced failures; catalog regressions are gone. Vitest, docs, ESLint and security scans pass. Fast Quality/API typechecks still fail on the inherited glm.ts TS2554; merge integrity still fails on the inherited changelog fragment. Coverage was not measured and production build was skipped. Local Vitest passes all 465 tests in 51 files. The first full unit phase finished with 37,315 passed / 26 failed / 22 skipped; the chained dashboard and serial phases did not run. Of those failures, 15 reproduce in the original CI-failure files on the base, 9 additional failures also reproduce identically on the base, and 2 load-sensitive timing checks pass when rerun serially.

## Coverage Notes

Tests cover catalog order/limits, price calculation, Codex identity and effort aliases, Responses routing, fallback parity, exclusion of retired/locally removed models, and legacy/new synchronized model caches. The capability fixture contains only model metadata, without credentials or account policies. Full coverage results are pending CI.

## Reviewer Notes

- Codex Astra completed a live request with client 0.153.3 during development. The subsequent 0.153.4 bump is covered by identity/discovery/executor tests; inference with 0.153.4, OpenAI API and Copilot was not live-tested.
- Copilot metadata was read from the authenticated models API. Catalog inclusion does not grant an account model access.
- October 2 retirements are deliberately applied early. Sonnet 4.6 is locally removed despite GitHub's annual-plan exception.
- No persisted user credentials or combo configurations are rewritten; catalog filters hide removed entries on read/sync. Other providers retain their model catalogs.


## CI follow-up

The first run exposed stale expectations for retired Copilot models in the fallback ladder, static/HTTP catalogs, context overrides, live-catalog reconciliation and VS Code import metadata. Fixtures now use retained models and preserve their behavioral assertions; the Opus fallback explicitly skips retired tiers and reaches Sonnet 5. No removed model was restored. The input-limit assertion follows the existing documented registry-input precedence, clamped to the synced provider window.

Inherited failures reproduced at c3945a724 include public error redaction/passthrough (HuggingChat, image generation, Kiro, Z.ai, stream and dashboard errors), API typecheck and changelog integrity. These remain separate from this feature under the repository base-red policy; tracking issue: #12732.

The additional baseline comparison ran 70 tests serially on both c3945a724 and the PR: both report 61 passed / 9 failed, with identical failing test names. The catalog event-loop and sanitizer timing tests pass in that serial rerun.

Latest reviewed CI run: https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/actions/runs/33935220973 (head 49ca57e35). Remaining unit failure counts by shard: 3 / 8 / 3 / 1. All are reproduced in the unchanged base. The two-commit structure is preserved.

title: Direct (non-combo) requests to a custom OpenAI-compatible model ignore supportsVision and force-route images to hardcoded glm/glm-4.6v
body:
### OmniRoute Version

3.8.50

### Installation Method

Docker / Docker Compose

### Operating System

Linux

### OS Version

Ubuntu 24.04

### Node.js Version

_No response_

### Provider(s) Involved

Custom OpenAI-compatible provider (self-hosted vLLM on RunPod); unrelated GLM Coding provider is the wrongly-selected fallback target

### Model(s) Involved

orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-NVFP4

### Client Tool

Direct API request (fetch/curl to /v1/chat/completions)

### Description

OmniRoute's vision-bridge logic hardcodes a fallback vision model (glm/glm-4.6v in this build) for any chat completion request that contains image content, regardless of whether the target model already declares vision support. For a custom OpenAI-compatible model added under "Custom Models" (with "Vision capable" explicitly checked), a request sent directly to that model (i.e. not through a Combo) is still silently redirected to the hardcoded fallback model instead of being sent to the configured model. In our case the fallback model isn't present in the connected GLM account's live catalog, so the request fails outright with a 400 instead of reaching the intended model.

This appears to be the same underlying issue as #8032 and #2484. The v3.8.50 changelog entry "fix(routing): consult customModels supportsVision flag in Combo routing (#9195)" seems to have scoped the fix to Combo routing only, leaving the direct/non-combo request path unpatched.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In OmniRoute, add a custom OpenAI-compatible provider pointing at a self-hosted vLLM instance.
2. Under Custom Models, add a model (path-shaped id, e.g. `orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-NVFP4`), and check "Vision capable" in its edit form.
3. Send a chat completion request directly to that model id via /v1/chat/completions (no Combo involved), with a message containing an `image_url` content part, e.g.:
```json
{
  "model": "orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-NVFP4",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": [
        { "type": "text", "text": "What color is this image? One word." },
        { "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "data:image/png;base64,<1x1 png>" } }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
4. Observe the response.

### Expected Behavior

Since the target model is explicitly flagged `supportsVision: true` (via the "Vision capable" checkbox in Custom Models), the request should be sent to that model as-is, with no model substitution.

### Actual Behavior

The request fails with a 400 error: {"error":{"message":"Model 'glm-4.6v' is not available in the active live catalog for provider 'glm'.","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"bad_request"}}

OmniRoute is attempting to silently substitute `glm/glm-4.6v` for the requested model purely because the request contains image content, ignoring the requested model's own `supportsVision: true` flag. It only surfaces as a visible error because that specific GLM checkpoint isn't present in our connected GLM account's catalog — but even where it is present, this would mean the configured model is never actually used for vision requests sent outside of a Combo.

### Test Impact

Needs a new unit test

### Error Logs / Output

```shell
Status: 400
Response body:
{"error":{"message":"Model 'glm-4.6v' is not available in the active live catalog for provider 'glm'.","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"bad_request"}}

For reference, a plain text-only request (no image) to the same model id ("orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-NVFP4") completes normally and is served by the correct model - only requests containing image content trigger the substitution.
```

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional Context

- Single account, custom provider connection ("vLLM-Runpod"), no proxy involved.
- The custom model's "Vision capable" checkbox was confirmed checked via the model edit form before testing.
- As a workaround, we are wrapping the same model in a single-model, priority-strategy Combo instead of connecting directly, on the theory that Combo routing correctly consults the supportsVision flag per #9195 while the direct/non-combo path does not. Will update this issue once that's confirmed.
- `glm-4.6v` does not correspond to anything we configured; we do have a GLM Coding connection, but its live catalog does not include this checkpoint.

### Validation Plan

- Add a custom OpenAI-compatible provider + a Custom Model with a path-shaped id and "Vision capable" checked.
- Send a chat completion request directly (no Combo) to that model id with an image_url content part.
- Expect: the request reaches the configured model and returns a normal response, with no attempt to substitute any other model regardless of whether that other model is actually available.
- Regression check: the same request via a Combo containing this model should continue to work as it does today (per #9195).

title: fix(compression): drain the worker pool queue when worker construction throws
body:
## Summary

Prevents the compression worker pool from retaining queued request bodies when worker construction throws synchronously.

This is deliberately a containment fix: it removes the queue-retention failure mode and makes fail-open behavior observable, but it does not repair the standalone build's worker resolution or worker dependency packaging. Compression still returns the original body when no worker can be created.

## Changes

- Drain every queued job fail-open when worker construction throws.
- Permanently short-circuit only known structural spawn failures; retry transient and unknown failures on the next request wave.
- Settle in-flight work on worker errors, exits, timeouts, `postMessage` throws, and pool shutdown.
- Add rate-limited, sanitized fail-open warnings.
- Pass a `URL` object to the LLMLingua worker constructor on Node.js 21+.
- Register the regression suite in Stryker's `tap.testFiles`.

## Validation

- `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/compression/compression-worker-pool-jam.test.ts` — 14 passed
- Adjacent compression and LLMLingua regression suites — 68 passed
- PR-mode complexity ratchets — unchanged (`complexity` 9 → 9; `cognitive-complexity` 3 → 3)
- Focused Prettier and `git diff --check` — passed
- Three specialized review passes found no remaining actionable defects.

The release branch is currently red independently of this change. The inherited failures include the `glm.ts` TS2554 error, invalid changelog fragment, provider-asset provenance object, mutation-list drift for `quotaScoring.ts`, and unrelated unit-test failures.

⚠️ base-red inherited: #12732

## Tests Added

- `tests/unit/compression/compression-worker-pool-jam.test.ts`

## Out of scope

- Repairing the Turbopack worker module-context rewrite.
- Repairing the dependency closure of the separately bundled compression worker.

title: feat(usage): redeem GLM Coding Plan Reset Cards from Provider Limits
body:
## What

z.ai sells **Coding Plan Reset Cards** — a card clears an exhausted GLM coding-plan window (the 5-hour or the weekly one) ahead of its natural rollover. OmniRoute already polls z.ai's quota endpoint and shows `nextResetTime`, but that read is passive: there was no way to redeem a card, so a user holding one had to leave the dashboard and do it on z.ai.

This wires the redemption into the Provider Limits UI that already exists for Codex reset credits, for `glm` / `glm-cn` / `glmt` / `zai`.

## Why the Codex flow could not simply be reused

`codexResetCredits.ts` is gated to `provider === "codex"` + `authType === "oauth"` and posts to ChatGPT's `wham/rate-limit-reset-credits`. Neither transfers: z.ai authenticates with the connection's **API key**, and the whole quota-row → button → picker chain was Codex-only at four independent points (`quotaParsing.ts` never emitted a reset row for the GLM family, `providerColumns.ts` had no column, `computeCanRedeemResetCredit` and the redemption hook both hard-compared to `"codex"`).

The UI, picker, confirmation modal and idempotency handling are reused as-is; only the gates widen and the endpoint becomes provider-chosen.

## Upstream contract

Two endpoints, next to the quota endpoint already in use:

```
GET  /api/biz/customer-package-reset/list?targetType=PERSONAL
POST /api/biz/customer-package-reset/use
     {"targetType":"PERSONAL","resetType":"WEEK","recordId":124128,"requestId":"<uuid>"}
  →  {"code":200,"msg":"Operation successful","data":124128,"success":true}
```

Two things worth flagging, both handled:

1. **Same credential as the quota route.** Verified directly against the live API: with no auth header it answers `code: 1001` ("Authentication parameter not received in Header"); with a Bearer token it answers `code: 401` ("token expired or incorrect") — identical to `/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit`. So no new credential type, and the existing API-key plumbing (including the team-plan `bigmodel-organization` / `bigmodel-project` headers) carries over unchanged.
2. **Failures arrive inside an HTTP-200 envelope.** `success: false` + `code` carry the real status, so `response.ok` alone is not a success check. `isGlmResetCardEnvelopeOk()` / `getGlmResetCardEnvelopeStatus()` centralise that, mapping `1001` → 401.

`requestId` is z.ai's idempotency key, so it is wired to the picker's existing per-selection key: a retried redemption cannot burn two cards.

## Cost control

Surfacing the banked count costs one extra request per quota poll, so it is only issued for keys that actually report a resettable window (`session`/`weekly`) — a pay-as-you-go key can never hold a card — and `fetchGlmResetCardCount()` never throws, so a card-less account or a transient upstream failure still renders its quotas.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `open-sse/config/glmProvider.ts` | `GLM_RESET_CARD_URLS` + `buildGlmResetCardFetch()`, mirroring `GLM_QUOTA_URLS`/`buildGlmQuotaFetch()` (both regions, team headers) |
| `open-sse/services/usage/glmResetCards.ts` | new — transport + envelope parsing, no DB access |
| `open-sse/services/usage/glm.ts` | fold the banked count into `getGlmUsage`, gated + best-effort |
| `src/lib/usage/glmResetCards.ts` | new — connection-aware list/redeem, mirrors `codexResetCredits.ts` |
| `src/app/api/usage/glm-reset-card/route.ts` | new — `GET` lists, `POST` redeems (Zod-validated, `sanitizeErrorMessage`) |
| `quotaParsing.ts`, `providerColumns.ts`, `utils.tsx`, `useCodexResetCreditRedemption.ts` | widen the four Codex-only gates; endpoint chosen per provider |
| `src/i18n/messages/en.json` | two strings said "Codex" for what is now a shared flow |

## Tests

`tests/unit/glm-reset-cards.test.ts` (10 cases): envelope parsing incl. the real card-less payload, window derived per bucket with an explicit `resetType` winning, the `1001`/`401`-inside-200 failure envelopes, URL/header construction per region and for team plans, an end-to-end redemption asserting the exact wire body, `409` when nothing is banked, the non-GLM provider rejected before any upstream call, best-effort behaviour on failure, and the widened UI gate.

## Verification status — please read

- The **API contract above is verified against the live z.ai API** (the auth probe, and the list/use exchange captured from a real redemption).
- **The suite was not run locally**: this was written on a machine with no Node.js runtime available, so `npm run lint`, `typecheck:core` and the test suites could not be executed and the pre-commit hooks did not run (no `node_modules`, hooks not installed — not bypassed). CI is the first real execution; happy to fix anything it surfaces.
- **One inferred detail.** The list payload I could capture had both buckets empty (`fiveHourResets: []`, `weekResets: []`) because the card had just been spent, so the *per-item* shape is not directly observed. Parsing is therefore defensive in the same style as `parseResetCredit` in the Codex lib — the id is matched across `recordId`/`id`/`packageResetId`/`resetId`, the window falls back to the bucket the item came from, and an item without an id is skipped. `recordId` and `resetType: "WEEK"` are confirmed from the redeem request. If you have a populated `list` response, that would pin the last detail down.
- Scope limited to `targetType: PERSONAL`, the target z.ai's own dashboard uses for individual coding-plan keys.

⚠️ base-red inherited: #12732

title: [BUG] Claude Web fails in Docker: tls-client asset resolver looks for nonexistent linux-ubuntu-amd64 v1.16.0 .so
body:
### OmniRoute Version

3.8.50

### Installation Method

Docker / Docker Compose

### Operating System

macOS

### OS Version

Sequioa 17.7.9

### Node.js Version

22.22.2

### Provider(s) Involved

claude web cookie 

### Model(s) Involved

_No response_

### Client Tool

claude code

### Description

## Environment

- OmniRoute version: 3.8.50
- Installation method: Docker
- Host: macOS with Docker Desktop
- Container architecture: linux/amd64
- Provider: Claude Web

## Problem

Adding/checking a Claude Web session cookie always returns `Invalid`.
The cookie is not actually validated because OmniRoute fails before making the request.

## Error

```text
No tls-client release asset found for tls-client-linux-ubuntu-amd64-1.16.0.so
```

## Reproduction

1. Start the OmniRoute Docker image `diegosouzapw/omniroute:latest`
2. Open the dashboard
3. Add Claude Web session cookie
4. Click Check cookie
5. Dashboard shows Invalid; server/provider error reports the missing TLS asset above

## Expected behaviour

The Docker image should include or download the correct TLS-client binary so Claude Web session validation can run.

## Notes

This appears related to #8579 (TLS-client-node binary resolution/download) and #5088 (`Invalid` masking the underlying TLS failure).

Please do not request or include session-cookie values; none are included in this report.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Docker Desktop on macOS and ensure Docker is running.

2. Start OmniRoute v3.8.50 with:

   docker run --rm -it \
     -p 127.0.0.1:8086:20128 \
     -v "$HOME/.omniroute:/app/data" \
     diegosouzapw/omniroute:latest

3. Open http://localhost:8086 in a browser.

4. Sign in to the OmniRoute dashboard and open the Providers/Connections page.

5. Choose Claude Web and select “Add session cookie”.

6. Paste a valid Cookie header from an authenticated Claude Web browser session.
   Do not include the literal “Cookie:” prefix.

7. Click “Check cookie”.

8. The UI reports “Invalid”, and the TLS-client loader error is:

   No tls-client release asset found for tls-client-linux-ubuntu-amd64-1.16.0.so

### Expected Behavior

When a valid Claude Web session-cookie header is pasted and “Check cookie” is clicked, OmniRoute should resolve the correct tls-client native binary for the current Docker/Linux AMD64 runtime, establish the required browser-like TLS connection, and validate the session successfully.

The dashboard should show that the Claude Web credential is valid and allow the connection to be saved and used. It should not display “Invalid” or fail with a missing tls-client release-asset error.

### Actual Behavior

The cookie check fails before validation. The UI says “Invalid” and the server reports:

No tls-client release asset found for tls-client-linux-ubuntu-amd64-1.16.0.so

### Test Impact

Needs a new unit test

### Error Logs / Output

```shell
Session Cookie Label
Required cookie: sessionKey. Paste the Cookie header value from your own signed-in Claude Web web session. Do not include the Cookie: prefix.

Check cookie
Invalid

No tls-client release asset found for tls-client-linux-ubuntu-amd64-1.16.0.so

[Claude Web credential validation]
Error: No tls-client release asset found for tls-client-linux-ubuntu-amd64-1.16.0.so

Dashboard result: Invalid
```

title: refactor(combo): split executeTarget into gates, attempt, and loop
body:
## Summary

`handleComboChatInner`'s 1327-line `executeTarget` is now three modules: pre-dispatch skip gates, the retry/side-effect loop, and the setTry/safety-timer dispatcher. `combo.ts` goes from 4080 to 2234 lines (`split("\n").length`). Round-robin stays in `combo.ts`.

## Why

`combo.ts` sat on its file-size freeze (4080). The leftover bulk was `executeTarget`, not more types. ROADMAP 3.8.52 lists this split under PREPARE.

## What moved

| Module | Role | LOC |
|---|---|---|
| `open-sse/services/combo/attemptLoopTypes.ts` | `AttemptLoopState` / `AttemptLoopDeps` | 118 |
| `open-sse/services/combo/executeTargetGates.ts` | 10 skip gates, breaker through admission | 330 |
| `open-sse/services/combo/executeTargetClassify.ts` | input-bound / body-specific 400 / homogeneous remainder | 55 |
| `open-sse/services/combo/executeTargetAttempt.ts` | retry loop + pin/LKGP/quality/cooldown | 1205 (frozen; classify already extracted) |
| `open-sse/services/combo/comboAttemptLoop.ts` | setTry, #11804 safety timer, speculative tasks, cooldown redispatch | 576 |

title: Memory reranking silently disabled when REQUIRE_API_KEY=true (401 on internal loopback call)
body:
# Memory reranking silently disabled when `REQUIRE_API_KEY=true`

**Version:** 3.8.50
**Component:** `src/lib/memory/retrieval.ts` — `applyRerank()`
**Impact:** memory reranking never runs on any instance with API-key enforcement enabled. Silent — no user-visible error.

---

## Summary

`applyRerank()` calls OmniRoute's **own** `/v1/rerank` endpoint over loopback, but sends no `Authorization` header. When `REQUIRE_API_KEY=true`, that endpoint requires a bearer token, so the gateway is refused by itself with **HTTP 401** on every retrieval.

Because reranking is intentionally fail-open, retrieval keeps working — just without reranking. Nothing surfaces to the user, and the deployment silently loses relevance ranking on every memory lookup.

On our instance this produced **9,616 failures in 6 hours**, the single largest error source, unnoticed for weeks.

---

## Root cause

`src/lib/memory/retrieval.ts:141`

```ts
// Loopback rerank URL — localhost only, never routed over the network.
const RERANK_LOOPBACK_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1/rerank";
```

`applyRerank()` (same file, ~line 150):

```ts
const res = await fetch(RERANK_LOOPBACK_URL, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },   // ← no Authorization
  body: JSON.stringify(body),
  signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000),
});

if (!res.ok) {
  log.warn("memory.rerank.http_fail", { status: res.status, model: rerankProviderModel });
  return items;                                       // fail-open, silent
}
```

The `/v1/rerank` route sits behind the same API-key middleware as the rest of `/v1/*` (`enforceApiKeyPolicy`, `authType: "apikey"`, `authHeader: "bearer"`). Loopback origin does not exempt it — the `hostname === "127.0.0.1"` check further down that file is an SSRF allowlist for *provider node base URLs*, unrelated to caller authentication.

---

## Reproduction

Environment: `REQUIRE_API_KEY=true`, `memory.enabled=true`, `memory.rerankEnabled=true`, a valid `rerankProviderModel`.

```bash
# Without a key — what applyRerank() effectively sends
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
  -X POST http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"<rerank-model>","query":"capital of France",
       "documents":["Paris","Berlin"],"top_n":2}'
# → 401

# Same request with a key
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"<rerank-model>","query":"capital of France",
       "documents":["Paris","Berlin"],"top_n":2}'
# → 200
# {"results":[{"index":0,"relevance_score":0.9917,"document":{"text":"Paris"}},
#             {"index":1,"relevance_score":0.3501,"document":{"text":"Berlin"}}]}
```

Backend health is not the issue — the reranker itself answers correctly. Only the internal hop is rejected.

---

## Why this stays invisible

Two mechanisms compound:

1. **Fail-open by design.** The docstring states *"rerank failure never fails retrieval"*. Retrieval returns unranked results; nothing propagates upward.

2. **The warning is unreachable by level-based log filters.** `memory.rerank.http_fail` is emitted in a bracketed text format with **no `level` field**:

   ```
   [WARN] [MEMORY_RETRIEVAL] memory.rerank.http_fail {"status":401,"model":"..."}
   ```

   Any `grep '"level":50'` or `level>=40` filter misses it entirely. In our 6-hour sample, 73,928 of 291,609 log lines belong to this non-pino family, including 9,655 warnings.

An operator running with API-key enforcement — the recommended production posture — gets degraded memory quality with no signal.

---

## Suggested fixes

In rough order of preference:

1. **Attach an internal credential to the loopback call.** Mint a process-scoped token at startup and send it as `Authorization`. Keeps the auth boundary intact.

2. **Skip the HTTP hop entirely.** The rerank handler lives in the same process; calling it directly avoids both the auth issue and a needless serialize/deserialize round-trip.

3. **Exempt loopback for this route only.** Simplest, but weakens the boundary — worth considering only if the endpoint is bound to `127.0.0.1`.

Independently of the fix chosen:

4. **Make the failure visible.** Either surface it in health output, or emit the warning with a proper `level` field so standard log tooling can see it. A silently degraded retrieval path is worse than a loud one.

5. **`RERANK_LOOPBACK_URL` hardcodes port 20128** while the server reads `PORT` from the environment. An instance on a non-default port would fail with `ECONNREFUSED` for the same silent reason. Deriving the port from the same source would close that case too.

---

## Workaround (for other operators hitting this)

Patching the compiled chunk to add the header restores reranking:

```
headers: { "content-type": "application/json",
           "authorization": "Bearer " + (process.env.OMNIROUTE_INTERNAL_KEY || "") }
```

with a dedicated API key exposed as `OMNIROUTE_INTERNAL_KEY`. Verified: 7 successful reranks, 0 failures across 4 memory-backed requests.

Note this is erased by any container recreation or image pull, so it needs re-application and a monitoring check.

title: fix(models): stop treating provider-supplied free flags as trusted without a documented free tier
body:
⚠️ base-red inherited: #12732

## Summary

Stop honoring upstream-supplied `isFree:true`, `:free`, and `0/0` pricing before consulting the shipped free-tier catalog. Today a disconnected or undisclosed provider with zero pricing or a borrowed `:free` suffix slips through, and the model listing and the `auto/*` router disagree on what's free. title: feat(reasoning): opt-in min output budget floor for thinking models
body:
## Problem
Thinking-capable models burn an entire small `max_tokens` budget on reasoning and return zero-content `finish_reason: "length"` turns, which combo `validateQuality` then rejects as a 502 (`reasoning truncated`). Clients probing with e.g. `max_tokens: 300` get an opaque failure.

## Change
Opt-in floor via `OMNIROUTE_REASONING_MIN_BUDGET` (positive int): a caller budget in `[256, floor)` on a thinking-capable model is raised to the floor, capped by the model's output cap.

- Unset/invalid env → budgets pass through verbatim; **#9507 no-enlargement contract unchanged** (setting the env IS the opt-in)
- Budgets `< 256` stay verbatim (#6274 capability probes)
- Floor never exceeds the model's known output cap
- Logs `Reasoning model <m>: adjusted max_tokens 300 -> 4096` when it fires

## Tests
- `tests/unit/reasoning-min-budget-floor.test.ts` — 7 cases: env-off passthrough, floor application, boundary at 256, cap clamp, probe passthrough, non-thinking skip, invalid env ignored
- Mutation-proofed: floor-branch / cap-clamp / probe-guard removals each turn the suite red (3/3)
- Existing `-6274` / `-9507` suites pass unchanged (2/2, 2/2)

## Ops notes
For self-hosted thinking models hand-registered via provider-models import, the floor requires capability resolution to flag `supportsThinking` — via `model_capability_overrides` `reasoning_efforts` + `max_output_tokens` (documented separately).

Deployed and live-verified on an operator fleet: log-evidenced `max_tokens 300 -> 4096`, `finish_reason: stop` with 508 reasoning tokens + full answer where the same request previously 502'd.

title: fix(streaming): fail fast when an upstream stream produces only lifecycle/heartbeat events, never real content
body:
## Summary

- Live incident (2026-09-04): a free-tier OpenRouter model
  (`minimax/minimax-m3:free`, under load) streamed nothing but OpenAI
  Responses `response.in_progress` heartbeats for ~90 seconds before the
  calling client's own idle timeout (120s for that internal task, 900s for
  the main agent) finally gave up with a generic timeout message. See
  `pipeWithDisconnect`'s own doc comment for the full mechanism.
- `ensureStreamReadiness`'s pre-handoff gate correctly treats a bare
  `response.in_progress` as "ready" (deliberately — `kiro.ts`'s early
  role-only start chunk relies on the exact same behavior) and hands the
  connection to the client. From that point nothing was watching whether
  the model ever actually said anything. The existing byte-level stall
  watchdog (ported from `decolua/9router#1243`) doesn't catch this either —
  it deliberately tracks raw upstream byte activity, not transform output,
  to avoid false-positiving on reasoning models, and the heartbeat bytes
  keep it satisfied indefinitely.
- Adds a second, independent watchdog to `pipeWithDisconnect`: armed once
  at stream start, cleared permanently the first time real model output is
  observed (reusing `createStreamContentWatcher`, the exact classifier
  `createDisconnectAwareStream` already trusts for its own end-of-stream
  #8649 empty-content check), firing only if the deadline elapses with
  lifecycle/ping frames only. Off by default — no arbitrary constant picked
  at this layer; `chatCore` wires it to the same adaptive
  `streamReadinessPolicy.timeoutMs` already computed for the pre-handoff
  readiness gate, so slow-first-content reasoning models keep the same
  generous, request-specific budget in both phases.
- A genuine invisible mid-stream provider swap is architecturally
  impossible over HTTP SSE passthrough once headers have reached the
  client — this cannot make combo silently retry with a different model.
  What it does: turn an indefinite silent hang into a fast, explicit,
  well-formed SSE error the calling agent's own existing retry/fallback
  logic reacts to immediately, instead of waiting out whichever client-side
  timeout happened to apply to that specific call.

## Related Issues

- Closes #
- Related to #

## Validation

- [x] Change type: routing / other (streaming reliability)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint` (targeted: touched files clean; unrelated pre-existing
      `chatCore.ts` unused-import errors verified via stash/pop)
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (`release/v3.8.51`);
      focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in
      this PR

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/stream-handler.test.ts` (+4 tests):
  - `pipeWithDisconnect flags a stream that only ever produces
    lifecycle/heartbeat frames, never real content` — reproduces the
    incident shape (a bare `response.in_progress` frame, nothing else) with
    a tight `contentStallTimeoutMs`. Verified RED on pre-fix code (falls
    back to the byte-stall watchdog's much longer budget, missing the
    incident's actual failure signature) and GREEN after.
  - `... does NOT flag a stream that starts with lifecycle frames but then
    produces real content` — no false positive once real output arrives.
  - `... content stall watchdog is off by default (no
    contentStallTimeoutMs)` — legacy behavior preserved when the option
    isn't threaded.
  - Existing byte-level stall watchdog tests (3) still pass unmodified,
    proving the two watchdogs are independent and don't interfere.

## Coverage Notes

- Touches `open-sse/utils/streamHandler.ts` (the watchdog itself),
  `open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingPipeline.ts` (threading), and
  `open-sse/handlers/chatCore.ts` (one call site, one new field). The new
  tests cover `pipeWithDisconnect` directly at the same level as its
  existing byte-stall coverage; `chatcore-streaming-pipeline.test.ts`'s
  existing type-contract test (loose variadic mock) still passes unchanged
  since the new option is additive/optional.

## Reviewer Notes

- No migration, no protocol change, no new config surface — purely additive
  and default-off unless explicitly wired.
- `git diff --numstat`: production +119/-15 across 3 files (`chatCore.ts`
  +5, `streamingPipeline.ts` +8/-1, `streamHandler.ts` +91/-14), tests
  +130. The production growth is the watchdog itself plus its wiring; it
  reuses `createStreamContentWatcher` and mirrors the existing byte-stall
  watchdog's exact arm/clear/wrappedController pattern rather than
  inventing a new mechanism.
- Full whole-project `tsc --noEmit` run against this branch produces zero
  errors in any touched file (pre-existing project-wide noise elsewhere is
  unaffected, verified via stash/pop).

title: refactor(providers): single source of truth for agy/antigravity public catalogs (#12724)

Fixes #12724.

`agyModels.ts` and `antigravityModelAliases.ts` carried two hand-maintained copies of the same model list — byte-identical since 2026-07-29, so every new Antigravity-backed model meant the same edit twice and the copies could silently drift. Note for later merges: two open PRs (#12608, #12672) touch both catalogs — after this lands, a catalog refresh only needs to edit `antigravityModelAliases.ts`.

title: fix(codex): fail the stream when the websocket closes before a terminal event
body:
## Summary

- When the Codex upstream WebSocket closes after partial output but before any terminal `response.completed` / `response.failed` / `response.incomplete` event, the executor now emits a terminal `response.failed` (code `upstream_websocket_closed`) instead of closing the client stream as if it had completed normally.
- A close that arrives after a legitimate terminal event remains a no-op — exactly one terminal event is ever emitted.
- Registers `upstream_websocket_closed` in the Codex public-error allowlist so the classified code survives the public error projection with the intended `provider_error` / 502 mapping.

Without this, an upstream connection drop mid-response silently truncates the answer: the client sees a normal stream end, retries/fallback never trigger, and the truncation is indistinguishable from a complete response.

## Related Issues

- None

## Validation

Change type and focused loop from the Contribution Golden Path:

- [x] Change type: routing
- [x] Focused regression and adjacent compatibility tests:

## Coverage Notes

- The premature-close test drives the full executor streaming path with a mock WebSocket transport (partial delta, then close) and asserts on the emitted SSE wire body: exactly one `response.failed`, `response.status: "failed"`, `error.code: "upstream_websocket_closed"`.
- The normal-close test sends `response.completed` and then closes, asserting exactly one terminal event and no failure injection.

## Reviewer Notes

- The new allowlist entry follows the existing `upstream_websocket_error` / `upstream_websocket_connect_failed` pattern (`provider_error`, 502 only).

  - `Unit Tests fast-path (1-4/4)`: failing files are all sanitizer/error-boundary family (HuggingChat transport redaction, dashboard request-failed redaction, Kiro stream errors, model-sync invalid JSON, tunnel-error sanitization, stream-handler public error boundaries, zai-web, image-generation-handler, error-sanitizer) — `tests/unit/executor-codex.test.ts` passes in every shard.

  - `Fast Quality Gates`: the file-size violations from the first run are resolved by cc4677917. The remaining gate failures are `open-sse-typecheck` (same inherited `glm.ts TS2554`) and `mutation-test-coverage` — the gate asks for `tests/unit/reset-aware-request-scope-12600.test.ts` to be added to `stryker.conf.json` for `open-sse/services/combo/quotaScoring.ts` (from #12600 on the base); neither file is touched by this PR and the base's own `stryker.conf.json` already lacks that entry.

title: fix(dashboard): expose Modal Base URL field in connection modals (#12704)
body:
Fixes #12704.

Modal is bring-your-own-deploy — every user runs their model on a unique endpoint (`https://<workspace>--<app>.modal.run/v1`), so there's no fixed host to preset. The server-side validator (`src/lib/providers/validation.ts`) already requires `providerSpecificData.baseUrl` for modal, but the add/edit connection modals only rendered Token ID / Token Secret, so there was no way to fill the required field and every Modal connection failed validation.

This adds `modal` to `CONFIGURABLE_BASE_URL_PROVIDERS`, the same mechanism kimi/moonshot use (#7447), so the connection modals now render the Base URL field for Modal — with a placeholder showing the app URL shape the validator expects. The Check button requires the URL before validating, matching the backend contract.

Tests: `tests/unit/modal-base-url-field-12704.test.ts` asserts modal is base-URL configurable, the placeholder shape, and that the server-side validator still rejects a baseUrl-less modal connection (the UI and backend can't drift apart). Two of the three tests fail without the fix. The existing modal + kimi + provider-page-helpers suites (35 tests) stay green; typecheck and lint pass.

base-red inherited: #12732 (pre-existing — blames other PRs, none related to this change).

title: fix(sse): strip _omniroute* handoff flags from upstream request bodies (#12729)
body:
Fixes #12729.

Context-relay and universal-handoff summary calls build their request bodies with internal `_omnirouteSkipContextRelay` / `_omnirouteInternalRequest` flags so the routing layer can recognize them and skip relay injection. Those flags were read before dispatch but never removed from the payload sent upstream, so since 3.8.50 every handoff summary call has been carrying them to the provider. Strict OpenAI-compatible providers (NVIDIA NIM, Groq) reject unknown parameters with a 400 `Unsupported parameter(s)`, which wasted one upstream round-trip per combo step — 504 occurrences in the reporter's call_logs, all starting right after the 3.8.50 upgrade.

The fix strips the internal flags where the body is serialized for upstream:

- `stripInternalBodyFields` (the shared list that already covered `_omnirouteResponsesStore` and the `_native*` passthrough markers) now also drops `_omnirouteSkipContextRelay`, `_omnirouteInternalRequest` and `_omnirouteSkipUniversalHandoff`. The routing-layer reads in chat.ts / combo.ts happen before dispatch, so nothing downstream needs them.
- The executors that serialize their own transformed bodies without going through the base dispatch path (glm, ninerouter, dario, gitlab) apply the same strip, and so does the base `countTokens` path for the same reason.

Tests: `tests/unit/strip-omniroute-internal-params-12729.test.ts` covers the helper directly and a full `DefaultExecutor` round-trip against a local HTTP server, asserting the flags never reach the wire while the rest of the request is untouched. Both tests fail without the fix and pass with it. The existing context-relay/handoff suites (41 tests) and the executor default/base suites (58 tests) stay green; `typecheck:core` and `npm run lint` pass.

title: Semantic cache ignores tool_choice and can replay forbidden tool calls
body:
## Problem
The OpenAI-compatible semantic cache can replay a completion produced with injected memory tools for a later request whose body sets `tool_choice: "none"`.

Observed on OmniRoute 3.8.x:
1. Send a request without `tool_choice`; memory is enabled and OmniRoute injects `memory_*` tools. The model returns `finish_reason=tool_calls` and this is cached.
2. Repeat the same messages/model with `tool_choice: "none"`.
3. OmniRoute returns the cached tool-call response in a few milliseconds, even though the request contract forbids tools.

The stored call artifact confirms the second request body contains `tool_choice: "none"`, while its response contains `tool_calls` and `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`.

## Impact
Structured-output clients receive an empty/non-JSON content body and fail closed. More broadly, the cache changes request semantics.

## Expected
Cache signatures must include behavior-changing request fields, at minimum `tool_choice`, tool definitions, response format, and other generation constraints. A cached result must never violate the current request's tool policy.

## Notes
No private prompts or credentials are included here. The issue was reproduced with synthetic JSON-only requests as well as a structured document-review client.

title: fix(dashboard): moonshot voucher/cash leftover follows bucket balance
body:
## Bug

On Moonshot / Kimi Open Platform keys, the dashboard can show **Available 0%** next to **Voucher 100%** and **Cash 100%**. That combination is not a real wallet state.

Moonshot's balance API returns three absolute numbers (`available_balance`, `voucher_balance`, `cash_balance`). The usage fetcher treated leftover as a boolean for Available (`0` vs `100`) but hardcoded voucher and cash leftover to `100` even when those buckets were `0`. The quota parser then walked the generic path, dropped `currency`, and the card painted a percentage bar instead of ¥0.00.

Measured on X500: node `moonshot-native` (`mnative` → `https://api.moonshot.cn/v1`), 38 connections. `quota_snapshots` for this provider is empty; the numbers come from `GET /v1/users/me/balance` at display time.

## Fix

- Drive leftover from `remaining > 0` for all three buckets.
- Stop marking the rows `unlimited: true` (that path also forces 100% in some widgets).
- Parse `available` / `voucher` / `cash` as credits rows so the card shows the currency amount.

Empty wallet → Available / Voucher / Cash all 0%. A leftover voucher of 5 with available 0 still shows Voucher 100% and Cash 0%.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/moonshot-quota-fetcher.test.ts` — empty buckets are 0%; voucher leftover stays 100% only when that bucket has money.
- `tests/unit/moonshot-quota-dashboard-rendering.test.ts` — producer → `parseQuotaData` → `getQuotaRemainingPercentage` is 0 for an empty wallet, with `isCredits` + `CNY`.
- Bug-injection: hardcode leftover to 100 → the empty-wallet test fails; restore → pass.
- Sibling: agentrouter credits rendering, provider-limits UI, T13 stale reset — 41/41 pass.

## Not in this PR

- HuggingChat / stream public-error unit failures on `release/v3.8.51` (unrelated).
- Filling `quota_snapshots` for Moonshot (display already live-fetches `/v1/users/me/balance`).

title: fix(auto-combo): give every mode pack quality and reliability weights
body:
## Summary

Picking a mode like `reliable` or `quality` used to mute two signals the scorer already knows: how good the output was (quality) and how often the provider failed in the last 24 h (reliability). So `reliability-first` didn't actually weigh reliability at all (`open-sse/services/autoCombo/modePacks.ts:13` replaces the defaults wholesale). Now every pack carries both — `quality 0.02` except `quality-first 0.03` (same as the default, so `quality-first` isn't weaker than `balanced`), `reliability 0.03` except `reliability-first 0.04`. Funding comes from `quota`/`costInv`/`tierPriority`; health (the circuit-breaker — open/half-open/closed) and stability (how steady the latency is) stay untouched, and each pack still sums to `1.0`.

## Related Issues

- Related to #12507 — same `AUTO-COMBO.md` area, no overlap.

## Validation

- [x] Change type: routing
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint` (pre-existing suppressions only; touched files clean when grepped by relative path)
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `open-sse/services/autoCombo/__tests__/autoCombo.test.ts` — gates that each pack has `quality` and `reliability`, a cold pool (no observations) doesn't change ranking, a warm pool does, `NaN` maps to neutral, and a healthy provider still beats a flaky one.
- `tests/unit/auto-combos-suffixes-4235.test.ts` — same per-pack gate.

## Coverage Notes

Touches `open-sse/services/autoCombo/modePacks.ts` and `scoring.ts`; covered by the two files above. No change to the default path (`reliability` stays `0` there).

## Reviewer Notes

Docs (`AUTO-COMBO.md:187/210/218/236/243` and `auto-combo-scoring.mmd` `f16`) updated alongside the code. When a pool has no observations, packs add a flat baseline — ranking only shifts once real failure-rate data fills up, and a closed breaker still outweighs a bad failure rate.

title: fix(providers): discovery ignores per-vendor-route reasoning.effort_values
body:
## Summary

OpenAI-compatible model discovery does not recognize per-vendor-route reasoning vocabularies declared under `vendors.<vendor>.capabilities.reasoning` in `GET /v1/models` (Merge Gateway's catalog shape, [documented here](https://docs.merge.dev/merge-gateway/capabilities/reasoning)). The practical consequence for any connection whose upstream declares this shape:

- Synced models carry no `supportedThinkingEfforts` / `defaultThinkingEffort`, so operator effort data resets on every model sync.
- Models whose upstream accepts a native `max` tier (e.g. `zai/glm-5.3-flash`, accepting `low|high|max`) cannot be used with forced-max reasoning rules — the request fails with `Reasoning effort 'max' is not supported by the configured target`, and manually patched sync data is reverted by the next sync.

This PR parses the shape into the existing `supportedThinkingEfforts` pipeline, **intersected across vendor routes**, and derives `defaultThinkingEffort` from that intersection when no higher-precedence declaration exists.

## Semantics

- **Intersection, not union.** The same canonical model declares different effort vocabularies per vendor route; a request naming an effort level is served by a route that honors it when one exists (unpinned requests self-narrow, per the upstream docs). A synced tier must therefore be honored on every route the model can land on — a union-advertised tier can be silently adjusted (`reasoning_effort_adjusted`) or 400 on a pinned request. Routes without `effort_values` (absent or empty) declare "no effort control" and are excluded.
- **Precedence.** Flat import field > `reasoning.supported_efforts` / `metadata.reasoning.supported_efforts` (#7694) > vendor-route intersection > `capabilities.effort_tiers` (#9160) / `supported_reasoning_levels` / `thinking.levels` (#8347).
- **Authoritative emptiness.** Disjoint vendor vocabularies produce an explicit empty list — no fall-through to a generic tier list that would advertise tiers no route honors.
- **Default derivation is source-gated.** The intersection's highest tier (ranked by canonical order — vendor arrays are not guaranteed sorted) becomes `defaultThinkingEffort` only when the `vendors` shape is the record's winning vocabulary source; a flat or nested declared list is never escaped.
- **Hardening.** Zod-validated (Hard Rule #7); malformed vendor entries and malformed tier entries are dropped individually — discarding a whole route would widen the intersection (fail-open).
- **Shape-gated, not provider-gated.** Any catalog declaring this structure gets the parsing; no provider-specific code path.

## Related Issues

- Related to #7694 (`reasoning.supported_efforts`), #9160 (`capabilities.effort_tiers`), #8347 (`supported_reasoning_levels` / `thinking.levels`), #10563 (model-catalog-driven native reasoning-effort vocabularies). Same parser file, extending the same precedence series with the vendor-route shape.

## Validation

Change type: provider / model discovery (per [Contribution Golden Path](../docs/ops/CONTRIBUTION_GOLDEN_PATH.md)).

- [x] Production-code change includes new/updated automated tests in this PR (12 tests: single-route parsing, cross-route intersection, no-effort-control routes excluded, malformed vendor/tier entries dropped individually, disjoint vocabularies authoritative-empty, synonym normalization, rank-based default, source-gated default, `normalizeDiscoveredModels` threading)
- [x] Focused tests:
  - `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/model-discovery-vendor-effort-values.test.ts tests/unit/model-discovery-reasoning-levels.test.ts tests/unit/sync-reasoning-supported-efforts-7694.test.ts tests/unit/agentrouter-models-discovery-7016.test.ts` (61/61)
  - `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/reasoning-routing.test.ts` (7/7 — composes with #12686: the gate honors the vocabulary this PR syncs)
- [x] `npm run lint` clean on changed files (prettier + eslint)
- [x] Shape verified against the [reasoning capability docs](https://docs.merge.dev/merge-gateway/capabilities/reasoning) and the live `api-gateway.merge.dev/v1/models` payload
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (`release/v3.8.51`)

## Test Coverage

New tests cover: single-route parsing, cross-route intersection, routes without effort control excluded, malformed vendor entries dropped individually, malformed tier entries filtered per entry, no-`vendors` legacy behavior preserved, synonym normalization, rank-based highest-tier default, default skipped when a higher-precedence shape wins, disjoint vocabularies authoritative-empty, and end-to-end `normalizeDiscoveredModels` threading into synced models.

title: 3.8.50 leaks internal `_omniroute*` parameters into upstream request bodies (400 from NVIDIA)
body:
## Summary

Since upgrading to 3.8.50, OmniRoute forwards its own internal fields in the
upstream request body. Providers that validate their input reject the request:

```
[400]: Validation: Unsupported parameter(s): `_omnirouteSkipContextRelay`, `_omnirouteInternalRequest`
[400]: property '_omnirouteInternalRequest' is unsupported
```

## Evidence that it is the upgrade

From OmniRoute's own `call_logs` table on this instance. The 3.8.50 server
started at **2026-09-03 19:27 UTC**; the first such 400 is **19:40:27 UTC**, and
there are **zero** occurrences anywhere before the upgrade.

| Date (UTC) | 400s | First | Last |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-03 (post-upgrade only) | 79 | 19:40:27 | 21:28:01 |
| 2026-09-04 | 425 | 04:11:50 | 12:26:07 |

**504 in total**, still occurring.

## Which providers

| Provider | 400s |
|---|---|
| nvidia | 501 |
| groq | 3 |

Providers that ignore unknown JSON fields (gemini, aion, opencode) are
unaffected, which is why this reads as an NVIDIA problem at first glance. It is
not — it is the request body.

## Impact

Not an outage: a combo simply fails over to the next target. The cost is a
wasted upstream call and its latency on every affected step. On this instance
that is roughly a fifth of one combo's steps.

## Environment

- OmniRoute 3.8.50 (upgraded from 3.8.49, where this does not occur)
- macOS, node v24.18.0, installed via `npm install -g omniroute`
- Requests are `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `stream: true`, routed through a
  `priority` combo
- No proxy, no custom middleware

## Expected

Internal routing fields should be stripped from the payload before it is sent
upstream, or namespaced somewhere that is not the provider request body.

## Note for whoever picks this up

`_omnirouteSkipContextRelay` suggests the context-relay path. This instance has
`OMNIROUTE_EMERGENCY_FALLBACK=false` set as a feature-flag override; every other
flag is at its default. There is no feature flag that turns the leak off — the
flag list has no context-relay toggle.

title: fix(conversations): show a pending spinner for unresolved tool nodes instead of "(empty)"
body:
## Summary

- `/dashboard/conversations` rendered every tool node with no content yet
  as a bare "(empty)" text bubble, whether it was a genuinely-purged node
  or simply a node still waiting on its display content to resolve from
  the owning call-log artifact (`resolveTurnDisplayContent`). Live
  conversations showed a confusing flash of "(empty)" bubbles before the
  real tool call/result content populated a moment later.
- `toTurn()` now maps `role === "tool" && !textPreview` to a distinct
  `pending` `NormalizedBlock` variant, rendered as a spinner + "resolving…"
  instead. Every other mapping (real empty assistant text, resolved
  tool_use/tool_result, resolved plain text) is unchanged.
- `toTurn()`/`ConversationTurn` moved out of the conversations page (a
  `"use client"` component that pulls in `ChatBubble`/`MarkdownMessage`'s
  dependency tree) into a small colocated pure module
  (`toTurn.ts`), so this mapping stays unit-testable without a
  browser/DOM harness. Net production LOC in `page.tsx` goes down.

## Related Issues

- Closes #
- Related to #

- [x] Change type: UI
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path

title: fix(sse): resolve empty conversation bubbles and handle missing call artifacts
body:
## Summary
Resolves an issue where assistant turns carrying `tool_calls` with missing or null `content` generated empty message bubbles in the conversation tree. Also adds fallback text previews for uncaptured call artifacts to ensure valid UI tree rendering.

## Changes
- **`open-sse/services/conversationTracker.ts`**: Extract structured `tool_use` blocks for assistant turns with `tool_calls` when `content` is missing or null. Handled object-shaped arguments correctly.
- **`open-sse/services/conversationTurnContent.ts`**: Pruned secondary `extractChatCompletionsToolUseTurns` pass to enforce single-source canonical turn extraction (`turnsFromBody`) and avoid duplicate role mapping conflicts.
- **`src/app/api/conversations/[id]/tree/route.ts`**: Use nullish coalescing (`??`) for `textPreview` to prevent valid empty strings (`""`) from triggering fallback text.
- **`tests/unit/conversationTracker.test.ts`**: Add unit tests for assistant turn extraction from `tool_calls`.
- **`tests/unit/conversationTurnContent.test.ts`**: Add unit tests for conversation tree rendering fallback content.

## RCA & Verification
- **Root Cause**: `extractCanonicalTurns` skipped `tool_calls` when message `content` was null, leading to missing turn nodes. Logical OR (`||`) in tree route coerced empty string previews to fallback strings.
- **Verification**: Unit test suite passed cleanly (24/24 tests pass):
  `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/conversationTracker.test.ts tests/unit/conversationTurnContent.test.ts`

title: [UPDATE] Cursor reports malformed tool-call args, but OmniRoute artifacts store valid complete arguments (3.8.50)
body:
## Environment

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| OmniRoute version | 3.8.50 (`diegosouzapw/omniroute:latest`) |
| Install method | Docker / Docker Compose |
| OS | Linux (server host), Linux client |
| Client tool | Cursor (OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint, `/v1`) |
| Models | Observed in Cursor on `cc/claude-sonnet-5`, `cc/claude-opus-5`, and `cx/gpt-5.6-sol-high` |
| Transport | Streaming SSE, `tools` + `tool_calls` |

## Update / correction

Further investigation against OmniRoute's own request logs and on-disk
call-log artifacts strongly suggests this is **not** OmniRoute emitting
malformed tool-call arguments. The original claim below is retained for
context, but the evidence now points at Cursor's OpenAI-compatible
tool-call / SSE assembly path.

I am updating this issue so maintainers do not spend time chasing a
gateway-side emit bug that the stored artifacts contradict.

## What Cursor reports

Cursor agent tool calls intermittently fail with:

```
Error: Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position N
Error: Unterminated string in JSON at position N
Error: Command failed to spawn: Invalid arguments: command: Required
```

This spans file write / string replace / shell / AskQuestion / Plan mode.
Plan mode is especially painful because `CreatePlan` always streams a
large Markdown document as tool-call arguments.

## Evidence from OmniRoute logs

For a failing Cursor session, OmniRoute log
`1788453037730-6131b2` contains the later request where Cursor echoes
the failure back as a tool result:

```json
{
  "role": "tool",
  "tool_call_id": "toolu_01AtS61szoRnSY8kCcBBrt9Z",
  "content": [{
    "type": "text",
    "text": "Error: Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position 49 (line 1 column 50)"
  }]
}
```

In that same later request, the corresponding assistant message that
Cursor re-sends has:

```json
{
  "id": "toolu_01AtS61szoRnSY8kCcBBrt9Z",
  "type": "function",
  "function": {
    "name": "AskQuestion",
    "arguments": "{}"
  }
}
```

So Cursor ends up treating the failed call as empty `{}`.

Tracing each failed `tool_call_id` back to the **original** OmniRoute
response artifact shows the opposite: the original emission was complete
valid JSON.

| tool_call_id (suffix) | tool | original args | later history | original JSON |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| `…AtS61s` | AskQuestion | 2248 B | `{}` | VALID |
| `…TzJtr4` | AskQuestion | 3227 B | `{}` | VALID |
| `…KGDdu` | CreatePlan | 13721 B | `{}` | VALID |
| `…AqCTxs` | CreatePlan | 15888 B | `{}` | VALID |
| `…KLXSfJ` | Shell | 343 B | `{}` | VALID |
| `…PKKmSA` | Shell | 223 B | `{}` | VALID |
| `…PUZvUB` | AskQuestion | 3737 B | `{}` | VALID |

Example original payload for `toolu_01AtS61szoRnSY8kCcBBrt9Z` was a full
nested AskQuestion object (~2248 bytes), not `{}`.

Parse-error positions from Cursor (`49`, `298`, `357`, `430`) also do not
match an empty object. They look like Cursor received a truncated or
partially assembled argument string, failed to parse it, then stored
`{}` in history as a fallback.

## Second case: different provider path, clear size threshold

A later failing session gives stronger evidence, because it runs through
a **different** translation path than the case above.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Requested model | `codex/gpt-5.6-sol` (served `gpt-5.6-sol`) |
| Provider | `codex` |
| Translation | `openai` -> `openai-responses` |
| Status | 200, streamed, ~93s |
| History | 59 messages, 18 tools |

In that request, **17 consecutive `Shell` tool calls** all arrive with
`arguments` exactly `{}` and all fail with:

```
Error: Command failed to spawn: Invalid arguments:
command: Required
```

Tracing those `tool_call_id`s back to the original OmniRoute response
artifacts shows every one was large and valid at origin:

| tool_call_id (suffix) | origin args | Cursor result |
|---|---:|---|
| `call_RHorl5G…` | 301 B | executed normally |
| `call_wLM5pqv…` | 9146 B | `{}` + `command: Required` |
| `call_k5mRAhy…` | 9722 B | `{}` + `command: Required` |
| `call_OKxh4nM…` | 11224 B | `{}` + `command: Required` |
| `call_0PhmI7y…` | 25197 B | `{}` + `command: Required` |

Example original payload for `call_OKxh4nM…` (valid JSON, truncated here):

```
{"command":"cat > apps/admin/src/app/admin/parsing/page.tsx <<'EOF'\n'use client';\n\nimport Link from 'next/link';…
```

Small tool calls in the same session all succeeded: `ReadFile`
(94–135 B), `Glob` (145–157 B), `GetDynamicTools` (56 B),
`UpdateCurrentStep` (47 B).

Two points this adds:

- The symptom is **not provider-specific**. It reproduces on
  `openai -> claude` and on `openai -> openai-responses`.
- For large arguments it is **not intermittent**. 17/17 consecutive
  large `Shell` calls failed, while a 301 B call in the same session ran
  fine. The observed threshold sits between ~301 B and ~9 KB.

## Reproduction against OmniRoute outside Cursor

I replayed the actual Cursor request shape outside Cursor against both:

- direct NetBird/internal OmniRoute `/v1`
- public HTTPS OmniRoute `/v1`

Using model `cx/gpt-5.6-sol-medium`, with:

- the real Cursor request body (~265 KB)
- 129 historical messages
- all 20 Cursor tool definitions
- `stream: true`
- forced `CreatePlan`
- Markdown tables + fenced code blocks
- a second variant that also includes the historical `arguments: "{}"`
  + parse-error tool result

Results outside Cursor:

| Route | Duration | Args | Plan body | JSON |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Direct | ~302s | 35494 B | 32511 chars | VALID |
| Public | ~261s | 31222 B | 27879 chars | VALID |
| Direct + failed history | ~335s | 39838 B | 36702 chars | VALID |
| Public + failed history | ~331s | 40016 B | 37128 chars | VALID |

A standards-compliant SSE client reconstructed complete valid tool-call
arguments in every successful replay. I could not reproduce Cursor's
malformed-JSON symptom by consuming OmniRoute SSE directly, even with the
exact large Cursor request shape.

Earlier, smaller synthetic `write_file` tests (16 KB JSX, ~160s streams)
were also byte-exact on both routes.

## Current conclusion

OmniRoute's stored original responses for the failed Cursor tool_call_ids
are valid and complete. Outside Cursor, the same large request shape also
assembles correctly. Cursor then reports malformed/empty tool arguments
and continues the conversation with `arguments: "{}"`.

Across both cases: 12 failed tool calls traced to origin, spanning
223 B to 25197 B, three tools (`Shell`, `AskQuestion`, `CreatePlan`) and
two provider translation paths. All were valid JSON at origin. Every one
became `{}` in Cursor's next request.

That points at Cursor's OpenAI-compatible custom-model tool-call / SSE
argument assembly, not at OmniRoute intentionally emitting empty or
malformed `function.arguments`.

Caveat: OmniRoute logs/artifacts store the reassembled response, not the
raw outbound SSE frames. A pure wire-emission bug would still be
invisible there. But given that an external SSE client cannot reproduce
the malformed JSON, and Cursor can, the weight of evidence is on Cursor.

## Request to OmniRoute maintainers

No OmniRoute code change requested based on current evidence. Leaving this
open mainly so the original report is corrected in public.

If useful, confirmation of one point would still help:
whether `/api/logs/{id}` `responseBody.tool_calls[].function.arguments`
is assembled independently of the bytes actually streamed to the client.
If yes, that closes the remaining "stored != transmitted" caveat.

title: De-duplicate the `agy` and `antigravity` public model catalogs
body:
> Verified against `upstream/main` @ `c0b2253f21` (2026-09-04).

## Problem / Use Case

`AGY_PUBLIC_MODELS` (`open-sse/config/agyModels.ts`) and `ANTIGRAVITY_PUBLIC_MODELS`
(`open-sse/config/antigravityModelAliases.ts`) are two hand-maintained copies of what is
currently the same list. Every time Google ships a new Antigravity-backed model, the same
edit has to be made twice, and the two files can silently drift.

The comment at the top of `agyModels.ts` states the rationale:

> The `agy` provider reuses the `antigravity` executor/translator (identical backend), but
> keeps its own catalog so the CLI and IDE model surfaces can evolve independently. Both
> currently expose the same callable Claude/Gemini/GPT set.

That rationale was real when the file was introduced, but it has not held since 2026-07-29.

### Evidence 1 — the two catalogs are currently identical

On `upstream/main` @ `c0b2253f21`, both lists contain the same 10 ids:

```
claude-opus-4-6-thinking   gemini-3.1-flash-lite   gemini-3.7-flash-low
claude-sonnet-4-6          gemini-3.1-pro-low      gemini-3.7-flash-medium
gemini-pro-agent           gemini-3.7-flash-high   gemini-3.7-flash-tiered
gpt-oss-120b-medium
```

`diff` of the sorted id sets is empty. The per-model spec fields match too — identical
distributions of `contextLength`, `maxOutputTokens`, `supportsReasoning`, `supportsVision`
and `toolCalling`.

### Evidence 2 — they have been identical for over a month

Every revision that has ever touched `agyModels.ts`, compared against
`ANTIGRAVITY_PUBLIC_MODELS` at the same commit:

| Date | Commit | agy ids | antigravity ids | Divergent ids |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-26 | `b4ec7807ab` (Release v3.8.50) | 10 | 10 | **0** |
| 2026-08-23 | `65e81158ab` (fix(ollama) …) | 10 | 10 | **0** |
| 2026-07-29 | `c9d4a45f18` (Release v3.8.49) | 15 | 15 | **0** |
| 2026-07-07 | `92715c8f2c` (Release v3.8.46, file added) | 15 | 19 | 4 |

The separation carried real content only at the moment it was introduced. The four ids that
IDE had and CLI did not, on 2026-07-07:

```
claude-sonnet-5
gemini-3-pro-preview
gemini-3-pro-image-preview
gemini-2.5-computer-use-preview-10-2025
```

All four are gone from both lists today. Since 2026-07-29 the catalogs have been byte-equal
in content across three separate revisions.

### Reproduce

```sh
git fetch upstream
cd <repo>

# current id sets
git show upstream/main:open-sse/config/agyModels.ts \
  | grep -oE 'id: "[^"]+"' | tr -d '"' | sed 's/id: //' | sort > /tmp/agy.ids
git show upstream/main:open-sse/config/antigravityModelAliases.ts \
  | awk '/ANTIGRAVITY_PUBLIC_MODELS/,/^\]\)/' \
  | grep -oE 'id: "[^"]+"' | tr -d '"' | sed 's/id: //' | sort > /tmp/anti.ids
diff /tmp/anti.ids /tmp/agy.ids   # empty

# divergence across history
for c in $(git log --format=%H upstream/main -- open-sse/config/agyModels.ts); do
  git show $c:open-sse/config/agyModels.ts \
    | grep -oE 'id: "[^"]+"' | tr -d '"' | sed 's/id: //' | sort > /tmp/g.ids
  git show $c:open-sse/config/antigravityModelAliases.ts \
    | awk '/ANTIGRAVITY_PUBLIC_MODELS/,/^\]\)/' \
    | grep -oE 'id: "[^"]+"' | tr -d '"' | sed 's/id: //' | sort > /tmp/a.ids
  echo "$(git log -1 --format=%ad --date=short $c) ${c:0:9} diff=$(diff /tmp/a.ids /tmp/g.ids | grep -c '^[<>]')"
done
```

## Proposed Solution

Keep the ability to diverge, remove the duplication: derive both catalogs from one shared
base plus an explicit per-surface delta.

```ts
// open-sse/config/antigravitySharedModels.ts
export const ANTIGRAVITY_SHARED_MODELS = Object.freeze([ /* the 10 current entries */ ]);

// agyModels.ts
export const AGY_PUBLIC_MODELS = buildSurfaceCatalog(ANTIGRAVITY_SHARED_MODELS, {
  add: [],      // CLI-only models
  remove: [],   // ids the CLI surface does not expose
});

// antigravityModelAliases.ts
export const ANTIGRAVITY_PUBLIC_MODELS = buildSurfaceCatalog(ANTIGRAVITY_SHARED_MODELS, {
  add: [],      // IDE-only models (e.g. the four from 2026-07-07)
  remove: [],
});
```

With both deltas empty today, the intent of the original comment is preserved — a future
IDE-only preview model is a one-line `add:` entry — while a new Gemini release becomes a
single edit instead of two.

`open-sse/config/providers/registry/agy/index.ts` keeps using `models: [...AGY_PUBLIC_MODELS]`
unchanged, so no consumer has to move.

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Leave as is.** Works, but every model release is a double edit with no compile-time
   guard against drift. The current lag illustrates the cost: Gemini 3.8 Flash shipped
   2026-09-02 and neither catalog has it yet, and each future catch-up is two edits.
2. **Delete `agyModels.ts` and point `agy` at `ANTIGRAVITY_PUBLIC_MODELS`.** Simplest, but
   discards the stated design intent and makes a future CLI/IDE split a revert rather than a
   one-line delta. Not proposed for that reason.
3. **Make the catalog dynamic** from `:fetchAvailableModels`. A discovery path already
   exists (`src/app/api/providers/[id]/models/discovery/`), but its results do not feed the
   registry. That is a larger change and orthogonal to this one — the pinned catalog is
   deliberate, and this request does not challenge that.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single shared source defines the entries common to both surfaces.
- [ ] `AGY_PUBLIC_MODELS` and `ANTIGRAVITY_PUBLIC_MODELS` are derived from it, each with an
      explicit (currently empty) add/remove delta.
- [ ] The public id set and every spec field of both catalogs are unchanged by the refactor.
- [ ] Adding a model to both surfaces requires editing exactly one file.
- [ ] A per-surface delta still works: adding an id to one `add:` list exposes it on that
      surface only.
- [ ] The stale "can evolve independently … both currently expose the same set" comment is
      replaced by one describing the shared-base mechanism.

## Area

Provider registry / model catalogs

## Related Provider(s)

`agy` (Antigravity CLI), `antigravity` (Antigravity IDE)

## Additional Context

The two providers already share the executor and translator — `agyModels.ts` describes the
backend as `identical`. This request only aligns catalog maintenance with that existing
reality; it does not propose merging the provider entries themselves.

## Expected Test Plan

- Extend `tests/unit/agy-provider.test.ts` and `tests/unit/antigravity-retired-public-models.test.ts`
  to assert each surface's resolved catalog equals `shared + add − remove`.
- Add a regression test asserting the exported id sets and spec fields are unchanged by the
  refactor (snapshot of the current 10 entries).
- Add a test that a non-empty `add:` on one surface does not leak into the other.
- `tests/unit/antigravity-image-catalog-separation.test.ts` should keep passing unmodified.

title: fix(cursor): recover Kimi tool calls emitted as history narration
body:
## Problem

Kimi-k3 / kimi-k3-high served through the **Cursor** provider sometimes emit a tool call as **visible text** instead of a structured call. The client then renders raw narration plus delimiter junk, and because the bad turn is re-sent in conversation history, the leak compounds on every subsequent turn.

Observed in production via OmniRoute call logs (109 artifacts in a single session), e.g.:

```
…Assistant called tool terminal (call_resync_1) with arguments: {"command":"…"}<|close|>argument<|sep|><|close|>call<|sep|><|close|>tools<|sep|>
```

with `finish_reason: "stop"` and **no `tool_calls` field** on the message.

## Root cause

Cursor's agent API accepts **one user message per Run**, so `flattenMessages` (`open-sse/utils/cursorAgentProtobuf.ts`) serializes prior `assistant.tool_calls` into plain text for the model to read as context:

```
Assistant called tool <name> (<id>) with arguments: <json>
```

Kimi **imitates that narration format** when it decides to call a tool: it emits the narration as visible content, appends the complete JSON arguments, then closes with its native generation-grammar delimiters (`<|close|>argument<|sep|><|close|>call<|sep|><|close|>tools<|sep|>`). Cursor's protobuf backend passes the whole thing through verbatim. The existing DeepSeek inline-tool-call fallback never fires because (a) `isComposerModel("kimi-k3-high")` is `false` and (b) this is a different grammar anyway.

## Fix

New `open-sse/utils/kimiToolCallNarration.ts`:

- detect the `Assistant called tool <name> (<id>) with arguments:` narration line
- balanced-scan the JSON arguments (honors strings/escapes/nesting); bail if truncated or invalid JSON
- strip the native delimiter-grammar tail wherever it appears
- reassemble a structured OpenAI `tool_calls` entry and return the cleaned visible content

Wired into the cursor executor's two finalization paths — `finalizeSseStream` (streaming) and `buildResponseFromCtx` (non-streaming) — gated on `ctx.toolCalls.length === 0` so it **never fires on a healthy turn**.

## Validation

- 9 new unit tests in `tests/unit/kimi-tool-call-narration.test.ts` — all pass.
- Ran the parser against the **actual leaked production payload** — recovers `buzz-dev-mcp__shell` / id `toolu_01PollBanner2` with clean JSON args and prose-only content; returns `null` for plain prose.
- Existing cursor / composer / translator suites still green.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` introduces no new errors in the touched files.

---

Rebased onto `release/v3.8.51` (this PR supersedes a mis-based earlier attempt).
