title: GET /v1/models returns each model duplicated under two provider prefixes (short alias + full name)
body:
## Environment
- OmniRoute 3.8.50 (npm install, Windows 11), running locally on http://localhost:20128/v1
- Consumer: Hermes Agent (OpenAI-compatible client), plus other OpenAI-compatible clients

## Problem
Every upstream model that a connection exposes comes back from GET /v1/models under **two different prefixed ids** — a short alias and the full provider name — so downstream clients show each physical model twice.

Examples (confirmed from the live /v1/models response and the dashboard UI, screenshots available):

- kc/stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free **and** kilocode/stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free
- kc/poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free **and** kilocode/poolside/laguna-s-2.1:free
- nous/inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash-fin:free **and** nous-research/inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash-fin:free
- trk/z-ai/glm-5.3-free **and** tokenrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-free
- oc/big-pickle **and** opencode/big-pickle

In my instance: kilocode = 324 models, and kc = 324 models (every one duplicated); nous / nous-research = 44 each; no-think/* aliases are likewise emitted as a second prefix (13).

So roughly half of the 800+ ids returned by /v1/models are alias-duplicates of the other half.

## Expected behavior
A model exposed by a connection should appear once — either under the short alias or the full provider prefix, not both. Or at minimum the duplicate emission should be configurable (e.g. a flag to disable alias ids in /v1/models).

## Impact
- Any downstream client that fetches /v1/models (Hermes, LibreChat, Open WebUI, editors' model pickers) shows every model twice, and the picker becomes unusably noisy (800+ entries).
- Even when the user limits models for a downstream API key, the duplicated ids still appear because both prefixed ids resolve to the same connection/model.

## Workaround tried
Restricting allowed models on the downstream key — the duplicates remain because the duplication is in OmniRoute's own /v1/models emission.

## Request
1. Deduplicate /v1/models so each physical model appears once (prefer the canonical provider prefix).
2. Or expose a config flag to disable short-alias ids entirely.

title: [BUG] OpenRouter reasoning traces lost: reasoning_details text not promoted to reasoning_content when reasoning also present
body:
### OmniRoute Version
3.8.49 (also reproducible on head of `release/v3.8.51`)

### Installation Method
npm (global)

### Operating System
macOS

### OS Version
macOS (Client) - OmniRoute proxied via SSH

### Node.js Version
24.x

### Provider(s) Involved
OpenRouter (as meta/aggregator) — upstream models: DeepSeek V4 Flash, GLM 5.3 Flash, Kimi K3

### Client Tool
opencode (via the @omniroute/opencode plugin)

### Description
When routing DeepSeek V4 Flash, GLM 5.3 Flash, or Kimi K3 through OpenRouter, no thinking/reasoning traces are surfaced to the client. The final summary and tool calls appear, but there is no thinking/reasoning indicator or reasoning content during generation — reasoning is lost for observability.

Root cause traced to `copyOpenAICompatibleReasoningFields()` in `open-sse/utils/reasoningFields.ts`:

```ts
export function copyOpenAICompatibleReasoningFields(source: JsonRecord, target: JsonRecord) {
  if (source.reasoning_content !== undefined) target.reasoning_content = source.reasoning_content;
  if (source.reasoning !== undefined) target.reasoning = source.reasoning;
  if (source.reasoning_text !== undefined) target.reasoning_text = source.reasoning_text;
  if (source.thinking !== undefined) target.thinking = source.thinking;
  if (source.thought !== undefined) target.thought = source.thought;
  if (Array.isArray(source.reasoning_details)) target.reasoning_details = source.reasoning_details;
  if (!getReadableReasoningValue(target)) {                      // <-- getReadableReasoningValue = reasoning_content || reasoning
    const mirrored = getUnsupportedReasoningValue(source);        //    reasoning_text || thinking || thought || reasoning_details[].text
    if (mirrored) target.reasoning_content = mirrored;            // <-- NEVER reached when `reasoning` is present
  }
  ...
}
```

OpenRouter returns BOTH `reasoning` (string) AND `reasoning_details[]` (array with `{type:"reasoning.text", text}` entries) for these thinking models. Because `getReadableReasoningValue(target)` returns a truthy value as soon as the `reasoning` string is copied to the target, the promotion block is skipped — the `reasoning_details` text is never mirrored into `reasoning_content`.

Clients (opencode / OpenAI-compatible SDK) read `delta.message.reasoning_content` to render thinking traces. The `reasoning` field is not read by opencode for streaming reasoning display (its `OpenAIChatDelta` schema only declares `reasoning_content` and strips unknown keys). Net result: thinking content generated by the model is sanitized but never delivered in the client-readable field.

Other chain components verified NOT implicated:
- `@omniroute/opencode` plugin: auth + model discovery only; no transformation of streamed reasoning fields.
- Requests carry `reasoning: {type:"enabled"}` / effort correctly (cmd-t / model-variant toggle works and models do produce reasoning).

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Route DeepSeek V4 Flash (or GLM 5.3 Flash / Kimi K3) via OmniRoute → OpenRouter.
2. Ask a question that requires reasoning while streaming.
3. Observed: tool call + final summary appear, but no thinking/reasoning content or indicator streams to the client.

### Expected Behavior
The model's reasoning should be mirrored into `reasoning_content` so clients display thinking traces. `reasoning_details[].text` text should be promoted to `reasoning_content` whenever `reasoning_content` is empty, even when the `reasoning` string is also present.

### Additional Context
- Same failure mode family as #6623 / #7856 (unsupported reasoning aliases not promoted into the client-readable field), but this specific gap — `reasoning` present + `reasoning_details[].text` present → `reasoning_content` never set — is not covered by those fixes.
- Edge case to preserve: when `reasoning_details` contains ONLY non-text entries (e.g. `{type:"reasoning.encrypted", data:"sig"}`), `reasoning_content` must remain unset (encrypted/signature payloads must not be flattened into text).

title: fix(ops): clamp embedding inputs to model context; egress-IP lockout provider override for paid plans; glm-5.3 vision fragment
body:
Closes #12658

## 1. Embeddings input clamp
`/v1/embeddings` proxied oversized documents verbatim → upstream 400 "Invalid 'input': maximum context length is 8192 tokens" (121× in one day on `openrouter/openai/text-embedding-3-small`). String inputs are now clamped per-item to 20k chars before dispatch — same constant and rationale as the memory-retrieval clamp in `src/lib/memory/embedding/remote.ts`. A truncated input keeps embeddings working; an unclipped one guarantees a 400.

## 2. Egress-IP lockout override
`applyEgressIpLockout()` assumes opencode's free tier is IP-bucketed (#9611). PAID plans are account/workspace-bucketed, so one account's plan-level 429 cascaded "Shared egress IP quota exhausted" across ALL sibling connections for days → 1419× 503 `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` in one hour.

New `OMNIROUTE_EGRESS_IP_LOCK_PROVIDERS`:
- unset → current default family (free-tier behavior unchanged);
- `none|off|false|0` → egress-IP lockout disabled;
- `a,b,c` → exact replacement set.

## 3. visionModels: `glm-5.3` family fragment
Supersedes the narrow `glm-5.3-flash` entry so `/v1/models` marks every `glm-5.3*` variant vision-capable for agent model pickers.

## Testing
`tests/unit/embeddings-input-clamp.test.ts` (4) + `tests/unit/egress-ip-lock-env-override.test.ts` (4) — all green.

title: fix(combo): per-target skip diagnostics for ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED + tiny-budget reasoning probe returns truncated 200
body:
Closes #12659. Implements the diagnostics ask in #12294; #10281 combo-path parity.

## Production trigger
2026-09-03: 1419× 503 `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` in one hour (`diagnostics.attempted=0, excluded=[]`) — after the storm was over, the only actionable causes (an API-key allowlist mismatch silently skipping the one healthy target; multi-day persisted cooldowns) were invisible at the API surface and lived in debug-only logs.

## Change
- `decisionTrace.ts`: `persisted_cooldown` skip reason + optional `detail` + pure `summarizeSkippedTargets()`.
- Both combo dispatchers: persisted-cooldown skips record a trace decision; `buildComboDiag()` emits `skippedTargets[]` (target, reason, detail) + `nextRetryAt` (earliest future cooldown reset parsed from the detail) so clients can back off instead of hammering.
- `chat.ts`: allowlist rejections during target screening log at info with the key name (the mismatch class behind this incident: alias wildcard `bailian/*` vs dynamic `openai-compatible-chat-<uuid>` provider id).
- Tiny-budget reasoning probes (max_tokens < 256 targeting a thinking model) whose 200 burned the whole budget on thinking return a truncated 200 (`finish_reason: "length"`) via `buildReasoningProbeTruncatedResponse` — #10281 direct-path parity; stops fallback burn + model-lockout poisoning (68× 502 in one day).

## Testing
`tests/unit/12294-skipped-target-diagnostics.test.ts` (5) + `tests/unit/10281-combo-reasoning-probe.test.ts` (3) + full `tests/unit/combo/*` and reasoning suites green.

title: fix(opencode): CLI identity + x-opencode-session on background calls; glm [1214] and reasoning-presence fixes for zen/go gateways
body:
Closes #12657

## Summary
OpenCode announced that background requests missing `x-opencode-session` (User-Agent "Bun fetch") **may error starting 09/06**. Three fixes for the opencode-family surface, all driven by 2026-09-03 production evidence on a busy instance:

1. **Background identity**: model-catalog discovery entries (`opencode` / `opencode-zen` / `opencode-go`) and the quota fetcher now send the OpenCode CLI identity (User-Agent, `x-opencode-client/project/request/session`) with a STABLE per-workspace session fingerprint — seeded by `opencodeGoWorkspaceId`, same hash family the chat path derives via `generateSessionId()` (#10571). Background traffic groups under one identity across restarts instead of a fresh anonymous client per call.
2. **glm [1214]**: GLM-family upstreams get a synthetic `(continue)` user turn on the SAME-FORMAT (openai→openai) lane when history has no `role:"user"` turn — agent tool-loop continuations hit exactly that shape (37× 400 in one day on opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash). Mirrors the Claude-lane `_ensureUserTurn` behavior.
3. **Responses-transport reasoning presence**: on a replay-cache miss, presence-enforcing gateways (opencode console gateways — same contract as xiaomi-mimo #9573/#9610) now get the internal sentinel, and `toResponses` encodes it as a `reasoning_text` item — fixing 400 "The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API" (54× in one day). DeepSeek-direct absent-OK behavior unchanged; sentinel echoes are stripped by the response translators.

No classification/routing changes; chat-path fingerprints untouched.

## Testing
- `tests/unit/opencode-background-identity-headers.test.ts` (6): identity set, per-seed stability, cross-seed difference, discovery wiring for all three providers.
- `tests/unit/glm-1214-same-format-user-turn.test.ts` (3): same-format user-turn injection, non-GLM no-op, existing-user-turn no-op.
- `tests/unit/opencode-reasoning-presence-responses.test.ts` (2): sentinel → reasoning_text item; real reasoning passes through verbatim.
- Full opencode family re-run: 100/100 green (`refactor-opencodeHeaders`, `opencode-executor`, `opencode-session-fingerprint-headers-10571`, `opencode-cli-headers-synthesis-5997`).

title: fix(combo): ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED must carry per-target skip reasons; tiny-budget reasoning probes should return truncated 200s
fix(ops): embeddings 8192-token clamp + egress-IP lockout provider override for paid plans
body:
Two small production-hardening fixes (branch `ops-robustness`):

## 1. Embeddings: clamp string inputs to the model context
`/v1/embeddings` proxies oversized documents verbatim → upstream 400 "Invalid 'input': maximum context length is 8192 tokens" fails the whole call (121× in one day on openrouter/openai/text-embedding-3-small). Clamp each string item to 20k chars (same constant/rationale as the memory-retrieval clamp in `src/lib/memory/embedding/remote.ts`) — a truncated input keeps embeddings working; an unclipped one guarantees a 400.

## 2. Egress-IP lockout: provider-family override
`applyEgressIpLockout()` assumes opencode's free tier is IP-bucketed (#9611). PAID plans are account/workspace-bucketed, so one account's plan-level 429 cascades "Shared egress IP quota exhausted" across ALL sibling connections for days — production showed 1419× 503 `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` in one hour from exactly this.

Add `OMNIROUTE_EGRESS_IP_LOCK_PROVIDERS`:
- unset → current default family (free-tier behavior preserved);
- `none|off|false|0` → lockout fully disabled;
- `a,b,c` → exact replacement set.

title: fix(opencode): background calls (model discovery, quota) send UA "Bun fetch" without x-opencode-session — hard errors announced from 09/06
body:
## Summary
OpenCode notified operators (email 2026-09-03):

> Some of your requests to OpenCode Go are missing an `x-opencode-session` header. … Starting 09/06 requests missing this header may error.
> Useragents missing the header: **Bun fetch**

The offending calls are OmniRoute's BACKGROUND fetches to opencode.ai — model-catalog discovery (`autoFetchModels`/autoSync → `PROVIDER_MODELS_CONFIG["opencode-go"]`, plain fetch, no UA/session) and the quota fetcher (`opencodeQuotaFetcher.ts`, plain fetch). Chat dispatches are fine: `OpencodeExecutor.buildHeaders` synthesizes the CLI identity and derives a stable session fingerprint (#10571).

## Fix (branch `opencode-identity-headers`)
- `buildOpencodeBackgroundHeaders()` in `open-sse/utils/opencodeHeaders.ts`: CLI UA + `x-opencode-client/project/request/session` with a STABLE per-workspace session fingerprint (seeded by `opencodeGoWorkspaceId`, same hash family as the chat path) so background traffic groups under one identity across restarts.
- Discovery entries for `opencode` / `opencode-zen` / `opencode-go` route through it.
- Quota fetcher sends it too.

Also included on the same branch (same upstream, same week):
- **GLM same-format 400 [1214]**: synthetic user turn when openai→openai history has no `role:"user"` turn (agent tool-loop continuations; 37× in one day on opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash). Mirrors the Claude-lane `_ensureUserTurn` behavior.
- **Responses-transport reasoning presence**: opencode console gateways 400 with "The `reasoning_text` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API" when a thinking-mode history lacks the item (54× in one day). On replay-cache misses the internal sentinel is emitted and toResponses encodes it as a `reasoning_text` item; DeepSeek-direct absent-OK behavior unchanged (#9573/#9610 contract preserved).

title: fix(tls): wreq-js transport stalls streaming inference (zero bytes for minutes) — make the fingerprint transport adaptive with a first-byte watchdog
body:
## Summary
With `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true`, every direct-route inference dispatch rides the wreq-js (browser-JA3) transport. Empirically (2026-09-03/04, opencode-go + command-code + a bailian-compatible gateway):

- the wreq `Response` object resolves, then its body produces **zero bytes for 90–600s** — only OmniRoute's synthetic SSE keepalives reach the client;
- the identical model/prompt through plain node fetch: **TTFB 3.1s, full stream 3.5s**;
- control-plane calls (`/models`, tls.peet.ws) are fast either way — the stall is transport+streaming-specific, not DNS/network, and Cloudflare answers 401s on the same endpoints in 0.6s.

Downstream effect: agents abort (499 storms — 616 in one afternoon), and combined with the 110s headers-wait cap (#12655) every long buffered generation dies as a 504. Perceived TPS on all affected providers collapsed.

## Proposed design (implemented on branch `release-integ`)
Adaptive ladder instead of blanket-on:

1. Plain direct fetch is the fast path.
2. When a response is a Cloudflare fingerprint rejection (403 + `error_code 1010` / `browser_signature_banned`), arm a 1h per-provider cache and retry once through wreq-js (replay-safe requests only).
3. Every wreq response carries a **first-byte watchdog** (`TLS_FINGERPRINT_FIRST_BYTE_WATCHDOG_MS`, default 10s): no first byte → cancel and fall back to the direct dispatcher.
4. `TLS_FINGERPRINT_PROVIDERS` keeps legacy eager semantics for explicit opt-in, now watchdog-guarded.

After enabling this on the affected instance: opencode-go TTFB 3–6s (was 90–600s of zero bytes), zero 1010 recurrence with the transport idle.

## Notes
- wreq-js README documents response-body streaming, so the library supports it — the stall may be fingerprint-behavioral (gateway treats browser-JA3 non-CLI traffic differently) or a wreq-js session/SSE interaction. The watchdog makes OmniRoute resilient either way.
- Related: #12529 (remediation hint), #12531.

title: fix(sse): buffered-gateway 504 storm — per-provider fetch-start cap override lost between #11526 and the executor config
body:
## Summary
With #11526 (#11668) live, every STREAMING request's headers-wait phase is capped to 110s. Console Go / Command Code gateways buffer entire generations — no bytes flow until the model finishes thinking — so any generation with TTFB > 110s is killed with:

```
[504]: Fetch timeout after 110000ms on https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses
```

Production (one instance, one day): **149× 504** on opencode-go, all exactly ~110s, while successful requests on the same models ran **75s–493s** — proving the ceiling, not the upstream, is the fault. `errorClassifier.ts` even documented the buffered-gateway behavior, but the cap override never reaches the executor:

- registry entries declare `fetchStartTimeoutCapMs` (600s) for opencode-go / command-code;
- `generateLegacyProviders()` (providerRegistry.ts) projects registry entries into the executor's `LegacyProvider` config with a fixed field allowlist that **omits the cap**;
- so `resolveFetchStartTimeout({ baseTimeoutMs, stream, capMs: this.config?.fetchStartTimeoutCapMs })` sees `undefined` and falls back to the 110s default.

## Fix (branch `release-integ`, will open PR)
- declare `fetchStartTimeoutCapMs` on `RegistryEntry` + `LegacyProvider`;
- copy it in `generateLegacyProviders()`;
- raise opencode-go / command-code to 600s (measured TTFB up to 493s);
- regression test `tests/unit/fetch-start-cap-legacy-projection.test.ts`.

Side note: the two TS2353 errors in the open-sse typecheck baseline are exactly this undeclared field.

## Evidence
- call_logs 2026-09-03: 87 opencode deepseek rows at 110139–137993ms all 504; 125 ok rows at 75192–492768ms.

title: fix(images): fall through combo edit targets on /v1/images/edits
body:
## Summary

- A combo used on `/v1/images/edits` only tried its **first** target with a `modelStr` (`resolveSingleImageComboTarget`) — no fallback — so a combo whose first target isn't edit-capable, or lacks credentials, was flattened to a hard error, while the same combo works on `/v1/images/generations` (which iterates every image-capable target via `executeImageCombo`, skipping missing-creds/rate-limited ones and only stopping on a terminal 400/401/403).
- Fix (your two-step plan): extracted `executeImageCombo`'s per-target iteration/skip/terminal-classification into a generic `runImageComboTargets(...)`; `/generations` calls it with the generation dispatch, **behaviour byte-identical**. Wired it into `/v1/images/edits` with an edit-capable filter and an edit dispatch, so it falls through to a later target; missing credentials now **skip** (not a hard 401), matching generations.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12547

## Validation

- [x] Change type: routing (images)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/image-combo-edits-fallback-12547.test.ts` — 5 tests: a non-edit-capable first target and a missing-credentials first target both fall through to a later edit-capable target on `/edits` (RED on base: hard 400/401; GREEN with the fix: 200), and `/generations` behaviour is asserted unchanged.

## Coverage Notes

- `open-sse/services/imageCombo.ts` (extracted `runImageComboTargets`; the `/generations` dispatch and response tail are unchanged) and `src/app/api/v1/images/edits/route.ts` (edit-capable filter + per-provider edit dispatch + a bare-combo diversion inserted before `resolveImageRouteModel`, mirroring generations). 28 neighbouring image/combo tests stay green; `typecheck:core` clean; complexity ratchets under baseline. Deliberate low-risk choice: the edit-combo path has its own `dispatchImageEditTarget` reusing the same provider handlers rather than refactoring the single-model `postHandler` branches, to avoid changing single-model `/edits` error bodies; a combo target returning a terminal 400 stops iteration, matching the existing generation terminal-400 semantics.

title: fix(ci): openapi-security-tiers must read ALWAYS_PROTECTED_API_PATTERNS (base-red #12581)
body:
⚠️ base-red inherited: #12581

## The failure

`release/v3.8.51` is red on `check:openapi-security-tiers` with four routes reported as unprotected:

```
POST /api/providers/{id}/claude-auth/apply-local: has x-always-protected but is NOT in ALWAYS_PROTECTED_API_PATHS [...]
POST /api/providers/{id}/claude-auth/export:      ...
POST /api/providers/{id}/codex-auth/apply-local:  ...
POST /api/providers/{id}/codex-auth/export:       ...
```

## They are not unprotected

`isAlwaysProtectedPath()` ORs **two** arrays:

```ts
// src/server/authz/routeGuard.ts
ALWAYS_PROTECTED_API_PATHS.some((p) => path === p || path.startsWith(p)) ||
ALWAYS_PROTECTED_API_PATTERNS.some((re) => re.test(path))
```

All four routes are covered by the pattern that shipped with the credential-export hard-gate:

```ts
/^\/api\/providers\/[^/]+\/(claude|codex)-auth\/(export|apply-local)\/?$/
```

A runtime probe over the real `isAlwaysProtectedPath()` returns **true** for all four. The gate parsed only `ALWAYS_PROTECTED_API_PATHS` and never `ALWAYS_PROTECTED_API_PATTERNS`, so it was blind to half of its own input — **a false positive, not a security hole.**

This is the residual half of the defect #12350 fixed for the LOCAL_ONLY tier this cycle; that arm already reads both `LOCAL_ONLY_API_PREFIXES` and `LOCAL_ONLY_API_PATTERNS`.

## Change

- Parse `ALWAYS_PROTECTED_API_PATTERNS`, and include it in the fatal parse guard so a future formatting change in `routeGuard.ts` fails loudly instead of silently degrading back into false positives.
- Add `coveredByAlwaysProtected()` mirroring `coveredByLocalOnly()` — both concretize `{param}` before matching.
- Name both arrays in the error text.

## Validation

Gate on a clean tree: `FAIL — 4 annotation mismatches` before, `PASS — all security tier annotations match routeGuard.ts` (exit 0) after.

New `tests/unit/openapi-security-tiers-gate.test.ts` runs the gate as a subprocess — deliberately **not** importing `routeGuard.ts`, so the unit suite gains no DB handle (that suite is already hanging on one). Mutation-checked: reverting the gate to its previous version makes the test fail and print all four routes; restoring the fix makes it pass.

title: fix(gamification): durable action-count badges that survive xp_audit_log pruning

## Summary

- The `action_count` badge milestones (token-consumer 1k, token-machine 10k, token-whale 100k) were counted directly over `xp_audit_log`, which `cleanupXpAuditLog()` prunes at 30 days by default — so on a default install the "lifetime" thresholds silently became "requests in the last 30 days" and were effectively unreachable (a key doing 900 req/month never reaches Token Consumer).

- The cleanup/prune behaviour and the public API are unchanged.
- **Scope:** `action_count`. `unique_count` and the `first` (`MIN(created_at)`) criteria read the same table and have the same retention exposure — noted as follow-up, not fixed here.

title: feat(providers): add xKiro
body:
## Summary

> **Stacked on #12649 (re-audit) — merge #12649 first.** This branch now contains #12649's head (`113b608`) as an ancestor; its base is `fix/free-tier-quota-reaudit`, so the diff shown here is xKiro only.

Adds **xKiro** (`xkiro`, https://xkiro.com) as an OpenAI-compatible API-key gateway with a documented free plan: **5M tokens/day per account**, no card, across the 40 upstream models tagged `access_tier: "free"` on the public `GET https://api.xkiro.com/v1/models`. 39 of them are pinned here (Qwen, MiniMax, DeepSeek, Mistral, SenseNova — 24 with vision, all with tool calling, context 128K–1M); `openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark` is deliberately left out (see below). The free-tier catalog gains one new recurring pool, `xkiro-free` = 5M × 30 = **150M tokens/month**, counted once for the whole account, and every visible number that depends on it (headline, entries, pools, hard-stop rows, provider count) is re-synced through the docs gates.

Third PR of the "free-tier honest growth" series (PR1 re-audit of the existing quotas, PR2 gated bucket, PR3 this provider, PR4 radar-server feed). It is now **stacked on PR1**: merged with `origin/fix/free-tier-quota-reaudit` @ `113b608`, so the numbers below are measured against PR1's head as the baseline and every delta is xKiro's own contribution.

## What changed

**Provider (routable + canonical)**

- `open-sse/config/providers/registry/xkiro/index.ts` (new) — `xkiroProvider` via `buildOpenAiCompatibleRegistryEntry`, `baseUrl https://api.xkiro.com/v1/chat/completions`, 39 pinned models with `contextLength` / `toolCalling` / `supportsVision` taken from the public models endpoint (2026-09-02). Wired in `open-sse/config/providers/index.ts` (import + `REGISTRY.xkiro`).
- `src/shared/constants/providers/apikey/gateways.ts` — canonical `xkiro` block (`serviceKinds: ["llm"]`, `passthroughModels: true`, `hasFree: true`, `freeNote`, `authHint`, `apiHint`). Bearer auth (`x-api-key` also accepted upstream).
- `src/shared/constants/providers.ts` — `"xkiro"` added to `AGGREGATOR_PROVIDER_IDS` (it fronts other vendors' models).

**Free-tier catalog**

- `open-sse/config/freeModelCatalog.data.ts` — 39 rows, all in pool **`xkiro-free`**, `monthlyTokens: 150_000_000`, `freeType: "recurring-daily"`, `tos: "caution"`, `hardStopGuaranteed: true`; `FREE_CATALOG_CURATED_AT` → `2026-09-03`. Evidence block (verbatim quotes, dated) sits above the rows:
  - https://xkiro.com/ — Free plan card: "$0 / month · Free forever · Free tokens 5M / day · Access to 40+ free models · No credit card"
  - https://docs.xkiro.com/models/tiers/ — "free — any account — Callable on every plan, including the free one, within a daily token allowance" (one allowance per account ⇒ one pool)
  - https://docs.xkiro.com/api/rate-limits/ — "Past it, free-model requests are blocked with a 429 until the daily reset" (⇒ `hardStopGuaranteed`)
  - `GET https://api.xkiro.com/v1/models` — the 40 `access_tier: "free"` rows (public, no key needed)
  - ToS (2026-07-30) forbids reselling/redistributing the service and violating the upstream providers' terms; personal proxy use is not addressed ⇒ `tos: "caution"`.
- **`openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark` is excluded** although it is tagged free upstream: xKiro does not declare where that route is served from (no provenance for an OpenAI-branded model on a third-party gateway), so pinning it would advertise a free model we cannot vouch for. The unit test locks the exclusion in.

**Tests**

- `tests/unit/free-provider-xkiro.test.ts` (new, TDD — red 4/4 before the implementation, green after): routable + canonical + aggregator; one 150M pool counted exactly once by `computeFreeModelTotals()` (with − without = 150,000,000); no `codex-spark` in registry or catalog; registry ⟷ catalog are the same 39 ids.

**Docs and counts (all gate-driven, `npm run check:docs-counts` + `check:docs-sync` green)**

- `docs/reference/PROVIDER_REFERENCE.md` regenerated (`npm run gen:provider-reference`, exact generator output).
- `README.md`, `llm.txt` + 41 `docs/i18n/*/llm.txt` mirrors (41 locales; the duplicate `in` locale was retired upstream), `docs/reference/FREE_TIERS.md` (headline, dated note, ToS row, per-provider row, hard-stop sentence, frontmatter date), `docs/architecture/{ARCHITECTURE,CODEBASE_DOCUMENTATION,REPOSITORY_MAP}.md`, `docs/frameworks/OPEN_SSE_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/diagrams/{readme-hero,promise-pillars,comparison-table,cli-terminal,free-tier-budget}.svg` (+ `docs/diagrams/README.md`), `public/images/tier-flow-{dark,light}.svg` — provider count, free-tier headline, entries/pools/hard-stop tallies, executor count, visible chips aligned with their own aria-labels (`90+` → `150+`, `352` → `357`, `348 more` → `353 more`).
- `AGENTS.md:49` and `package.json` `description`: **number only** (see operator note).

## Numbers before / after

Measured on this branch with the same code the gate uses (`computeFreeModelTotals()`, the canonical provider collections, `REGISTRY`); "before" = **PR1's head** (`fix/free-tier-quota-reaudit` @ `113b608`), which is now this PR's base.

| Metric                                             | Before (PR1 @ `113b608`) | After                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Canonical providers                                | 356                      | **357** (+1)                                   |
| Steady recurring free tokens / month               | ~1.47B                   | **~1.62B** (+150M)                             |
| First month (steady + one-off credits)             | ~2.10B                   | **~2.25B** (+150M)                             |
| Free-tier catalog entries                          | 442                      | **481** (+39)                                  |
| Recurring pool keys                                | 34                       | **35** (+`xkiro-free`)                         |

| Providers carrying `hasFree: true`                 | 152                      | **152**                                        |
| Provider executors (soft count)                    | 108                      | **109**                                        |

Every delta is exactly xKiro's own contribution — nothing else moved across the merge. Exact live values: steady `1,623,225,000`, first month `2,249,725,000`.

> **Why the headline reads ~1.62B and no longer ~1.63B:** this PR's contribution is unchanged (+150M). The baseline moved underneath it — PR1's re-audit reclassified `gemini` and `ollama-cloud` as uncapped (−80M), re-scoped `groq` to five per-model caps (+15M), raised `nara` to a 7M/day bucket (+60M) and reclassified `cerebras` as a one-time signup credit (−30M). PR1's ~1.47B + xKiro's 150M = **~1.62B**.

All "after" values are the ones `npm run check:docs-counts` reports as *actual* on this branch — none were hand-guessed.

## ⚠️ Operator note

This PR bumps the provider count in **`AGENTS.md:49`** ("356 LLM providers" → 357) and in **`package.json` `description`** — number only, demanded by `check:docs-counts` (STRICT), same precedent as #12440. `AGENTS.md` is an agent-instruction surface, so **explicit operator approval is needed at merge** for that one-line change.

Base sync done: this branch is merged with **PR1's head** `origin/fix/free-tier-quota-reaudit` @ `113b608` (merge commit `5732484`). Eight files conflicted, all of them headline-number/count drift:

- `open-sse/config/freeModelCatalog.data.ts` — took PR1's re-audited `nara` block (8 rows @ 210M with its evidence comment, replacing the old 3 rows @ 150M) **and** kept all 39 xKiro rows; `FREE_CATALOG_CURATED_AT` → `2026-09-03`. Verified as a set: 442 → 481, no PR1 row lost.
- `README.md`, `docs/reference/FREE_TIERS.md`, `docs/getting-started/FREE-TIERS-GUIDE.md`, `docs/diagrams/README.md` — took PR1's structure and wording (its re-audit narrative, the Groq per-model-caps phrasing), re-applied the xKiro prose, then set every count to what the gate reports live.
- `docs/diagrams/readme-hero.svg`, `docs/diagrams/free-tier-budget.svg` — number text nodes only. The budget card's bar segments and per-pool legend were recomputed from the live catalog (18 segments: 17 quantified pools + Groq's merged 30M), keeping the existing geometry. The `scripts/research/gen-budget-card-svg.mjs` generator was deliberately **not** used: its row regex predates `hardStopGuaranteed`, so it silently drops all 39 xKiro rows.
- `config/quality/file-size-baseline.json` — kept **both** justification keys (`_rebaseline_2026_09_03_12649_free_tier_reaudit_gateways` from PR1 and `_rebaseline_2026_09_03_12648_xkiro_provider` from this PR) and set the `gateways.ts` cap to the merged file's actual size, **1480**.

That number went stale the moment the 39 xKiro rows landed (the doc says 44 and the gate agrees). The test now derives both expected counts from the catalog itself, so it cannot drift again.

## Live validation — PENDING (awaiting the owner's free xKiro key; will be completed before marking the PR ready)

Done without a key (2026-09-02), as evidence of the validation endpoint and of the upstream model list the catalog was built from:

```bash

{"error":{"message":"Missing ClientApiKey. Send \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" or the \"x-api-key\" header.","type":"authentication_error","code":"authentication_error"}}   # HTTP 401
```

title: fix(config): persist background-degradation entry deletions
body:
## Summary

- `applyBackgroundDegradationSection()` (`src/lib/config/runtimeSettings.ts`) merged
  `{ ...getDefaultDegradationMap(), ...stored }`, so a stored map that omits a default key was
  indistinguishable from one that never touched it — the key was always back-filled from defaults and
  a deletion made through the dashboard reappeared on the next apply/restart.
- `detectionPatterns` in the same function already treats a present stored value as authoritative
  (defaults only when empty), so the two halves of the same object disagreed on semantics — the tell
  that this was an oversight, not intent.
- Fix: make `degradationMap` stored-authoritative-when-present, mirroring `detectionPatterns` and
  `normalizeBackgroundDegradation()` (which only keeps keys present in the stored record). No schema change.
- **Migration trade-off:** a config saved before this fix with an incomplete stored map — because it
  silently absorbed a "deletion" as an omission — stays incomplete once the merge stops back-filling.
  That is intentional (the stored map is now taken at face value), not a regression.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12424

body:
## Summary

A `messages` array containing a `null` (or any non-object) entry passes all entry guards and then crashes translators with a raw `TypeError`, surfacing as HTTP 500. Verified against real code:

- `openaiToClaudeRequest` with `messages: [null]` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'role')`

The existing guards (#5110, #6402, #6407, #6412) check that `messages` is a non-empty array and that scalars are well-typed, but nothing checks the entries themselves — and the route schema (`z.array(z.unknown())`) accepts `[null]`.

## Expected

Extend the entry-guard family: reject non-object message entries with a clear 400 (`messages: Expected array of objects`), same as the sibling guards. Well-formed requests behave exactly as before.

title: feat(ui): scroll-driven hand-weaving animation for the MiLADEiA rug
body:
Adds a self-contained WebGL component that knots the rug onto a bare loom, top down, as the page scrolls — warp cords, weft shots, then rows of coloured knots that grow, are beaten down and sheared.

It is not a reveal of the photograph. The artwork is resampled onto the rug's own knot lattice (420 x 707, the gauge measured from the source) and rebuilt from it every frame, so the motifs step the way hand-knotting steps them. The weaving front leans, undulates and frays rather than running level. "MiLADEiA" is in the artwork itself, so the same front constructs it letter by letter; the renderer only gives it the higher, glossier pile that cream silk has.

- One runtime asset (~300 KB), which is both the texture and the no-WebGL fallback image, so it is never downloaded twice. The knot lattice and the per-knot material data are derived in two GPU passes at init and the full-resolution artwork is released, leaving ~2.4 MB of VRAM.
- No animation library: one fullscreen triangle and three small GLSL ES 1.00 programs, so it runs on a WebGL 1 or 2 context alike.
- Progress is a pure function of scroll position, so reversing runs the weave backward through the same states and a flung scroll settles on exactly the frame a direct scroll would.
- Degrades to the finished rug as a plain image for no WebGL, a driver refusal, or prefers-reduced-motion. Quality tiers cap DPR and total pixels and drop fibre octaves; a rolling frame budget lowers the tier once if frames come in slow. Detail finer than the pixel grid fades toward its mean instead of aliasing.
- The context is created once and kept: disposing it calls loseContext(), and a canvas whose context has been force-lost can never hand out another, so resizing and scrolling away only pause the loop.

Presented at /rug, a route of its own — this repository's landing page belongs to a different product, and the component drops into whichever page should carry it.

body:
Itens OK-to-defer da review final whole-branch da PR #12508 (Fase 2 do Orchestration Canvas). Nenhum bloqueia; agrupados para rastreio.

- [ ] **History não hidrata `memoryHits`** — `reconstituteHistoricalTask` (`src/app/api/a2a/tasks/[id]/route.ts`) devolve `metadata: {}` e nunca lê o evento `memory_hits` persistido, então a seção "Memória" no drawer só existe dentro da janela de TTL em memória. Hidratar a partir de `listA2ATaskEvents`.
- [ ] **Repetir do Conductor perde `requirements.cli/model`** — o schema de detalhe do hub (`hubProxy.ts`) não parseia esses campos, então a nova execução pode cair em CLI/modelo diferente do original. Ou propagar, ou avisar no tooltip.

- [ ] **Recall de memória sem timeout próprio** — um backend HTTP lento (default de 30 s no `genericBackend`) atrasa o início da task. Um `Promise.race` de 1–2 s mantém o "best-effort" honesto.

title: feat(rate-limit): raise per-connection maxWaitMs cap from 2min to 10m…
body:
## Summary

Raises the per-connection `maxWaitMs` schema cap from **120,000ms (2 min)** to **600,000ms (10 min)** in the provider rate-limit overrides schema.

## Motivation

NVIDIA-hosted models (Kimi-K3, MiniMax-M3, DeepSeek, etc.) routinely take **3-5+ minutes** to respond. The current per-connection cap of 120,000ms forces operators to choose between:

1. **Setting a high global timeout** — which degrades fast-fail routing for ALL providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq respond in <10s and should fail fast)
2. **Accepting timeouts on slow NVIDIA models** — losing access to capable-but-slow models

This change lets operators set high timeouts **per-connection** via:
`Dashboard > Providers > NVIDIA > Edit > Rate Limit Overrides > Max Queue Wait (ms)`

## Changes

- `src/shared/validation/schemas/provider.ts` — raise rateLimitOverrideNumber cap from 120_000 to 600_000
- `tests/unit/provider-rate-limit-overrides-schema.test.ts` — update test ceiling assertion from 120001 to 600001

## Impact

| Provider Type | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Fast (Groq, OpenAI, Anthropic) | Inherits global (60s) | No change |
| Slow (NVIDIA) | Capped at 120s per-connection | Can now set up to 600s per-connection |

No default values change. The global requestQueue.maxWaitMs remains untouched.

## Testing

```bash
npx vitest run tests/unit/provider-rate-limit-overrides-schema.test.ts
```

Verified: setting maxWaitMs: 600000 in rateLimitOverrides now passes validation. Values above 600000 are still rejected.

title: fix(providers): OpenCode Zen Responses models reject OmniRoute auth header
body:
## Bug Description

OpenCode Zen's Responses models can reject the authentication header sent by OmniRoute. This was reproduced with the free `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` model after routing it through the Responses protocol.

This is complementary to #11046/#11049, which fixed the earlier URL/body mismatch for Muse Spark. The remaining question is the upstream auth scheme for Zen Responses requests, plus registry support for the new 1.3 model.

## Environment

- OmniRoute: v3.8.50 (Docker)
- OS: Linux
- Provider: `opencode-zen`
- Client surface: OmniRoute `POST /v1/chat/completions`
- Upstream: `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1`
- Model: `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free`
- API keys redacted in all tests and logs

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add an OpenCode Zen API-key connection to OmniRoute.
2. Discover the model from `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models`, or register it as a custom model because v3.8.50 does not yet declare `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` in the static registry.
3. Set the model compatibility/wire format to `openai-responses`.
4. Send a small request through OmniRoute using `opencode-zen/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free`.
5. Compare the same request directly against the upstream Responses endpoint using the same API key.

## Direct Upstream Verification

From the same host and with the same redacted API key:

- `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/responses` with `Authorization: Bearer ***` → HTTP 401 `Invalid API key`.
- The same request with `x-api-key: ***` → HTTP 200 response object.
- The same Authorization vs. `x-api-key` result was observed for `muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free`.

The OpenCode Zen documentation lists both Muse Contributor models on the `/v1/responses` endpoint.

## Actual Behavior Through OmniRoute

The request returns HTTP 500. The recent OmniRoute log reports:

```text
opencode-zen | all 2 accounts unavailable
provider=opencode-zen model=muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free lastStatus=500
```

The installed registry declares the provider as:

```typescript
authHeader: "Authorization",
authPrefix: "Bearer",
```

`OpencodeExecutor.buildHeaders()` also sends `Authorization: Bearer ...` for every non-Claude request format, including `openai-responses`.

The custom-header safety layer intentionally rejects auth header names such as `Authorization` and `x-api-key`, so this cannot be worked around through `customHeaders` or the Compatibility UI.

## Expected Behavior

OmniRoute should either:

1. send the authentication scheme required by the OpenCode Zen Responses endpoint; or
2. expose a safe, provider/model-scoped auth-header configuration; or
3. return a clear compatibility error instead of a generic 500/account-exhaustion result.

The new `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` model should also be declared with `targetFormat: "openai-responses"` and the appropriate capability metadata.

## Scope Question

Please confirm whether the `x-api-key` requirement is specific to the Muse Contributor backend or applies to all OpenCode Zen models served through `/v1/responses` (for example GPT/Grok Responses models). Standard Chat Completions models and Claude-format `/messages` models use different paths and were not claimed as affected by this report.

## Related Issues

- #11046 — Responses-shaped Muse request sent to `/chat/completions`
- #11049 — fixed Muse Spark 1.2 Responses routing
- #11142 — Muse model imported but unusable on older OmniRoute versions
- #12196 — related Responses routing gap on `opencode-go`, but not this Zen auth issue

## Validation Plan

- Add a regression test covering the selected auth header for Zen Responses models.
- Add `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free` to the Zen registry with `targetFormat: "openai-responses"`.
- Verify a real completion through OmniRoute, including the 1.2 Contributor model as a compatibility control.
- Keep the auth header out of logs and issue output.

title: feat(cache): configurable dual-layer semantic caching with Redis/In-Memory vector stores and model discovery
body:
## Summary
This PR implements a production-ready, configurable dual-layer semantic caching system for OmniRoute:

1. **Dual-Layer Architecture**:
   - **Layer 1 (Exact Match)**: Sub-millisecond direct SHA-256 hash lookup.
   - **Layer 2 (Semantic Match)**: Normalized cosine vector similarity search with configurable threshold (default 0.80) to serve paraphrased queries without upstream calls.

2. **Pluggable Vector Storage**:
   - **In-Memory (LRU)**: Built-in zero-dependency vector cache.
   - **Redis Vector Store**: Redis/Valkey backend with automatic connection pooling, RediSearch vector indexing support where available, and resilient fallback.

3. **Dashboard UI & Configuration (`/dashboard/settings/cache`)**:
   - Real-time provider and embedding model selection with auto-detected dimension and context-length badges.
   - Interactive "Test Embedding Model" button with live latency verification and DB credential auto-resolution.
   - Cache clear controls and storage backend toggles.

4. **Modality & Endpoint Guardrails**:
   - Automatically detects embedding models (e.g. `harrier-oss-v1-0.6b`, `text-embedding-*`) during sync and provider import.
   - Enforces endpoint policies to exclude non-chat models from chat completion endpoints, preventing 400 Bad Request errors.

5. **Audit & Metrics Sync**:
   - Dual-writes to both the vector store and SQLite (`storage.sqlite`) for local audit trail.
   - Accurately tracks and updates hit counts, tokens saved, and hit rates for both exact and semantic hits.

## Verification
- Unit and integration test suites: `tests/unit/model-embedding-discovery-and-cache.test.ts`, `tests/unit/cache-config-route-8219.test.ts`, and `tests/unit/ui/cache-settings-tab-bounds-8219.test.tsx` all passing.
- Verified against live upstream providers (Minimax `MiniMax-M3` and Lemonade `harrier-oss-v1-0.6b`) and live Redis (`redis://192.168.31.147:6379`).

title: fix(pricing): accept sync-written fields on PATCH and surface actionable save errors
body:
## Summary

- Saving model pricing from the dashboard (`/dashboard/costs/pricing`) fails with a `400` and a useless `Falha ao salvar preços: [object Object]` toast. Two overlapping defects:
  - `pricingFieldsSchema` (`.strict()`) only knew the 5 token-cost fields, but entries written by `transformToOmniRoute` (`src/lib/pricingSync.ts`) also carry `mode` + 12 non-token cost fields. The dashboard PATCHes the edited provider's full model map as echoed from GET, so strict validation rejected the API's own output. The schema now accepts those fields explicitly (still `.strict()` — unknown keys are still rejected).
  - `PricingTab.tsx` assumed `errorPayload.error` was a `string`; validation failures return the `{ error: { message, details } }` envelope. The save/reset paths now funnel the body through `extractApiErrorMessage`, which now renders `details` as `field: message` after the envelope message (previously `[object Object]`).

## Related Issues

- Closes #12494
- Claim + plan comment: https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/issues/12494#issuecomment-5529030380

## Validation

- [x] Change type: UI (+ shared validation schema / error-rendering util)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base; focused checks rerun afterward

Focused loop: `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/pricing-schema-roundtrip-12494.test.ts tests/unit/api-error-message-5340.test.ts tests/unit/pricing-sync-status-7955.test.ts tests/unit/model-overrides-provider-prefix-9557.test.ts` → 23/23 pass. `npm run lint` (with the repo suppressions config) and `npm run typecheck:core` are clean; branch is on the current `release/v3.8.51` tip (ad500de9e).

## Tests Added Or Updated

- Added `tests/unit/pricing-schema-roundtrip-12494.test.ts`: schema GET → PATCH round-trip with a fully sync-written entry, strict still rejects unknown/invalid values, validation-envelope rendering, and source-contract assertions for the PricingTab wiring.
- Regression re-run (all green): `tests/unit/api-error-message-5340.test.ts`, `tests/unit/pricing-sync-status-7955.test.ts`, `tests/unit/model-overrides-provider-prefix-9557.test.ts`.

## Coverage Notes

- Touches `src/` in three places (pricing schema, shared error-message util, PricingTab error paths). The new test file covers the schema branches (accepted sync fields, unknown-key rejection, invalid values) and the envelope-rendering branches (string error / message+details / message-only / fallback) directly.

## Reviewer Notes

- On save, echoed entries land in the user pricing namespace (pre-existing GET/PATCH design): after a manual save, `pricingSync` no longer auto-overwrites that provider. This follows the maintainer-diagnosed fix direction ("tolerar os campos não-token no PATCH — strip ou passthrough restrito"); explicit typed passthrough was chosen over stripping so the API round-trips its own GET output.
- `extractApiErrorMessage` now appends `details` (`field: message`) after the envelope message when present. Envelopes without `details` render byte-for-byte as before, so existing call sites only see richer messages on validation failures.
- `pricingFieldsSchema` rejects negatives via `min(0)`; `transformToOmniRoute` only persists `Number.isFinite` values, so legit LiteLLM data cannot trip it.

title: fix(ci): pin TLS_CLIENT_VERSION=1.16.0 (CVE-2025-68121) #12084
body:
## Summary
Pins `TLS_CLIENT_VERSION=1.16.0` in the Dockerfile to fix CVE-2025-68121 (Trivy CRITICAL, CVSS 9.8).

## Root Cause
- `bogdanfinn/tls-client` v1.15.1 ships with Go stdlib 1.24.1 containing an out-of-bounds slice read in `net/http` (CVE-2025-68121).
- The `tls-client-node` postinstall.js defaults to fetching `latest` from GitHub Releases API.
- On 2026-09-02, `latest` was still v1.15.1 — every clean build silently shipped the vulnerable `.so`/`.dylib` binary.

## Fix
Added `ARG TLS_CLIENT_VERSION=1.16.0` + `ENV TLS_CLIENT_VERSION=\${TLS_CLIENT_VERSION}` before the postinstall RUN block. This:
- Makes the version explicit and auditable
- Uses v1.16.0 (Go stdlib 1.24.7) which is not vulnerable
- Allows override via `--build-arg TLS_CLIENT_VERSION=1.16.0` (or newer patch)

## Testing
- Local build with clean checkout passes and `ldd` on the binary confirms v1.16.0
- Trivy scan of resulting image shows no CVE-2025-68121

Fixes #12084

title: fix(backend): chat dispatch ignores model-picker additions (customModels vs syncedAvailableModels)
body:
---
name: Bug report
about: Create a report to help us improve
title: "Chat dispatch ignores model picker additions (customModels vs syncedAvailableModels)"
labels: bug,area:dispatch
---

## Describe the bug

`getActiveProvidersWithSyncedModel` in `src/lib/db/models.ts` only reads from `key_value(namespace='syncedAvailableModels')` and ignores `key_value(namespace='customModels')`. Models added through the provider dashboard's "model picker" are written to `customModels`, but the chat dispatch path doesn't consult that namespace, so perfectly valid models return:

```
400 invalid_request_error
"Model '<model>' is not available in the active live catalog for provider '<provider>'"
```

even though the model is fully in the live catalog (visible via `GET /api/providers/{id}/models`).

## To Reproduce

1. Add a model through the provider dashboard model picker (e.g. `nvidia/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro-0813`)
2. Add that model to a combo, or reference it directly as `provider/model`
3. Send a chat request
4. Observe the error above
5. Run `POST /api/providers/{id}/sync-models` and the same request starts working — because sync rewrites `syncedAvailableModels` from the upstream catalog, but also drops any non-synced models (destructive side effect, not what the user asked for)

## Expected behavior

Chat dispatch should accept any model that's in either `customModels` (user-pinned via picker) **or** `syncedAvailableModels` (discovered from upstream catalog).

## Actual behavior

Only `syncedAvailableModels` is consulted. Models added via picker are invisible to chat until the next sync — and sync is destructive.

## Environment

- OmniRoute version: 3.8.50+ running via `omniroute serve --daemon --port 20128`
- Affected providers observed: nvidia, opencode-go
- Triggered when scaling to 64 sub-agents × 16 chats, the `Main` combo with `nvidia/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro-0813` in the chain

## Related

- #12298 (stale dashboard data)
- #12168 (provider unhealthy status)
- #12073, #11804

## Proposed fix (sketch)

Union `key_value(namespace='customModels')` into the live-model set in `getActiveProvidersWithSyncedModel`. ~15 lines, additive, no migration.

title: chore(deps): pin browserslist override to ^4.28.8
body:
## Summary

One-line `package.json` override pinning `browserslist` to `^4.28.8` to fix a cold-install `RangeError: Out of range argument` in node 22 when downstream tooling (autoprefixer >=10.5.0, caniuse-lite via vite 8) requires the newer query-parser.

## Why

Without this override, `npm install` resolves browserslist to ^4.27.x, which fails on the `'last-N-versions'` query syntax with:

```
RangeError: Out of range argument
    at Object.parse (node:internal/querystring:159:23)
    at parseDataQuery (.../browserslist/node.js:...)
```

The `browserslist` library is pulled in transitively through `@yarnpkg/parsers`, `monaco-editor`, and `vite`. Pinning the override removes the failure mode without changing the direct dependency tree.

## Change

```diff
   "overrides": {
+    "browserslist": "^4.28.8",
     "onnxruntime-node": "1.24.3",
```

## Test

```bash
rm -rf node_modules
npm ci
npm run build
```

Expected: clean install, no `RangeError`.

## Provenance

This is a re-built 1-line delta from `KooshaPari/OmniRoute@6da8329cb`. The original commit also modified `README.md`, `config/quality/eslint-suppressions.json`, and `config/quality/quality-baseline.json`; those changes have already landed on upstream `release/v3.8.51` (or were re-baselined). Only this single `package.json` line remains portable as of 2026-09-03.

These are private, non-internet-routable addresses, so this is not independently exploitable — it discloses that the maintainer runs a Proxmox host and a CI runner VM on a specific private subnet, which is only useful as minor reconnaissance if combined with another foothold on the same network.

Not independently actionable; listed for completeness as an infrastructure-disclosure hygiene item rather than a standalone vulnerability.

Convenience defaults for a personal/maintainer environment were left in a script committed to the public repository instead of requiring the values be supplied via environment variable or a local, gitignored config file.
