title: fix(i18n): quote raw <name> in the auto-sync profiles description
body:
## Summary

- `featureFlags.definitions.OMNIROUTE_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES.description` (`src/i18n/messages/en.json:12971` and the same key in the other 41 locales) carries the literal path `~/.claude/profiles/<name>/settings.json`. next-intl parses `<name>` as a rich-text tag; `FeatureFlagsGrid.tsx:426-428` renders the description through plain `t()` and never passes a tag element, so the message fails to compile with `INVALID_MESSAGE: UNCLOSED_TAG` and the Settings → Feature Flags card shows the raw key instead of the description, in every language.
- The placeholder is now wrapped in ICU single quotes (`'<name>'`) in all 42 locale files and in the TypeScript default (`src/shared/constants/featureFlagDefinitions.ts:613`), the same form as #12369 for `ccOnboardingKeyPlaceholder`. One substring changed per file, nothing else touched. Reproduced and verified against `use-intl`'s `development` build (the one Turbopack dev mode loads): raw `<name>` → `UNCLOSED_TAG` + key fallback; `'<name>'` → the literal path renders; `<name>` → the entities are returned verbatim by `t()` and would be displayed as text, so the entity form used by earlier fixes is not suitable for a real file path the user is meant to copy. The production build of `use-intl` tolerates the raw tag on the plain `t()` path, which is why the symptom is context-dependent, as the report says.
- Deliberately out of scope: the reporter's second follow-up (a CI gate that parses every `en.json` value with the ICU parser). `tests/unit/i18n-vi-completeness.test.ts` already skips any key whose English source does not parse, so that gate is a separate change with its own allowlist; it will be proposed as an issue first. This PR fixes one message and adds one focused guard.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12505
- Related to #12302 / #12369 (same class, `ccOnboardingKeyPlaceholder`, same ICU-quote form)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: i18n
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: new test 5/5; `tests/unit/i18n-vi-completeness.test.ts`, `i18n-cc-alias-unclosed-tags`, `i18n-deno-relay-unclosed-tag`, `i18n-placeholder-parity`, `i18n-ui-value-drift`, `i18n-translation-ratio-gate`, `settings-i18n-keys`, `i18n-config` 43/43; `npm run i18n:sync-ui:dry`, `npm run i18n:check-ui-coverage`, `npm run i18n:check-value-drift`, `npm run i18n:check-glossary` all PASS; `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK; `node scripts/check/check-complexity-ratchets.mjs --base-ref origin/release/v3.8.51` OK; `vi.json` carries no `__MISSING__` marker for this key
- [ ] `npm run lint` — eslint and prettier run on the two touched source/test files only (exit 0); the repository-wide run was not executed for a one-substring locale change
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base `release/v3.8.51`; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR
- SonarQube is temporarily opt-in while the private project has no quota; it is not a PR gate.

Mutation: with the locale/TS change reverted the new test fails 3 of 5 cases (ICU parse, quoted form, TS default); green 5/5 with the change.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/i18n-feature-flag-auto-sync-profiles-tag-12505.test.ts` (new, 5 cases): the key exists in all 42 locales (count from `config/i18n.json`, no BOM); every locale value parses with `@formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser`; every locale uses `profiles/'<name>'/` and neither the raw nor the entity form; `createTranslator` renders `~/.claude/profiles/<name>/settings.json` literally in every locale with no `INVALID_MESSAGE`; the TypeScript default parses and uses the same quoting.

## Coverage Notes

- `src/shared/constants/featureFlagDefinitions.ts`: one string literal changed; the new test imports the module and asserts the `OMNIROUTE_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES` description. No logic changed, no coverage moved.
- `src/i18n/messages/*.json` are data files, covered by the new test and by the existing `i18n-vi-completeness` ICU-regression case, which now actively checks this key because the English source parses.

## Reviewer Notes

- The diff is 42 locale lines plus one TS line, each replacing `profiles/<name>/` with `profiles/'<name>'/`; a `git diff --word-diff` review confirms nothing else moved (no reordering, no BOM, same trailing newline).
- The open PRs that touch the locale files (#12488, #12487, #12486, #12369, #12148 and others) edit different keys; none touches `OMNIROUTE_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES`, so a rebase is textual-only. #12486 edits `featureFlagDefinitions.ts` around lines 298-323, away from line 613.

title: fix(db): auto-clean conversation_turn_nodes and orphaned conversations
body:
## Summary

- `conversation_turn_nodes` and `agentic_conversations` (migrations 155/156, #10263) had no retention path at all: `src/lib/db/cleanup.ts` never referenced either table, there is no cascade FK, and nothing else deletes from them. The reporter's numbers in #12453 (1.15M node rows, ~775 MB of a 1.1 GB `storage.sqlite` after four days, ~190 MB/day) are the same failure class as #6848 / #4354 / #10421.
- The nodes are identity-only: the transcript view resolves each turn's display content from the `call_logs` row that `last_correlation_id` points at (`156_conversation_turn_nodes.sql` header). Once `cleanupCallLogs` purges that row the node can never render again, so both tables now follow the existing `retention.callLogs` window (`src/types/databaseSettings.ts`) instead of getting a knob of their own, as the issue proposes. No new dashboard setting, no new environment variable, and `docs/reference/ENVIRONMENT.md` is untouched because there is nothing new to document there.
- Two new functions registered at the end of `runAutoCleanup`: `cleanupConversationTurnNodes()` deletes nodes with `last_seen_at` before the cutoff through the shared `deleteFromTableBefore` helper (`src/lib/db/cleanup/usagePurge.ts`, so a database that predates migration 156 is a no-op rather than an error); `cleanupAgenticConversations()` then sweeps roots past the same cutoff that have no remaining node, with `WHERE last_seen_at < ? AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM conversation_turn_nodes n WHERE n.conversation_id = agentic_conversations.id)`. The `last_seen_at` guard uses the index from migration 155 and keeps a root that `createConversation` wrote moments ago, before the same request inserted its nodes.
- Semantics are the ones the issue describes: deleting an old node only affects reconnect anchors, and a conversation resumed after the window mints a new id, which is already the documented anchor-miss behavior of `resolveConversationId`. Deliberately out of scope: the "Clear all" / `resetUsageHistory` paths (a separate, user-triggered contract), and a `last_seen_at` index on `conversation_turn_nodes`. The node DELETE is a table scan today because migration 156 defined no index on that column; it runs once per cleanup cycle, and I can send the index as a follow-up migration if the maintainer wants it.

title: fix(images): /v1/images/edits flattens a combo to its first target and never falls back
body:
### Problem / Use Case `/v1/images/edits` accepts a combo name, but it flattens the combo to its first target and never tries the others, while `/v1/images/generations` runs the full combo strategy with per-target fallback since #9239. The same combo therefore behaves differently on the two image routes. Where it happens on `release/v3.8.51`: - `resolveSingleImageComboTarget()` (`src/lib/images/imageRouteModel.ts:60-75`) returns only the first target that has a `modelStr`; `resolveImageRouteModel()` uses it for every bare (slash-less) name at `:91-96`. - `src/app/api/v1/images/edits/route.ts:346-365` calls `resolveImageRouteModel(fullModel)` once and continues with a single `resolvedModel`. There is no `getComboByName` / `executeImageCombo` diversion in that file; the one in `generations/route.ts:155-163` runs *before* `resolveImageRouteModel` precisely "so we skip single-target flattening" (comment at `:156`). - The edit-capable branches are `codex-responses` (`edits/route.ts:395`), `fal-ai` edit models (`:484`), `adobe-firefly-image` (`:532`), `openrouter` (`:551`) and custom OpenAI-compatible nodes (`:605+`). Anything else with a built-in config gets `400 Image edit is not supported for built-in provider "

"` at `:597-603`; a built-in with no credentials gets `401 No credentials for provider` at `:414-419`; a custom node with none gets `400` at `:623-628`; rate limits return `429` at `:420` / `:629`. Concrete case — combo `img-edit` with targets `[openai/gpt-image-2, codex/gpt-image-2]` or `[adobe-firefly/firefly-image-4, codex/gpt-image-2]`, Codex credentials present: - `POST /v1/images/generations {"model":"img-edit"}` → `executeImageCombo` filters image-capable targets, iterates them, skips the ones without credentials or rate-limited (`open-sse/services/imageCombo.ts:98-122`), returns the first success with `fallbackAttempts` in the meta headers. - `POST /v1/images/edits` with `model=img-edit` → resolves to the first target and answers `400 Image edit is not supported for built-in provider "openai"` (or `401 No credentials for provider: adobe-firefly` when Firefly is first and not connected). The second target could have served the edit and is never consulted. The combo's order also matters more than it should: a user who lists a generation-only provider first gets a hard 400 on edits even though the combo is perfectly valid for generations. ### Proposed Solution Give `/v1/images/edits` the same combo semantics as generations, in two steps so the first is a pure refactor: 1. Extract the target loop of `executeImageCombo()` (`imageCombo.ts:83-156`: credential resolution, `allRateLimited` skip, terminal-vs-retryable classification, fallback count) into a generic `runImageComboTargets(targets, { filter, dispatch })` and have `executeImageCombo` call it with `handleImageGeneration` as the dispatch. No behaviour change on generations. 2. In `edits/route.ts`, when the model is a bare combo name, run the same loop with an edit-capable filter (Codex, Firefly, Fal edit models, OpenRouter, custom OpenAI-compatible nodes) and a dispatch that reuses the route's existing per-provider branches; keep the terminal statuses (400/401/403) terminal per target so a combo with no edit-capable target still answers clearly, and surface `fallbackAttempts` in the meta headers as generations does. Open points I would like your call on before writing it: - Whether a target that answers 401 (no credentials) should be skipped like on generations (`imageCombo.ts:109-113` treats missing credentials as retryable) or stay terminal as the edits route does today. - Whether the combo diversion should also apply to `n > 1` / multi-reference requests, or only to the single-image path first. ### Alternatives Considered - Only re-ordering the combo in the dashboard: works for one user, but any combo that mixes generation-only and edit-capable providers stays order-sensitive on edits and not on generations. - Making `resolveSingleImageComboTarget` prefer an edit-capable target when called from the edits route: fixes the 400 but still gives up on the first credential/rate-limit failure, so it is half of the generations behaviour. - Having the edits route call `executeImageCombo` directly: not possible today, it dispatches `handleImageGeneration` and does not carry the multipart image bytes, hence the generic runner in step 1. ### Acceptance Criteria - `POST /v1/images/edits` with a bare combo name whose first target is not edit-capable, and whose later target is, returns the later target's result with `fallbackAttempts >= 1`. - A combo with no edit-capable target returns one 400 that names the combo, not the first provider. - Rate-limited (429) and 5xx targets fall through to the next target; the last error is returned when all fail, as on generations. - `/v1/images/generations` combo behaviour and `tests/unit/combo/image-combo.test.ts` are unchanged by step 1. ### Area Proxy / Routing, Provider Support ### Related Provider(s) Codex, Adobe Firefly, Fal, OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible custom providers ### Additional Context Combo/alias resolution on both routes: #3214 / #3215 (PR #3219), bare combos over aliases: #3527. Full combo strategy on generations only: #9239 (PR #9499; `open-sse/services/imageCombo.ts`, `src/app/api/v1/images/generations/route.ts`). Response shape fix that touched both routes: #12268 / PR #12362. Base `release/v3.8.51`, commit `1a0375f`. ### Expected Test Plan - Extend `tests/unit/image-routes-combo-edits-3214-3215.test.ts` (the file #9239's test plan pointed at for multi-target combos) with: first target generation-only + second Codex → 200 from Codex; first target without credentials + second with → 200; no edit-capable target → single 400; all rate-limited → 429. - Keep `tests/unit/combo/image-combo.test.ts` green after the extraction, plus `image-generation-route`, `8510-adobe-firefly-edits-route`, `10197-openrouter-image-edits-route`, `fal-image-edit`; `typecheck:core`, `check:open-sse-typecheck`, `check-complexity-ratchets`. Happy to send the two PRs (refactor first, then the edits wiring) once you have picked the 401 semantics.

title: fix(gamification): action_count badges are computed over a 30-day-pruned xp_audit_log
body:
### Problem / Use Case

The four `request` action-count badges are computed over a table that is pruned every 30 days by default, so the lifetime totals they describe can never be reached on a default install.

`checkActionCountBadges()` (`src/lib/gamification/events.ts:171-198`, called from `emitGamificationEvent` at `:104` on every awarded action) counts rows in `xp_audit_log`:

```ts
"SELECT COALESCE(COUNT(*), 0) AS count FROM xp_audit_log WHERE api_key_id = ? AND action = ?"
```

and compares the result with the thresholds `first-token` 1, `token-consumer` 1,000, `token-machine` 10,000, `token-whale` 100,000 (`events.ts:185-198`). `getActionCount()` in `src/lib/gamification/badges.ts:324-342` does the same for the `action_count` criteria that `evaluateBadges()` reads.

Since #6801 (PR #7260), `cleanupXpAuditLog()` (`src/lib/db/cleanup.ts:348-368`) deletes every `xp_audit_log` row older than `retention.xpAuditLog` days and runs inside `runAutoCleanup()` (`cleanup.ts:460`). The default is 30 days (`src/types/databaseSettings.ts:125`, schema cap 365 in `src/shared/validation/settingsSchemas.ts:573`) and auto-cleanup is on by default.

So with the defaults the badge descriptions in `badges.ts:32-59` ("Made 1,000 API requests", "Made 10,000 API requests", "Made 100,000 API requests") are effectively "made N requests inside the last 30 days". A key that sends 900 requests a month for a year never unlocks Token Consumer; Token Whale needs about 3,300 requests a day, every day. The `token_share` ladder (`generous` 1,000 up to `community-hero` 1,000,000) has the same shape, and the `unique_count` (`badges.ts:349-362`) and `first` (`badges.ts:485-501`, `MIN(created_at)`) criteria read the same pruned table.

**Reproduction** (focused test against `release/v3.8.51`, temp `DATA_DIR`, default retention):

1. Insert 1,200 `xp_audit_log` rows for one key, `action = 'request'`, `created_at = '2026-07-01 12:00:00'`.
2. The `events.ts:178` query returns 1200.
3. `await cleanupXpAuditLog()` returns `{ deleted: 1200 }`; the same query now returns 0.
4. `await emitGamificationEvent({ apiKeyId, action: "request" })` — the query returns 1, `hasBadge(key, "token-consumer")` is `false` although the key has made 1,201 requests.

```
{ before: 1200, deleted: 1200, after: 0 }
{ afterRequest: 1, tokenConsumer: false, firstToken: true }
```

The same sequence with rows dated inside the window unlocks the badge, which is what makes this a retention interaction and not a badge bug.

### Proposed Solution

Two ways to make the counts durable; the choice is yours:

**Option A — durable per-key, per-action counter (recommended).** Add a small `xp_action_counts (api_key_id, action, count, updated_at)` table incremented in `addXp()` (`src/lib/db/gamification.ts:157-174`, the single insert point) in the same statement batch as the audit row, backfilled once from whatever `xp_audit_log` still holds in the migration, and read by both `checkActionCountBadges()` and `getActionCount()`. Retention keeps pruning the audit log; badges no longer depend on it. This mirrors how `user_levels.total_xp` already survives the prune.

**Option B — exclude `xp_audit_log` from the default prune.** Set the default to the 365-day cap or make the row opt-in, and add a note to the retention setting that pruning resets the request badges. Cheapest change, but it only stretches the window and gives back the unbounded growth #6801 wanted to stop.

Either way the badge descriptions and the retention setting's help text should agree on what is being counted.

### Alternatives Considered

- Counting from `call_logs` / usage history instead of the audit log: those tables have their own retention (`callLogs`, `usageHistory` in the same settings block) and are not keyed by gamification action, so the same problem moves rather than disappears.
- Using `user_levels.total_xp / XP per request` as a proxy: XP per action is not constant (anti-cheat can reject awards, `token_share` and `daily_login` add XP) so the derived count drifts.
- Pinning the count on the first row's `id` (`MAX(id) - MIN(id)`): breaks as soon as several keys interleave.

### Acceptance Criteria

- With default retention, a key whose `request` rows are older than 30 days still unlocks `token-consumer` on its 1,000th lifetime request after cleanup has run.
- `cleanupXpAuditLog()` keeps deleting audit rows; `runAutoCleanup()` result shape is unchanged.
- `getActionCount()` and `checkActionCountBadges()` agree on the same source.
- Existing `tests/unit/db-cleanup-xp-audit-log.test.ts` and `tests/unit/gamification/*` stay green.

### Area

Analytics / Usage Tracking, Other (gamification)

### Related Provider(s)

None

### Additional Context

Retention prune introduced by #6801 / #7260. Badge dedup guard: #3472. Sibling gamification issue on the same award path: #12426. Base `release/v3.8.51`, commit `1a0375f`.

### Expected Test Plan

- New unit test that seeds rows outside the window, runs `cleanupXpAuditLog()`, emits one `request` event and asserts the badge unlocks (red on the current base, green with either option).
- Migration test for the backfill if Option A is chosen.
- `tests/unit/db-cleanup-xp-audit-log.test.ts`, `tests/unit/gamification/*.test.ts`, `typecheck:core`, `check:db-rules`.

I can send a PR demonstrating whichever option you prefer.

title: fix(devin): accept Windows sandbox paths in the agentic home check
body:
## Summary

- `isIsolatedHome` (`open-sse/executors/devin-cli-agentic.ts:118-120`) recognized only `/home/bridge` and paths containing `/.sandbox/`. On Windows, `DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME=C:\Users\...\.sandbox\home` is `path.isAbsolute()`-true but never matches the forward-slash `.sandbox` check, so `buildDevinChildEnv` threw `unsafe_devin_home` (`[500]: DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME must be an absolute path inside the bridge sandbox`) on every Windows host, whatever the value.
- The helper now normalizes `\` to `/` before comparing (the same approach as `normalizeCommandToken` in `src/lib/acp/registry.ts:283-285`) and is exported as `isIsolatedDevinHome`. Accepted forms: `/home/bridge`, and any absolute path with a `.sandbox` directory segment, on Linux (`/opt/omniroute/.sandbox/home`) and Windows (`C:\Users\x\.sandbox\home`, `D:/omniroute/.sandbox/home`, UNC `\\server\share\.sandbox\home`).
- Deliberately unchanged: `path.isAbsolute()` in `buildDevinChildEnv` still gates absoluteness (a relative `.sandbox` path is still rejected), and `.sandbox` is still required as a directory segment. The issue's example `C:\Users\...\devin-sandbox` does not contain `.sandbox` and is still rejected; the documented Windows form is `<drive>:\...\.sandbox\...`. Accepting an arbitrary configured Windows directory would loosen the fail-closed contract, so it is left as the maintainer's call. `docs/reference/ENVIRONMENT.md:423` notes the Windows form.

title: fix(orchestration): keep the first staleSince while a source keeps failing
body:
## Summary

- `buildSourceStatuses` (`src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/orchestration/hooks/useOrchestrationSnapshot.ts:63-90`) stamps every failed source with the current poll's `nowIso` (lines 76, 79, 87), and the poll loop replaced the whole list with `setStatuses(next)`. With the `sourceStale` message now live, `SourceNode` (`nodes/SourceNode.tsx:24-28`) therefore read "stale since <last poll>" instead of the first error, and because `snapshotContentKey` serialises `s.sources`, the key changed on every 5s/30s tick for as long as a source was down — re-minting the node/edge arrays the `React.memo` gate exists to protect.
- This is the second bullet of #12392 ("`staleSince` avança a cada poll"). Fix: a pure `carryStaleSince(prev, next)` helper (line 99) copies the previous `staleSince` onto a source that was already failing, applied through the functional update `setStatuses((prev) => carryStaleSince(prev, next))` (line 152). A source that recovers is pushed as `{ ok: true }` with no `staleSince`, so the next failure is stamped fresh; a first failure keeps this poll's `nowIso`. `buildSourceStatuses`, `mergeSnapshot` and the conductor `offline` branch are untouched.
- Deliberately out of scope: the other bullets of #12392 (toolbar debounce race, placeholder-only stale indicator in `mergeSnapshot`, a11y, `noMatches`, particle budget, drawer error banner, `toggleCsv`) — each is a separate surface and the issue stays open.

title: fix(video): clamp estimateJpegFrameBytes, reuse the shared JPEG prefix
body:
## Summary

- `estimateJpegFrameBytes` (`src/lib/guardrails/videoBridgeFrameContract.ts:24-27`) subtracted the padding count from the floored estimate with no floor of its own, so the padding-only payloads the charset-only pattern admits (`data:image/jpeg;base64,=` and `==`) came back as `-1`. Consequence-free in today's upper-bound usage, as #12323 notes, but a documented byte estimate never goes negative: the return is now `Math.max(0, ...)` (item 1).
- The three encode sites named in the issue (`videoBridgeContactSheet.ts:123`, `videoBridgeRuntime.ts:1000`, `videoBridgeDrilldownLifecycle.ts:173`) still built their frame data URIs from a hardcoded `data:image/jpeg;base64,` template literal; they now import `JPEG_FRAME_DATA_URI_PREFIX` from the shared contract (item 2). Byte-for-byte identical output, since the constant is the same literal.
- Deliberately out of scope: item 3 (`videoBridgeBrokerClient.ts:104`, the case-sensitive broker-output regex) and item 4 (structural base64 validation). Both are behaviour decisions per the issue text, so the issue stays open; this PR is `Refs`, not `Closes`. `videoBridgeRuntime.ts` gains a single import of the zero-dependency contract module, so no import cycle is introduced (`videoBridgeContactSheet.ts` already imported both).

## Related Issues

- Closes #
- Related to #12323 (items 1 and 2)
- Related to #12322 (the shared contract this builds on)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: other (backend guardrails / video frame contract)

- `tests/unit/guardrails/videoBridgeFrameContract.test.ts` (2 new cases): padding-only payloads (`=`, `==`, `A=`, `A==`) estimate `>= 0`, stay an upper bound of the real decode, and `=`/`==` estimate exactly `0`; and a source-level check that the three encode sites no longer contain the `data:image/jpeg;base64,` literal and do reference `JPEG_FRAME_DATA_URI_PREFIX`. Red on the base (2 fail / 3 pass: `"=" estimated -1`, `videoBridgeContactSheet.ts hardcodes the JPEG prefix`), green with the change (5/5). The three existing cases are unchanged.

title: fix(compression): terminate idle workers instead of dropping them
body:
## Summary

- `CompressionWorkerPool.finish()` (`open-sse/services/compression/compressionWorkerPool.ts:188`) evicted an idle worker with `this.remove(slot, false)`, and `remove()` (`:198-203`) only called `worker.terminate()` `if (terminate)`. The idle path therefore deleted the slot from the pool set but never terminated the thread; `compressionWorker.ts:13` keeps a `parentPort.on("message")` listener, so the worker's event loop and V8 isolate stayed alive forever, and `dispatch()` (`:156`) spawned a replacement because `workers.size < size`. The `OMNI_COMPRESSION_WORKERS` cap held in bookkeeping only: every idle cycle leaked one live thread. This is the mechanism confirmed on #11804 (request-driven thread growth, ~90 threads parked in `ep_poll`, RSS far outside the main heap) and the one-line patch the reporter measured on a live instance: 57 leaked workers / 72 threads / 5.77 GB climbing before, 0 leaked / 15 threads / 846 MB flat after.
- `remove()` now always terminates the thread. The `terminate` parameter is removed rather than flipped at the idle call site: `close()` and `fail()` already passed `true`, so the parameter only existed to express the buggy case. A short comment on `remove()` records why dropping the slot alone is not enough. `close()`, `fail()`, timeouts and the queue/dispatch logic are otherwise unchanged; `terminate()` failures are still swallowed as before.
- Out of scope, on purpose: the `callLogArtifactWorker` hypothesis raised mid-thread (later marked unconfirmed by its author), the six bundled copies of the pool in the Next.js server chunks (they pick this change up at build time), and any change to the idle timeout or pool size defaults.

## Related Issues

- Closes #11804
- Related to #12245 (the combo loop-safety timer leak reported on the same issue, already merged)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: other (compression worker pool, `open-sse/`)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: `tests/unit/compression/compression-worker.test.ts` + `tests/unit/compression/compression-worker-file-resolution.test.ts` 17/17 (4 suites), `node scripts/check/check-complexity-ratchets.mjs --base-ref origin/release/v3.8.51` OK (0 violations, base 0), `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK, `npm run typecheck:core` exit 0
- [ ] `npm run lint` — eslint run on the two touched source files only (`--suppressions-location config/quality/eslint-suppressions.json`), exit 0; the repository-wide command was not run
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base `release/v3.8.51` (`1a0375fba`); focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR
- SonarQube is temporarily opt-in while the private project has no quota; it is not a PR gate.

Red/green: the new case fails on the base with `idle eviction must terminate the worker thread: 0 !== 1` and passes with the change (three consecutive runs, 8/8 in the file).

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/compression/compression-worker.test.ts` (1 new case, "terminates an idle worker instead of only dropping it from the pool"): spies on `Worker.prototype.terminate` and `Worker.prototype.postMessage` around a local `{ size: 1, idleMs: 50 }` pool, runs one job, waits past the idle window, and asserts that exactly one worker was spawned, that `terminate()` was called once, and that the process does not retain the worker's `MessagePort` (`process.getActiveResourcesInfo()`). The `finally` block restores both prototypes, closes the pool, and terminates any worker the pool forgot, so a future regression fails the assertion instead of keeping the test runner alive. The seven existing cases are untouched.
- No `stryker.conf.json` change: `open-sse/services/compression/` is not in the `mutate` list.

## Coverage Notes

- `open-sse/services/compression/compressionWorkerPool.ts`: the idle path of `finish()` and the unconditional `terminate()` in `remove()` are exercised by the new case; `close()` by the new case's `finally` and the existing timeout case; `fail()` by the existing "fails open" case. No touched file lost coverage.

## Reviewer Notes

- Behavioural change is limited to idle eviction: the thread is now terminated at the moment it is removed from the set, which is what `close()` and `fail()` already did. Nothing about job routing changes, so a request arriving after eviction still gets a freshly spawned worker exactly as before.
- Anyone patching an installed 3.8.50/3.8.51 bundle by hand should note that the minified idle call site appears in five files (four Next.js runtime chunks plus `open-sse/mcp-server/server.js`), as documented on the issue; a normal build from this branch covers all of them.
- No migrations, feature flags, or env changes.

title: fix(gemini): strip prefixItems from Gemini tool schemas
body:
## Summary

- `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS` (`open-sse/translator/helpers/geminiHelper.ts:9-105` on the base) is the only strip-list `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` applies to tool parameter schemas (`removeUnsupportedKeywords`, `geminiHelper.ts:643`), and it did not contain the JSON-Schema-2020-12 tuple keyword `prefixItems`. Claude Code's built-in tools describe `[start_line, end_line]` ranges as a tuple nested under `items`, so every tool-bearing Claude Code request routed to a Gemini model was rejected before generation with `400 Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "prefixItems" at 'tools[0].function_declarations[1].parameters.properties[5].value.properties[0].value.items': Cannot find field` (#12509). All three tool shapes that `buildGeminiTools` accepts go through the same cleaner (`geminiToolsSanitizer.ts:207`, `:220` for Claude `input_schema`, `:238` for OpenAI `function.parameters`), so the Claude Messages compatibility path the reporter uses and the OpenAI path were both affected.
- Before: `prefixItems` survived at every nesting level (top-level array property, sibling of `items`, and the reporter's tuple under `items`) and reached Gemini verbatim. After: `prefixItems` is added to `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS` next to `uniqueItems` (#9617), so it is removed recursively at every level, the same way `multipleOf`, `strict` and `encrypted` already are. When the tuple carried `items: false` (the 2020-12 idiom for "no extra elements"), Phase 8 `ensureArrayItems` (`geminiHelper.ts:733` on the base) already injects `{ type: "string" }`, so the parameter stays a valid Gemini array with an `items` schema; when a regular `items` schema sits next to `prefixItems`, that `items` schema is kept untouched.
- Deliberately out of scope: promoting `prefixItems[0]` into `items` (the tuple's element types can differ, and Gemini has no way to express positional typing, so the safe default `items` schema is the honest translation); touching `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_CONSTRAINTS` beyond what it already derives from the Set; any change to the Antigravity envelope or to response schemas.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12509
- Related to #9617 (same class of fix, `uniqueItems`)
- Related to #12310 (touches the same file; see Reviewer Notes)

## Validation

Choose the change type and focused loop from the
[Contribution Golden Path](../docs/ops/CONTRIBUTION_GOLDEN_PATH.md). The full unit suite,
Vitest, the 60% coverage gate, and the production build all run in CI on this PR (#8329):

- [x] Change type: provider (Gemini tool-schema translation)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: `tests/unit/12509-gemini-prefixitems.test.ts` 5/5 plus the neighbouring Gemini schema suites (`9617-gemini-uniqueitems`, `gemini-codex-encrypted-tool-schema`, `gemini-schema-recursive-type`, `gemini-strict-tool-schema`, `gemini-tool-params-object-3357`, `translator-gemini-schema-pattern-property`, `9568-gemini-tool-casing-mismatch`, `gemini-tool-choice`, `v1beta-gemini-tool-calling-6222`) 45/45; `node scripts/check/check-complexity-ratchets.mjs --base-ref origin/release/v3.8.51` OK; `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK; `npm run typecheck:core` exit 0; eslint on the two touched `.ts` files exit 0
- [ ] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base `release/v3.8.51` (`1a0375fba`); focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR
- SonarQube is temporarily opt-in while the private project has no quota; it is not a PR gate.

Mutation: with the `"prefixItems"` entry removed from `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS` (the base), all 5 new tests fail (0/5); with it, 5/5 pass.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/12509-gemini-prefixitems.test.ts` (new, 5 cases): the reporter's shape — a `[start_line, end_line]` tuple nested under `items` with `items: false` — through the OpenAI `function.parameters` path and through the Claude `input_schema` path; a top-level `prefixItems` tuple with no `items` (asserts Gemini still gets an `items` schema); `prefixItems` next to a regular `items` schema (asserts that `items` survives unchanged); and a guard that `prefixItems` is registered in `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS`. Every case asserts the serialized `functionDeclarations` no longer contain `prefixItems`. Red on the base (0/5), green with the change (5/5).
- No existing test file changed.

## Coverage Notes

- `open-sse/translator/helpers/geminiHelper.ts`: the one-entry change to `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS` is exercised end-to-end through `buildGeminiTools` → `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` → `removeUnsupportedKeywords` and `ensureArrayItems` by the new test file; the existing `9617-gemini-uniqueitems.test.ts` and the other Gemini schema suites above stay green.
- No touched file lost coverage; the diff to production code is a Set entry plus its comment.

## Reviewer Notes

- #12310 (`fix(gemini): preserve nullable in response schemas`) edits the same file, but only `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity`'s signature and body (`@@ -621` and `@@ -631`); this PR only touches the `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS` literal at the top of the file, so the two apply in either order without a conflict. #12310's own guard test (`nullable` must stay out of the Set) is unaffected.
- The reporter's real payload has `prefixItems` under `items` inside an object property; the test reproduces that exact nesting (`properties.ranges.items.prefixItems`) rather than only the top-level case, so the recursive strip is what is being verified.
- Behavioural note for reviewers: a tuple-typed parameter is translated to a plain array whose `items` schema is either the sibling `items` the client sent or the `{ type: "string" }` default from #10578. That loses positional typing, but Gemini's schema subset cannot express it either way, and the previous behaviour was a hard 400 for the whole tool list.
- No stryker `tap.testFiles` change: `geminiHelper.ts` and `geminiToolsSanitizer.ts` are not in `stryker.conf.json`'s `mutate` list.

title: feat(backend): split test execution tiers to cut the 5k-file unit suite cost

labels.name: keep-open
labels.description: Ongoing community thread — exclude from stale auto-close

body:
## Problem

The test suite has grown to an inefficient scale that wastes build and test time locally and in CI:

- `tests/unit": 4,299 files; `tests/integration": 127 files; TypeScript under `tests/": ~5,036 files (CodeGraph index).
- 30+ `test:*` npm scripts across 4 runners (`node:test`, 2x Vitest configs, Playwright) plus shard/serial/live variants.
- Discovery globs in `test:unit`/`test:coverage:runner` enumerate the same large file sets repeatedly, so sharding, coverage, and local iteration all pay the full cost.

## Impact

- Long local iteration (`test:unit`, `test:coverage`) and CI shard fan-out for what should be fast unit feedback.
- High maintenance cost: naming/folder conventions drifted (`tests/unit/*` flat + 25+ subfolders + `dashboard/` + `serial/`), live/e2e/boundary tests mixed near unit tests.
- Coverage gate (60/60/60/60) runs over the whole set, amplifying the cost of every run.

## Proposal (audit + cleanup plan)

1. Audit: duplicate/overlapping suites (chatcore/combo/translator), dead or live-only tests hiding in unit paths, slowest files.
2. Consolidate: merge near-duplicate suites, move live/e2e/boundary out of unit globs, unify naming/folder rules.
3. Split execution tiers: fast unit (default) vs integration vs live/e2e, so `npm run test:unit` stays fast.
4. No coverage regression: keep 60/60/60/60 gate green; update baselines only on genuine improvement.

 Happy to take this on starting from `release/v3.8.51`.

title: fix(audio): resolve combo names on /v1/audio/translations
body:
## Summary

- `POST /v1/audio/translations` rejected combo names that `GET /v1/models` advertises. On the base, `src/app/api/v1/audio/translations/route.ts:68-77` hands the raw `model` string to `parseTranslationModel()` and returns `400 Invalid translation model: <combo>. Use format: provider/model` when it is not a `provider/model` id; nothing calls `getComboByName()` first. Every sibling already resolves combos: chat, embeddings, `/v1/audio/transcriptions` (#9134, fixed by #9382 at `src/app/api/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:183-212`), `/v1/audio/speech` and `/v1/videos/generations` (#10469, fixed by #10471). Translations was the one route those fixes did not cover, so the same combo name with the same file worked on `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and failed on `/v1/audio/translations`.
- Before: `model=traducao` (a `priority` combo over `localstt/whisper-1`) → `400 Invalid translation model: traducao. Use format: provider/model`, no upstream call. After: one upstream call to `http://localhost:9000/v1/audio/translations` whose multipart `model` is `whisper-1`; the response is the upstream body. Literal `provider/model` ids skip the lookup and unknown bare names keep the existing 400 and format hint.
- The change mirrors the transcriptions route exactly. The single-target body of `POST` moves unchanged into `translateWithModel(formData, modelStr, startTime)`; after `enforceApiKeyPolicy`, a bare name (no `/`) is looked up with `getComboByName()` and, when it is a combo, fanned out through `handleComboChat()` with one multipart copy per target (`withModel()` copies every field and replaces only `model`; the uploaded Blob is reused). Unknown bare names and literal ids fall through to `translateWithModel()` as before. No handler, registry, provider, schema or response-shape change.
- Deliberately out of scope: the alias-candidate credential fallback that transcriptions has (`audioModelAliasCandidates` / `findAlternateAudioProvider`) is not added here, since translations never had it and it is a separate behavior; `withModel()` and the combo block are duplicated from the transcriptions route rather than lifted into `_shared/`, to keep this diff mirror-shaped and reviewable against #9382 (a follow-up could factor both routes onto one helper).

## Related Issues

- Closes: no open issue for this route (open issues and PRs searched for `audio translations combo`; none found).
- Related to #9134 and #9382 (transcriptions), #10469 and #10471 (speech and videos), #5809 (the translations endpoint).

## Validation

Choose the change type and focused loop from the
[Contribution Golden Path](../docs/ops/CONTRIBUTION_GOLDEN_PATH.md). The full unit suite,
Vitest, the 60% coverage gate, and the production build all run in CI on this PR (#8329):

- [x] Change type: routing
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: `tests/unit/audio-translations-combo-resolution.test.ts` 3/3; neighbours `audio-transcriptions-combo-resolution`, `9134-repro-audio-combo-rejection`, `video-combo-route`, `audio-translations-route`, `audio-transcription-handler`, `audio-provider-nodes-selection`, `audio-speech-dynamic-node-9096`, `audio-alias-prefix-10586`, `audio-nested-model-credential-fallback` and `tests/unit/combo/*` 252/252; `node scripts/check/check-complexity-ratchets.mjs --base-ref origin/release/v3.8.51` OK (0 new violations); `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK; `npm run typecheck:core` exit 0; `eslint` and `prettier --check` on the two touched TypeScript files exit 0
- [ ] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base `release/v3.8.51`; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR
- SonarQube is temporarily opt-in while the private project has no quota; it is not a PR gate.

Red/green: with the base `route.ts` swapped in, the combo case fails with `400 Invalid translation model: traducao. Use format: provider/model` (actual 400, expected 200) and the other two cases pass; with the change all three pass.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/audio-translations-combo-resolution.test.ts` (new, 3 cases): creates a real `openai-compatible` provider node (`prefix: localstt`, `apiType: audio-transcriptions`) and a `priority` combo `traducao` in the test database, stubs `globalThis.fetch`, and asserts at the upstream sink. (2) `model=localstt/whisper-1` → dispatched directly, same URL, multipart `model=whisper-1`. (3) `model=definitely-not-a-combo-or-model` → 400 with `Invalid translation model`, zero upstream calls.

The `translateWithModel()` body is the previous `POST` body moved verbatim; its upstream dispatch is additionally covered by the existing `tests/unit/audio-translations-route.test.ts` (handler level).

title: feat(resilience): surface TLS-fingerprint remediation when Cloudflare 1010 hits
body:
Fixes #12529

## Summary

A Cloudflare `403` / `error_code 1010` rejection means the CDN banned the CLIENT's TLS/UA signature — not the account. #9929 already classifies this as `FINGERPRINT_REJECTION` so it no longer poisons account state, and the repo already ships the actual fix: a Chrome-124 TLS impersonation transport (`open-sse/utils/tlsClient.ts` via the optional `wreq-js` dependency). But the transport is off unless `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true`, the dependency is optional, and **nothing anywhere connects a 1010 to that fix** — operators see benign-classified 403s and the one-line remediation stays hidden.

This PR emits a **throttled (once-per-process) remediation hint** when a response is classified `FINGERPRINT_REJECTION` while `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT` is not enabled:

```
[errorClassifier] Cloudflare fingerprint rejection (1010 / browser-signature ban) detected.
Remediation: install the optional 'wreq-js' dependency and set ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true
(plus TLS_FINGERPRINT_PROVIDERS=<providers> to cover proxied egress) so egress presents a browser TLS fingerprint.
```

## Change

- `open-sse/services/errorClassifier.ts`: `maybeEmitFingerprintRemediationHint()` called in the fingerprint-rejection branch; module-level once-flag with `resetFingerprintRemediationHintForTest()` seam; hint suppressed entirely when the transport is enabled.
- `tests/unit/error-classifier.test.ts`: regression test pinning classify-unchanged, throttle-to-once, message contents (`wreq-js`, `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true`), and suppression when enabled.
- `tests/unit/12529-fingerprint-remediation-auth-path.test.ts`: regression on the **auth.ts consumer path** (maintainer request on #12529) — drives `markAccountUnavailable` end-to-end with a real Cloudflare-1010 403 and asserts the account stays active/non-terminal **and** the hint fires from that path.
- `changelog.d/fixes/12529-tls-fingerprint-remediation-hint.md`.

No classification, combo-routing, or account-state changes (#9929 behavior untouched). No new dependencies (wreq-js is already an optionalDependency).

## Testing

- `node --test` with the repo loader stack (`tsx/esm` + polyfills):
  - `tests/unit/error-classifier.test.ts` — **35/35 pass** (34 baseline + 1 new).
  - `tests/unit/12529-fingerprint-remediation-auth-path.test.ts` — **3/3 pass**: 1010 through `markAccountUnavailable` keeps the connection active/non-terminal (`banned`/`expired`/`credits_exhausted` all asserted against) **and** emits exactly one hint containing `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true` and `wreq-js`; repeated 1010s stay throttled to one emission; suppressed entirely when `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true`.
- Branch merged current `release/v3.8.51` (merge state was DIRTY; now MERGEABLE — includes upstream's #10725 Kiro IDC block in the same 403 region).

## Deployment evidence

On the affected production instance: enabling `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true` (wreq-js present since install) switched direct egress to the Chrome-124 fingerprint — verified via `tls.peet.ws/api/all`:

- wreq-js `chrome_124` session: `ja3_hash 24a38702f3a11cf1d1c52478881cb992` (browser UA, h2)
- Node default fetch: `ja3_hash d67b094811e5145139d7cea5f014309f`

1010 rejections stopped after enablement. For the Python-stack variant of this phenomenon (urllib flagged, curl passes), `curl_cffi`'s browser impersonation is the equivalent client-side fix — noted for completeness in #12529.

title: feat(resilience): surface the Cloudflare 1010 TLS-fingerprint remediation hint

labels.name: keep-open
labels.description: Ongoing community thread — exclude from stale auto-close

body:
## Context

Cloudflare-fronted upstreams (e.g. `opencode.ai/zen/v1`) intermittently reject OmniRoute's egress with `403` / `error_code 1010` ("access denied … based on your browser's signature") while `curl` on the same key and byte-identical body succeeds. #9929 correctly classified this as `FINGERPRINT_REJECTION` so it no longer poisons account state, and the repo already ships the actual fix: a **Chrome-124 TLS impersonation transport** (`open-sse/utils/tlsClient.ts`, via the optional `wreq-js` dependency — JA3/JA4 impersonation, sessions, cookie jars, per-account isolation).

## The gap

The transport is **effectively undiscoverable**:

- It is off unless `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true`.
- `wreq-js` is an *optional* dependency, so installs vary in whether it's even present.
- When a 1010 hits, nothing anywhere — logs, health, combo traces — connects the failure to the flag. Operators see repeated 403/1010 classified as a benign provider error (thanks to #9929) and move on; the one-line fix stays hidden.

Measured on a production instance (macOS, launchd, v3.8.51-era install): `wreq-js` was present since install, the flag was simply never set.

## Fingerprint proof

Through the transport (wreq-js `chrome_124` session) vs Node's default fetch, against `tls.peet.ws/api/all`:

```
wreq-js    -> ja3_hash 24a38702f3a11cf1d1c52478881cb992  (Chrome UA, h2)
node fetch -> ja3_hash d67b094811e5145139d7cea5f014309f  (undici default)
```

After enabling the flag on the affected instance, egress presents the browser fingerprint and the 1010s no longer occur (also consistent with #9929's curl-vs-urllib observation — the CDN classifies on TLS/UA signature, and Python `urllib` is likewise flagged; the Python-stack equivalent is `curl_cffi`'s browser impersonation).

## Proposed change (PR follows)

Emit a **throttled, once-per-process remediation hint** when a response is classified `FINGERPRINT_REJECTION` and `ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT` is not enabled:

```
[errorClassifier] Cloudflare fingerprint rejection (1010 / browser-signature ban) detected.
Remediation: install the optional 'wreq-js' dependency and set ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true
(plus TLS_FINGERPRINT_PROVIDERS=<providers> to cover proxied egress) so egress presents a browser TLS fingerprint.
```

- Zero behavior change when the transport is enabled (hint suppressed).
- No change to classification, combo routing, or account state (#9929 untouched).
- Ships with a regression test pinning throttle-once + suppression-when-enabled.

Related: #9929 (classification), #12274 (browser-grade fingerprints for the browser-pool surface — same root phenomenon, different executor).

title: fix(free-tiers): remove obsolete Together $25 signup credit from first-month budget
body:
### Problem / Use Case

At current default-branch commit `86e83d4138441c3c842c2a3bc5c20d1b06db41d1`, the free-tier summary still counts Together as a `$25` signup credit / approximately `25M` first-month tokens:

- `docs/reference/FREE_TIERS.md:19`
- `docs/reference/FREE_TIERS.md:44`
- provider summary row near `docs/reference/FREE_TIERS.md:220`
- README first-month headline is derived from the same catalog

That contradicts both current Together documentation and OmniRoute own completed #5470. Together now says it does not offer free trials and requires a minimum `$5` credit purchase for platform access. API keys are unavailable until that minimum funding exists.

Current sources:

- https://docs.together.ai/docs/billing-credits
- https://support.together.ai/articles/1862638756-changes-to-free-tier-and-billing-july-2025
- https://support.together.ai/articles/4999040689-where-to-find-your-api-key
- Prior OmniRoute correction: #5470

Together may list individual `$0.00` models, but those are not zero-deposit signup capacity when obtaining an API key requires funding. They must not preserve the `$25 signup credit` or inflate free-to-start token totals.

### Proposed Solution

- Remove the obsolete Together `$25` / `~25M` signup-credit allocation from the free-budget source data.
- Recompute the first-month headline and every generated surface from the canonical catalog.
- Classify Together as prepaid/billing-required. If zero-priced models remain discoverable, label them as requiring a funded account and keep them out of zero-deposit capacity totals.
- Add a regression assertion that a provider marked billing-required cannot contribute a signup-credit budget without a current explicit grant source.

### Acceptance Criteria

- No generated/current guide claims Together grants `$25` on signup.
- First-month budget is recomputed without that allocation.
- Together billing warning, provider metadata, free-tier catalog, and routing risk classification agree.
- Focused catalog/docs consistency tests pass.

### Expected Test Plan

Run the free-tier/catalog generators and their focused consistency/docs gates; assert Together contributes zero signup-credit tokens.

title: fix(docker): fix Bun variant build, SQLite runtime and process.execPath startup on main
body:
### Summary

Fixes multiple failure modes preventing the Docker Bun variant (`Dockerfile.bun`) from building and starting on `main`:

1. **`run-standalone.mjs` runtime resolution**: Replaced hardcoded `spawnWithForwardedSignals("node", [entry], ...)` with `process.execPath`. In `oven/bun:*-slim` containers, `node` is absent from PATH, causing an immediate startup crash (`spawn node ENOENT`).
2. **Runner base image version**: Bumped `runner-base` from `oven/bun:1.3.14-slim` to `oven/bun:1.4.0-slim` to match the `base` stage and latest Bun runtime.
3. **`better-sqlite3` native addon elimination for Bun**: Under Bun, OmniRoute uses the native `bun:sqlite` database driver. Stripped vendored `better-sqlite3` binaries from the runner image to prevent dlopen/NAPI crashes prior to driver fallback.
4. **Builder layer caching & smoke checks**: Added dependency layer caching prior to `bun install` and replaced fragile native rebuild steps with `wreq-js` binding verification and native `bun:sqlite` smoke checks.
5. **Security & permissions**: Enforced non-root `USER bun` execution with `chown -R bun:bun /app /app/data`.

### Tests & Validation

- `tests/unit/build/bun-runtime-native-addon.test.mjs`: Verifies `Dockerfile.bun` removes `better-sqlite3` native addons and excludes them from the runner.

title: fix(rerank): clamp Voyage top_k and honor NVIDIA return_documents
body:
## Summary

- Two rerank adapter defects in `open-sse/handlers/rerank.ts`, both on the current `release/v3.8.51` base:
  - **Voyage `top_k` exceeds the documents sent.** `handleRerank` normalizes `top_n: top_n || documents.length` from the caller's *unfiltered* array (`rerank.ts:237`) before the request adapter runs; the Voyage adapter then drops exact empty strings (`rerank.ts:80-82`) but still emits `top_k: body.top_n || docTexts.length` (`rerank.ts:87`), i.e. the unfiltered count. `POST /v1/rerank` with `documents: ["a", "", "b"]` and no `top_n` sends 2 documents with `top_k: 3`; Voyage rejects `top_k > documents.length` with HTTP 400 and the caller sees a gateway failure for a request that is valid under the Cohere-style contract this endpoint exposes. The same happens for an explicit `top_n` larger than the surviving count.
  - **NVIDIA ignores `return_documents: false`.** The NVIDIA response adapter always emits `document: { text }` (`rerank.ts:109`), while its deepinfra (`rerank.ts:121,128`) and voyage (`rerank.ts:147,163`) siblings gate the field on `options.return_documents !== false`, and the handler already passes `return_documents` into the adapter for every provider. Callers that opt out of document echo still get the full text back on NVIDIA.
- After: the Voyage request adapter clamps `top_k` to `Math.min(body.top_n || docTexts.length, docTexts.length)`, so a legitimate `top_n` below the count is untouched and only the impossible case is corrected; the NVIDIA response adapter gates `document` exactly like deepinfra and voyage. Default behavior (`return_documents` omitted or `true`) is unchanged.
- Out of scope: the `top_n || documents.length` default in the handler (it is correct for every other provider, which does not drop documents), Voyage's handling of whitespace-only documents (accepted and ranked upstream, see #7809), and any change to `index` remapping or score ordering.

## Related Issues

- Closes: none. No open issue tracks either defect (open issues searched for `rerank`, `voyage top_k`, `return_documents`).
- Related to #7809, #7811 (Voyage adapter: empty-string filtering and `top_k` mapping), #5332 (NVIDIA/deepinfra adapters and the `return_documents` gate on deepinfra)

## Validation

Choose the change type and focused loop from the
[Contribution Golden Path](../docs/ops/CONTRIBUTION_GOLDEN_PATH.md). The full unit suite,
Vitest, the 60% coverage gate, and the production build all run in CI on this PR (#8329):

- [x] Change type: provider (rerank request/response adapters in `open-sse/handlers/rerank.ts`)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: `tests/unit/rerank-*.test.ts` 46/46 (12 files, 3 suites); `npm run check:provider-consistency` OK; `npm run check:provider-assets` OK; `node scripts/check/check-complexity-ratchets.mjs --base-ref origin/release/v3.8.51` OK (new-code violations 0/0); `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK; `npm run typecheck:core` exit 0; `eslint` on the three touched files exit 0
- [ ] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base `release/v3.8.51` (rebased onto `86e83d413`, no conflicts); focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR
- SonarQube is temporarily opt-in while the private project has no quota; it is not a PR gate.

Red/green: with the base `rerank.ts` swapped in, the two touched test files report 25 pass / 3 fail — exactly the three new cases that encode the defects (`nvidia … return_documents=false`, `voyage … clamps top_k to the surviving document count`, `voyage … clamps an explicit oversized top_n`). With the change, 28/28.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/rerank-voyage-7809.test.ts` (+3 cases): `top_k` clamped to the surviving count when `top_n` mirrors the handler's unfiltered default (`["a", "", "b"]`, `top_n: 3` → `documents: ["a", "b"]`, `top_k: 2`); an explicit oversized `top_n: 10` with two empty strings is clamped to 2; a legitimate `top_n: 2` over three non-empty documents stays 2.
- `tests/unit/rerank-providers-5332.test.ts` (+3 cases): NVIDIA omits `document` when `return_documents: false` while keeping `index` and `relevance_score`; includes `document.text` when `return_documents: true`; includes it when `return_documents` is omitted (default preserved).
- `changelog.d/fixes/PENDING-rerank-topk-and-return-documents.md`: changelog fragment; the `PENDING` prefix will be replaced with this PR's number.

## Coverage Notes

- `open-sse/handlers/rerank.ts`: the Voyage `top_k` expression is exercised by the three new `transformRequestForProvider` cases (clamped, clamped from explicit oversized, not clamped); the NVIDIA `returnDocuments` branch is exercised in both directions plus the omitted-option default by the three new `transformResponseFromProvider` cases. Existing cases in both files (empty-string filtering, index remapping, sorting, `top_n` honoring, deepinfra gate) are unchanged and green.
- No touched file lost coverage; the change adds one branch per adapter and both branches of each are covered.

## Reviewer Notes

- Both changes are confined to the two provider-specific adapters; no shared handler path, endpoint, registry, or other provider changes.
- The clamp uses `Math.min` on the already-computed value rather than moving the `top_n` default into the adapter, so the handler's normalization (and the `top_n` logged in `saveCallLog`) is untouched; only the value sent to Voyage changes.
- The NVIDIA gate follows the sibling adapters verbatim (`options.return_documents !== false`), so a missing option keeps today's behavior of returning the text.
- No live call against Voyage or NVIDIA was made for this PR; the 400 is documented Voyage behavior for `top_k > len(documents)` and the tests assert the request payload shape rather than the provider response.

title: feat(gamification): pay the documented streak and badge XP rewards
body:
## Summary

- `XP_REWARDS` (`src/lib/gamification/xp.ts:155-158`) documents `streak_bonus` ("per consecutive streak day, multiplied by streak length") and `badge_unlock`, but the award pipeline never paid either: `events.ts` kept a private reward table without them (`getXpForAction`), `updateStreak()` did not report whether the streak had just extended, and `checkAndUnlockBadge()` unlocked badges with no XP.
- Every request that extends a daily streak now pays `streak_bonus × streak length` once per UTC day; every badge unlocked through the pipeline pays `badge_unlock` once per badge. Bonus XP goes through the same `addXp` + level sync + global/weekly/monthly leaderboard path as action XP, so level-ups and rankings include it.
- Idempotency: `advanceStreak()` reports `extended` only on the call that moves the record to today, and a same-day `xp_audit_log` check is evaluated and inserted synchronously; `unlockBadge()` now returns whether it inserted the `(api_key_id, badge_id)` row, and XP is paid only then. Restarts and duplicate events cannot double-pay.
- The Radar supporter recognition unlock stays XP-free, as its comment requires. No other scoring changes; `getXpForAction`, badge thresholds and `evaluateBadges()` are untouched. Amounts follow `XP_REWARDS` (2 × streak, 10 per badge). The docs table (`docs/frameworks/GAMIFICATION.md:239-252`) names different rewards and amounts; that is tracked separately in #12501, and which table is authoritative is the maintainer's call. If the docs values win, the two constants in `XP_REWARDS` are the only place that changes: the award path introduced here reads them and nothing else. Deliberately out of scope: wiring `evaluateBadges()` (no callers; it would change which badges unlock and needs `badge_definitions` seeded at startup), retroactive bonus for streaks already in progress, paying on day 1 of a streak. Step 1 of `emitGamificationEvent` is unchanged, so #12390's rate-limit gate applies cleanly; extending it to bonus XP is a one-line follow-up in `awardBonusXp` once it lands.

title: feat(claude): auto-register OmniRoute's MCP server in Claude Desktop's config
body:
## Context

Split out of **#11638** ("auto-detect Claude Desktop / Claude CoWork in code-tools integration").

That issue bundled two asks that turned out to have very different feasibility:

1. **Register OmniRoute's MCP server in Claude Desktop** — implementable today. *This issue.*
2. **Route Claude Desktop's LLM traffic through OmniRoute** — blocked. Anthropic's *Third-Party Inference Gateway* is a real GA feature, but per the documented flow the setting is GUI-menu-driven (Developer → Configure Third-Party Inference) with no confirmed writable config file, so it does not fit the file-write auto-apply pattern. That half stays in #11638 pending confirmation of whether the setting persists to a file on disk.

Splitting so the shippable half stops being blocked by the unresolved one.

## Problem

Connecting Claude Desktop to OmniRoute's MCP server is a **manual, copy-paste-a-JSON-blob** step today. `open-sse/mcp-server/README.md:58` documents it:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "omniroute": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["path/to/omniroute/open-sse/mcp-server/server.ts"],
      "env": {
        "OMNIROUTE_BASE_URL": "http://localhost:20128",
        "OMNIROUTE_API_KEY": "your-key"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Note the `path/to/omniroute` and `your-key` placeholders — the user has to resolve the install path and mint an API key by hand, which is exactly the friction the CLI-tools auto-apply flow already removes for every other client.

A repo-wide search confirms this is net-new: `claude_desktop_config.json` appears **only** in that README, never in code.

## Proposed solution

Add Claude Desktop as a target in the existing CLI-tools detect/apply framework — the same shape as the ~25 per-tool settings routes already under `src/app/api/cli-tools/` (`claude-settings/`, `codex-settings/`, `cline-settings/`, …):

1. **Detect** the Claude Desktop install and locate `claude_desktop_config.json` per platform:
   - macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
   - Windows: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`
   - Linux: `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
2. **Apply**: merge an `mcpServers.omniroute` entry into the existing JSON — **merge, never overwrite**; the file commonly holds other users' MCP servers.
3. Resolve `args` (the real server path for this install) and `env` (base URL + a generated API key) automatically, instead of leaving placeholders.
4. Back up the file before writing, reusing the existing `cli-tools/backups/` mechanism.
5. Surface it in the dashboard's code-tools UI like the other targets, including a "remove" path that deletes only our entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Claude Desktop is detected on macOS, Windows and Linux (and reports "not installed" cleanly when absent).
- [ ] Applying writes a valid `mcpServers.omniroute` entry with real resolved values — no `path/to/...` or `your-key` placeholders.
- [ ] An existing `claude_desktop_config.json` with other MCP servers keeps them all; only `mcpServers.omniroute` is added or updated.
- [ ] A malformed/unparseable config fails closed with a clear error and does not truncate the user's file.
- [ ] Removing the integration deletes only our entry.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: merge-into-existing, first-time-create, malformed input, and per-platform path resolution.

## Out of scope

Routing Claude Desktop's LLM traffic through OmniRoute — tracked in #11638.

Refs #11638

title: fix(providers): devin-cli spawn error leaves SSE controller closed twice → uncaughtException
body:
### OmniRoute Version

3.8.50

### Installation Method

npm (global)

### Operating System

Linux

### OS Version

Ubuntu 26.04 (Oracle), kernel 6.17.0-1020-oracle, aarch64

### Node.js Version

v24.16.0

### Provider(s) Involved

- devin-cli
- antigravity
- openrouter
- nvidia

### Model(s) Involved

- `devin-cli/claude-sonnet-5` / `claude-sonnet-5-xhigh`
- `antigravity/claude-opus-4-6-thinking`
- `openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6:batch`
- `nvidia/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro-0813`

### Client Tool

Devin CLI / API consumer using `/v1/chat/completions` with `auto/best-coding` combo

### Description

The `omniroute` process repeatedly throws an `uncaughtException` with the message `Invalid state: Controller is already closed` from `ReadableStreamDefaultController.enqueue`. The crash appears to happen when a child-process-backed provider (notably `devin-cli`) exits or errors while the response `ReadableStream` is still being consumed, and something attempts to `enqueue` into a controller that has already been closed.

In the current log sample, the same error occurred **10 times** in a single day and surfaced as **5 uncaughtExceptions**.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a combo that includes `devin-cli` models (e.g. `auto/best-coding`).
2. Ensure the `devin` binary is **not** in `$PATH` (or `CLI_DEVIN_BIN` is unset).
3. Send a streaming chat-completion request that routes through `devin-cli` first.
4. Wait for `devin-cli` to fail with `502 Stream ended before producing a non-ping SSE event: Devin CLI not found: devin`.
5. Observe the fallback chain advance to `antigravity`, `openrouter`, etc.
6. During this transition, `omniroute` emits the `Invalid state: Controller is already closed` uncaughtException.

### Expected Behavior

- A failing provider/child process should not leave the shared response stream in an invalid state.
- The controller should be closed exactly once, and any late `enqueue` attempts should be guarded.
- The process should not emit `uncaughtException` for a recoverable provider error.

### Actual Behavior

The following `uncaughtException` is written to `logs/application/app.log`:

```
Invalid state: Controller is already closed
TypeError: Invalid state: Controller is already closed
    at ReadableStreamDefaultController.enqueue (node:internal/webstreams/readablestream:1105:13)
    at o (/home/ubuntu/.nvm/versions/node/v24.16.0/lib/node_modules/omniroute/dist/.build/next/server/chunks/_0o8_5h8._.js:144:499)
    at B (/home/ubuntu/.nvm/versions/node/v24.16.0/lib/node_modules/omniroute/dist/.build/next/server/chunks/_0o8_5h8._.js:148:4)
    at ChildProcess.<anonymous> (/home/ubuntu/.nvm/versions/node/v24.16.0/lib/node_modules/omniroute/dist/.build/next/server/chunks/_0o8_5h8._.js:162:257)
    at ChildProcess.emit (node:events:509:28)
    at maybeClose (node:internal/child_process:1124:16)
    at Socket.<anonymous> (node:internal/child_process:481:11)
    at Socket.emit (node:events:509:28)
    at Pipe.<anonymous> (node:net:350:12)
```

This is followed by provider-specific errors (e.g. `Antigravity upstream error (400)`, `openrouter 404 Batch API only`), streams being aborted (`request_signal_aborted`, `hedge-cancelled`), and the combo eventually returning a `200` with no content to the client.

### Test Impact

Needs a new integration test

### Error Logs / Output

```shell
# Number of occurrences in the current application log
grep -c "Invalid state: Controller is already closed" logs/application/app.log
# => 10

grep -c "⨯ uncaughtException" logs/application/app.log
# => 5

grep -c "Devin CLI not found" logs/application/app.log
# => 33
```

Relevant surrounding log excerpt (timestamps UTC, 2026-09-02):

```
20:40:12.654  STREAM     Stream ended before producing a non-ping SSE event: Devin CLI not found: devin. (devin-cli/claude-sonnet-5-medium)
20:40:12.670  COMBO      Provider devin-cli connection 67d5f222-... error (502) — marking for skip on remaining targets (#1731v2)
20:40:12.678  COMBO      Trying model 9/3659: antigravity/claude-opus-4-6-thinking
20:40:12.813  app        ERROR Invalid state: Controller is already closed ...
20:40:12.815  app        uncaughtException:  Invalid state: Controller is already closed ...
20:40:13.102  app        [ERROR] [400]: Antigravity upstream error (400)
20:40:13.109  ProxyEgress antigravity status=error
20:40:18.728  [STREAM] ANTIGRAVITY | ... | disconnect: request_signal_aborted
20:40:18.729  [STREAM] NVIDIA | ... | disconnect: hedge-cancelled
20:40:18.748  ProxyEgress nvidia status=error
20:40:18.751  COMBO      combo trace ... terminal={"status":200,"errorClass":null} decisions=3659
```

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional Context

- The stack trace shows the exception originates from a `ChildProcess` `Socket`/`Pipe` callback writing to a `ReadableStreamDefaultController`.
- This pattern is strongly associated with `devin-cli` failing to spawn because the `devin` binary is missing, but it may affect any child-process provider that exits while the stream is still alive.
- The process itself does not die (the parent `omniroute v16.3.1` is still running), but the current request is corrupted and `uncaughtException` handlers may leave the runtime in an inconsistent state.

### Validation Plan

- Add an integration test that:
  1. Configures a combo where the first provider is a mock child-process that exits immediately with a non-zero code.
  2. Verifies the response `ReadableStream` is closed cleanly and only once.
  3. Asserts no `uncaughtException` is emitted and the request falls back to the next provider successfully.
- Manual regression:
  - `grep -c "uncaughtException" logs/application/app.log` should be `0` after a `devin-cli`-free request cycle.

title: fix(providers): strip prefixItems from Gemini tool schemas to avoid upstream 400
body:
### OmniRoute Version

3.8.50

### Installation Method

Docker / Docker Compose

### Operating System

Linux

### OS Version

ubuntu 26.04 

### Node.js Version

_No response_

### Provider(s) Involved

 Gemini (Google AI Studio)

### Model(s) Involved

gemini/gemini-3.6-flash

### Client Tool

Claude COde 

### Description

Any Claude Code request that includes tool definitions fails with a 400 when routed through OmniRoute to a Gemini model, because one of Claude Code's built-in tool schemas uses the JSON-Schema-2020-12 keyword `prefixItems` (for a tuple-typed array parameter, e.g. a `[start_line, end_line]` range). Gemini's function-calling schema is a restricted OpenAPI-3.0-style subset and doesn't recognize `prefixItems`, so the entire tool list is rejected before any generation happens. Non-tool requests (plain chat) through the same route work fine — this is isolated to the tool-schema translation path.

This is the same class of bug fixed in #1421 (`additionalProperties` stripped from Gemini tool schemas). That fix's strip-list already covers `additionalProperties`, `$schema`, `const`, `default`, `not` — `prefixItems` just isn't included yet.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to an OmniRoute instance, model = any Gemini model (reproduced on `gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview`, `gemini/gemini-3.6-flash`, `gemini/gemini-3.1-pro-preview`)
2. Connect Claude Code CLI to that endpoint (Anthropic Messages compatibility mode)
3. Start a session and send any prompt that triggers a built-in tool call (even a plain "hi" that leads Claude Code to read a file or list a directory is enough)
4. Request fails immediately with a 400, before any tokens are generated

### Expected Behavior

The Gemini tool-schema sanitizer strips `prefixItems` the same way it already strips `additionalProperties`/`$schema`/`const`/`default`/`not`, and the request reaches Gemini successfully with tool calling intact.


### Actual Behavior

Request is rejected outright:

> API Error: 400 Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "prefixItems" at
> 'tools[0].function_declarations[1].parameters.properties[5].value.properties[0].value.items':
> Cannot find field.

No tool call can succeed through this provider/client combination until the field is stripped upstream of Gemini.

title: fix: escape raw <name> tag in OMNIROUTE_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES description across 43 locales
body:
## Summary
The Feature Flags card for `OMNIROUTE_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES` (Settings → Feature Flags) renders the **raw key name** instead of its description on the live app. Root cause: the description contains a literal path placeholder with a raw `<name>` tag that next-intl parses as an unknown rich-text tag.

Reported from fork `chirag127`, branch `release/v3.8.51` @ `073b98462` (fully synced with upstream). Windows 11, Node 24, Turbopack dev mode.

## Symptom
- On `/dashboard/settings/feature-flags`, the `OMNIROUTE_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES` card shows `featureFlags.definitions.OMNIROUTE_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES.description` (raw key fallback) instead of the description.
- Depending on context, next-intl throws `INVALID_MESSAGE: INVALID_TAG` in the console.

## Root cause
All 43 locale files (`src/i18n/messages/*.json`) contain the invalid value under `featureFlags.definitions.OMNIROUTE_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES.description`:

```json
"description": "After provider-model synchronization, regenerate ~/.claude/profiles/<name>/settings.json profiles from the live catalog. This never changes the active or default Claude configuration and is off by default."
```

The Feature Flags page renders descriptions via plain `t()` (`src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/settings/components/FeatureFlagsGrid.tsx:422-428`):

```tsx
description: t.has(`definitions.${flag.key}.description`)
  ? t(`definitions.${flag.key}.description`)
  : flag.description,
```

`<name>` is parsed as a rich-text tag, but no tag element is ever passed — the message fails to compile and the card falls back to the raw key. The same class of bug as #12302 (`ccOnboardingKeyPlaceholder`).

Note: the TS default in `src/shared/constants/featureFlagDefinitions.ts:611` (`description: "...~/.claude/profiles/<name>/settings.json..."`) has the same raw tag; the locale value overrides it, so the locale is what renders.

## Verified fix (single-quote escaping)
Wrap the placeholder in ICU single quotes so it renders literally:

```json
"description": "After provider-model synchronization, regenerate ~/.claude/profiles/'<name>'/settings.json profiles from the live catalog. This never changes the active or default Claude configuration and is off by default."
```

Verified through `intl-messageformat` (the exact parser next-intl uses): `'<name>'` → literal `<name>`, no error. Applied to all 43 locale files; the live page now renders the full description and the console is clean. Escaping via `<`/`>` is NOT acceptable here — the value is a real file path shown to the user (`~/.claude/profiles/<name>/settings.json`), so literal angle brackets must render.

## Suggested follow-ups
1. Apply the same escaping to the TS default in `featureFlagDefinitions.ts` for consistency.
2. Add a CI check that parses every locale file with `intl-messageformat` so a raw `<tag>` in a message rendered by plain `t()` fails the build instead of silently breaking pages.

title: fix(api): thread X-OmniRoute-Fallback-Attempts through chat completions (#12339)
body:
## Problem

As reported in #12339 by @diegosouzapw:

On `/v1/chat/completions` responses (both streaming `stream: true` and non-streaming `stream: false`), the `X-OmniRoute-Fallback-Attempts` HTTP header is absent (or defaults to `0`), even when a combo failover to a non-primary target occurred before the stream/response opened.

While `X-OmniRoute-Provider` and `X-OmniRoute-Model` update correctly to the winning provider, the fallback attempts counter was completely missing from chat responses.

## Root Cause

1. **Missing parameter in response-header builders:** Both `assembleStreamingResponseHeaders` and `buildNonStreamingResponseHeaders` built metadata headers without accepting or passing `fallbackAttempts` into `buildStreamingResponseHeaders` / `attachOmniRouteMetaHeaders`.

2. **Missing forwarding in `chatCore.ts`:** `handleChatCore` did not accept `fallbackAttempts` or pass it to either header builder.

3. **Dropped in the dispatch chain:** While `open-sse/services/combo.ts` properly calculates `fallbackCount`, it was not passed through `handleSingleModel` (`chat.ts`), `executeChatWithBreaker` (`chatHelpers.ts`), or `dispatchChatWithAffinityEviction`.

## Fix

### 1. Response Header Builders

- **`open-sse/handlers/chatCore/nonStreamingResponseHeaders.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts?: number` to the `args` type.
  - Forwarded `fallbackAttempts: args.fallbackAttempts` to `deps.attachOmniRouteMetaHeaders`.

- **`open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingResponseHeaders.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts?: number` to the `args` type.
  - Forwarded `fallbackAttempts: args.fallbackAttempts` to `buildStreamingResponseHeaders`.

### 2. Core Handler & Dispatch Chain

- **`open-sse/handlers/chatCore.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts = 0` to `handleChatCore` parameters.
  - Forwarded `fallbackAttempts` to `buildNonStreamingResponseHeaders` and `assembleStreamingResponseHeaders`.

- **`src/sse/handlers/chatHelpers.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts = 0` to `executeChatWithBreaker` options.
  - Forwarded `fallbackAttempts` into `handleChatCore`.

- **`src/sse/handlers/chat.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts?: number` to the `target` type in `handleSingleModel`.
  - Forwarded `fallbackAttempts: target?.fallbackAttempts ?? 0` into `handleSingleModelChat`.
  - Added `fallbackAttempts?: number` to the `runtimeOptions` type in `handleSingleModelChat`.
  - Forwarded `fallbackAttempts: runtimeOptions?.fallbackAttempts ?? 0` into `dispatchChatWithAffinityEviction`.

### 3. Combo Layer

- **`open-sse/services/combo.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts: fallbackCount` when dispatching targets in `handleComboChatInner` (`handleSingleModelWithTimeout`).
  - Added `fallbackAttempts: fallbackCount` when dispatching targets in `handleRoundRobinCombo` (`handleSingleModel`).

- **`open-sse/services/combo/types.ts`**
  - Added `fallbackAttempts?: number` to the `SingleModelTarget` type definition.

### 4. Changelog

- Added `changelog.d/fixes/12339-fallback-attempts-chat-completions.md`.

## Tests Added
