title: fix(command-code): floor tiny muse-spark output budgets so hidden reasoning cannot consume the whole budget
body:
## Summary

- muse-spark (Meta) models routed through **command-code** burn their entire output budget on invisible server-side reasoning before emitting any visible content. With a small
caller-set `max_tokens` (e.g. 64) the upstream answers HTTP 200 with **null content** (`out=64, reasoning=61`) — the client receives an empty assistant turn and OmniRoute flags the
fake success as "Provider returned empty content". This is the reproduction in **#12130**.
- Fix: reuse the already prefix-aware `MUSE_SPARK_PATTERN` (`/(?:^|\/|\b)muse-spark/i`) to detect muse-spark ids — **including provider-prefixed forms**
(`meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor`, `cmd/meta/muse-…`) that a bare `startsWith("muse-spark")` would miss — and floor a tiny caller budget to `MUSE_SPARK_MIN_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 512` so
the hidden reasoning phase can never consume the whole budget.
- Applied in **both** command-code body builders: `buildOpenAiBody` (the `/provider/v1/chat/completions` path that the reproduction goes through) and `buildCommandCodeCliBody` (the
`/alpha/generate` 403/404 fallback), mirroring the existing `applyMuseSparkMinOutputTokens` behavior already shipped for the opencode-go executor.

## Related Issues

- Related to #12130 (OpenAI API returns null content when model output consists of reasoning tokens, e.g. `command-code/meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor`) — the exact `out=64,
reasoning=61, content:null` reproduction this fix targets.
- Related to #11214 (muse-spark output budget is floored so it stops returning empty-content responses) — same empty-content-on-small-budget class; previously applied only to
opencode-go, now extended to command-code.
- Related to #10986 (original reasoning-only `content:null` report) — this fix paves the `/provider/v1` path so the budget-floor mitigation prevents the empty-content condition
rather than relying on a downstream fallback.

## Validation

- [x] Change type: provider / routing
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path

  `node --test tests/unit/command-code-executor.test.ts` → 20/20 pass
  `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.typecheck-core.json` → clean
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (`release/v3.8.51`); focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/command-code-executor.test.ts` — 2 new cases:
  - `meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor` + `max_tokens: 64` → raised to `512` (the #12130 bug path)
  - large budget (`4096`) left untouched (no over-flooring)

> The existing `tests/unit/opencode-muse-spark-min-output.test.ts` (11/11 pass) confirms the opencode-go executor is **untouched** — only command-code was modified.

## Coverage Notes

- `open-sse/executors/commandCode.ts` is covered by the two new tests above, exercising `applyMuseSparkMinOutputTokens` on both the floor and no-op paths (bare + prefixed id
detection).
- Full `npm run test:coverage` (global 60% gate) was attempted; the c8 `--merge-async` run stalled into an 8GB `coverage/tmp` on this Windows workstation, so the per-change gates
above (scoped tests + typecheck) were used as the focused loop. The global 60% gate runs in CI on the PR (#8329).

## Reviewer Notes

- Detection now uses the prefix-aware `MUSE_SPARK_PATTERN`. For command-code this is a **superset** of any prior bare-prefix check — no model is exempted, only newly covered (e.g.
the `meta/…` id in this reproduction).
- This PR is the **budget-floor prevention** approach: it stops the empty-content condition for small caller budgets. It does **not** add a reasoning→content fallback inside the
`/provider/v1` raw passthrough for the case where a model emits reasoning-only with a *large* budget — that remains the domain of #10986's fallback (already present on the
`/alpha/generate` path). Maintainer's note in #12130 confirms `/provider/v1` currently returns the upstream `Response` unmodified; if we also want a downstream reasoning→content
fallback there, that is a deliberate follow-up.
- No new dependency, feature flag, DB migration, or manual validation required.

title: fix(devin): treat Devin CLI model ids as literal — never strip or synthesize effort suffixes
body:
## Problem

The Devin CLI providers (`devin-cli`, `devin-cli-agentic`, `devin-desktop`; aliases `dv`/`dva`) serve a catalog whose model ids **embed the reasoning tier**: `claude-opus-5-low`, `claude-opus-5-medium`, … and `gpt-5-6-sol-max`/`-low` are distinct upstream models (see `open-sse/config/providers/registry/devin/catalog.ts`).

Two cross-cutting mechanisms assume a trailing `-{effort}` suffix is a client-side variant, and both corrupt Devin ids:

**1. Dispatch-time strip (`applyClaudeEffortVariant`)** strips the suffix from any id whose base is a known Claude model — correct for the `claude`/`cc` lanes, wrong for Devin. Live evidence from a self-hosted v3.8.51 deployment:

```
POST /v1/chat/completions  model: dva/claude-opus-5-low
→ 400 { "Model is not present in the current Devin catalog: claude-opus-5" }
```

The executor (`assertKnownDevinModel`) rejects the stripped base because upstream has one id **per tier**. Only accidental double-suffixed ids survived (`dva/claude-opus-5-max-low` → strip `-low` → real `claude-opus-5-max`), which made failures look random: `claude-opus-5-low`/`-medium`/`-high`/`-xhigh`/`-max` and the whole `claude-sonnet-5-*` family 400, while `claude-5-fable-*` (a name the static registry doesn't know) worked.

**2. Catalog variant synthesis** advertised phantom ids on top of tier-embedded ids (`dva/gpt-5-6-sol-max-low`, `dva/kimi-k3-*`) that 400 when called.

## Fix

Three gates treat Devin ids as literal, keyed off a single helper (`isDevinLiteralModelIdProvider` — ids + aliases + `provider/model`-qualified prefixes):

- `applyClaudeEffortVariant`: early return for Devin providers — no strip, no `reasoning_effort` mutation.
- `shouldExposeClaudeEffortVariants` (`appendClaudeEffortVariants`): no `-<level>` variants for devin-prefixed ids.
- `isSkippedEffortProvider` (`appendSyncedEffortVariants`): Devin providers join codex/glm/kimi as providers that own their own suffix mechanism — the tier IS the id.

## What does NOT change

- `claude`/`cc` lane stripping (`cc/claude-opus-5-high` → `claude-opus-5` + `reasoning_effort=high`) — untouched, covered by existing + new control tests.
- Non-Devin variant synthesis (OpenCode-style catalog-only clients keep getting `<model>-<level>` ids for Anthropic-served models).

## Tests

- `tests/unit/devin-literal-effort-ids.test.ts` (new): helper matching, both catalog appenders skip Devin entries, `isSkippedEffortProvider` coverage.
- `tests/unit/chatcore-claude-effort-variant.test.ts`: four new cases — devin-cli-agentic keeps `claude-opus-5-low` literal, alias `dva` covered, devin-cli/devin-desktop/`dv` covered, claude-lane control still strips.

## Live validation

Self-hosted v3.8.51 native deployment (before → after): `dva/claude-opus-5-low` 400 → 200, `dva/claude-5-fable-low` unaffected (200 → 200), `dva/swe-1-7` unaffected, phantom variant ids disappear from `/v1/models`, `cc/claude-opus-5-high` routing unchanged.

Note for reviewers: ids like `dva/claude-opus-5-max-low` that previously "worked" by accident will now (correctly) 400 — callers should use the real tier ids (`dva/claude-opus-5-max`, `dva/claude-opus-5-low`, …), which this PR makes selectable in catalog-only clients for the first time.

title: fix(docker): standalone bundle omits @wreq-js native binding, breaking Codex app-server WebSocket

body:
### OmniRoute Version

3.8.51

### Installation Method

Docker / Docker Compose

### Operating System

Linux

### OS Version

Debian 13 with Dokploy

### Node.js Version

_No response_

### Provider(s) Involved

Codex App Server

### Model(s) Involved

cxa/gpt-5.6-luna -> codex-app-server/gpt-5.6-luna

### Client Tool

Codex CLI

### Description

Connecting a containerized `codex-app-server` to OmniRoute via WebSocket fails immediately with `Codex app-server websocket transport unavailable.`
The root cause is that wreq-js fails to load inside the Next.js standalone Docker runtime `([TlsClient] wreq-js unavailable; TLS fingerprint transport disabled)`. The dynamic `createRequire(import.meta.url)` in `open-sse/utils/tlsClient.ts` throws an error inside the compiled .next/standalone environment, swallowing the exception and hard-nulling `this.websocketFn`.
This module resolution failure persists even if the native `@wreq-js/binding-linux-x64-gnu` binary is manually injected into the container with correct node user permissions, pre-loaded via `NODE_OPTIONS=--require`, or entirely polyfilled with the standard ws library. The Next.js standalone tracer seems to aggressively isolate or mangle the dynamic require path, very similar to the tsx issue described in #12152 .

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy `diegosouzapw/omniroute:next` (or v3.8.50) via Docker Compose.
2. Deploy a secondary `ghcr.io/icoretech/codex-docker:latest` container exposing port 1456.
3. Configure OmniRoute with `OMNIROUTE_CODEX_APPSERVER_WS=ws://codex-app-server:1456` and the associated token file.
4. Start the stack and observe the immediate `[TlsClient] wreq-js unavailable warning` in the OmniRoute logs.
5. Send a chat completion request to a Codex App Server model (e.g., cxa/gpt-5.6-luna).
6. The request instantly fails with a 502 WebSocket transport unavailable error.

### Expected Behavior

OmniRoute successfully loads the WebSocket transport and establishes a JSON-RPC connection to the local app-server. Alternatively, since the local app-server explicitly ignores TLS fingerprinting (as noted in `appServerClient.ts`), it should safely fall back to the native Node `ws` library rather than strictly requiring `wreq-js`.

### Actual Behavior

Next.js fails to resolve `wreq-js` dynamically, disabling the WebSocket factory globally. Routing requests to the app-server instantly throws: `[STREAM] CODEX-APP-SERVER | gpt-5.6-luna | 88ms | error: Codex app-server websocket transport unavailable`.

### Test Impact

Needs a new integration test

### Error Logs / Output

```shell
▲ Next.js 16.3.2
- Local:         http://localhost:20128
- Network:       http://0.0.0.0:20128
✓ Ready in 0ms
✓ Running next.config took 3ms
[TlsClient] wreq-js unavailable; TLS fingerprint transport disabled
...
{"level":30,"time":"2026-09-01T18:50:59.743Z","service":"omniroute","module":"sse","tag":"HTTP","method":"POST","path":"/v1/chat/completions | cxa/gpt-5.6-luna | 1 msgs","msg":"📥 POST /v1/chat/completions | cxa/gpt-5.6-luna | 1 msgs"}
{"level":30,"time":"2026-09-01T18:50:59.797Z","service":"omniroute","module":"sse","tag":"ROUTING","msg":"cxa/gpt-5.6-luna → codex-app-server/gpt-5.6-luna"}
{"level":30,"time":"2026-09-01T18:50:59.812Z","service":"omniroute","module":"sse","tag":"AUTH","msg":"Using codex-app-server account: ***..."}
[18:50:59] 🌊 [STREAM] CODEX-APP-SERVER | gpt-5.6-luna | 88ms | error: Codex app-server websocket transport unavailable
{"level":40,"time":"2026-09-01T18:51:00.024Z","service":"omniroute","module":"sse","tag":"AUTH","msg":"[T-PROBE] noauth codex-app-server failure 502 recorded — connection stays in the pool"}
```

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional Context

Troubleshooting confirmed the native `wreq-js` binding works flawlessly at the OS/Node level inside the container (`node -e "console.log(require('wreq-js'))"` succeeds when mounted with correct UID 1000 ownership). The failure is strictly isolated to Next.js's standalone execution context swallowing the dynamic require. Since `wreq-js` is an optional dependency, it likely needs to be explicitly added to `EXTRA_MODULE_ENTRIES` or `experimental.serverComponentsExternalPackages` in the Next.js build pipeline so the tracer preserves it.

Compose 1:
```yaml
services:
  omniroute:
    image: diegosouzapw/omniroute:next
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      codex-app-server:
        condition: service_started
    stop_grace_period: 40s
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "healthcheck.mjs"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 15s
    ports:
      - 20128:20128
      - 20129:20129
    environment:
      - NODE_ENV=production
      - RUST_LOG=${CODEX_APPSERVER_RUST_LOG:-info}
      - PORT=${PORT:-20128}
      - DASHBOARD_PORT=${DASHBOARD_PORT:-${PORT:-20128}}
      - API_PORT=${API_PORT:-20129}
      - API_HOST=${API_HOST:-0.0.0.0}
      - HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0
      - DATA_DIR=/app/data
      - PATH=/home/node/.local/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
      # --- Enable wreq-js Native WebSocket/TLS Transport ---
      - ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true
      - ENABLE_SOCKS5_PROXY=true
      # --- App Server Connection ---
      - OMNIROUTE_CODEX_APPSERVER_WS=ws://codex-app-server:1456
      - OMNIROUTE_CODEX_APPSERVER_WS_TOKEN_FILE=/run/codex-appserver/token
    volumes:
      - omniroute-data:/app/data
      - codex-appserver-token:/run/codex-appserver

  codex-app-server:
    image: ghcr.io/icoretech/codex-docker:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "1456:1456"
    environment:
      - CODEX_HOME=/home/codex/.codex
      - RUST_LOG=${CODEX_APPSERVER_RUST_LOG:-debug}
    pre_start:
      - image: busybox
        user: root
        command: sh -c 'if [ ! -f /run/codex-appserver/token ]; then tr -dc A-Za-z0-9 </dev/urandom | head -c 32 > /run/codex-appserver/token; fi'

      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

volumes:
  omniroute-data:
  codex-appserver-token:
  codex-appserver-home:
```

Compose 2 - `wreq-js` injection:
```yaml
services:
  omniroute-init:
    image: node:22-slim
    command: >
      sh -c "mkdir -p /polyfill &&
      echo \"const WebSocket = require('ws');
      module.exports = {
        createSession: async () => ({ fetch: async () => ({ status: 200, headers: new Map(), body: null }), close: () => {} }),
        websocket: async (url, opts) => new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
          const ws = new WebSocket(url, { headers: opts.headers });
          const wrapper = { send: (d) => ws.send(d), close: (c, r) => ws.close(c, r), onmessage: null, onerror: null, onclose: null };
          ws.on('message', (d) => wrapper.onmessage && wrapper.onmessage({ data: d.toString() }));

    volumes:

  omniroute:
    image: diegosouzapw/omniroute:next

        condition: service_completed_successfully
    stop_grace_period: 40s
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "healthcheck.mjs"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 15s
    ports:
      - 20128:20128
      - 20129:20129
    environment:
      - NODE_ENV=production
      - RUST_LOG=${CODEX_APPSERVER_RUST_LOG:-info}
      - PORT=${PORT:-20128}
      - DASHBOARD_PORT=${DASHBOARD_PORT:-${PORT:-20128}}

      - ENABLE_TLS_FINGERPRINT=true

      - CODEX_HOME=/home/codex/.codex

    pre_start:
      - image: busybox
        user: root
        command: sh -c 'if [ ! -f /run/codex-appserver/token ]; then tr -dc A-Za-z0-9 </dev/urandom | head -c 32 > /run/codex-appserver/token; fi'
    command:
      - app-server
      - --listen
      - ws://0.0.0.0:1456
      - --ws-auth
```

title: fix(cli): preflight the port before serving so a second instance cannot de-register the first
body:
## Problem

Starting `omniroute serve` against a port another OmniRoute already owns printed three identical raw Node stack traces and no explanation:

```
⚠ Server exited (code=1). Restarting in 1s... (1/2)
⨯ Failed to start server
Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use 0.0.0.0:20128
```

The conflict was handed to the child process, so it only surfaced after the child had been spawned and retried twice on the supervisor's restart budget, and it never named the process actually holding the port.

## The real damage

Both spawn attempts happen **after** `writePidFile("supervisor")` and the failed child's `cleanupPidFile("server")`. So an instance that cannot bind overwrites the pid files of the healthy instance that *does* own the port:

- `supervisor/.pid` ends up pointing at the dead starter
- `server/.pid` is deleted outright

which de-registers a server that is up and serving. Observed live: healthy server `19348` under supervisor `11108`, while `supervisor/.pid` read `21440` (dead) and `server/.pid` was gone. `omniroute stop` still worked, but only by falling through to its `killByPort` port fallback rather than by the pid files.

## Fix

`serve` now resolves the port owner **before** spawning anything or touching a pid file:

```
✖ Port 20128 is already in use by PID 19348.
  Another OmniRoute is most likely already serving there, so open http://localhost:20128 before starting a second one.
  To replace it:    omniroute stop, then start again
  To run alongside: omniroute serve --port <other-port>
```

That is real output from the patched code run against an actual conflict.

Discovery is `findListeningPids()` in `bin/cli/utils/pid.mjs` — netstat on win32, lsof elsewhere. It mirrors `killByPort()`'s discovery in `stop.mjs`; consolidating the two is worth doing next time that file is touched, and is deliberately left out of this PR to keep `killByPort`'s injected-deps tests (#9455) untouched. A discovery failure reports the port as **free**, since a false "busy" would block a legitimate start, the worse of the two failures.

## Tests

New `tests/unit/cli-serve-port-in-use-preflight.test.mjs`, 6 cases: win32 netstat parsing (including that `TIME_WAIT` rows and other ports are ignored), posix lsof parsing, discovery failure treated as free, `reportPortInUse` naming the port/PID/remedies, and an end-to-end case that opens a real socket and asserts the preflight finds the owning process.

The `#2460` / `#6800` / `#11766` readiness guards still pass (6/6), since `pid.mjs` is shared.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01CJf2dxEpiwZqyZujWk57T2

title: fix(cli): escalate the readiness probe timeout so a slow health response is not a phantom boot failure
body:
## Problem

`omniroute serve` prints

```
⚠ Server did not respond within 60s. It may still be starting, or may have failed silently.
```

over a server that is **up and serving traffic**. In the reported case the process went on to
proxy real requests for the rest of the session; only the readiness signal timed out.

## Root cause

Every probe of `/api/monitoring/health` was aborted at a fixed `AbortSignal.timeout(2000)`, and a
timed-out probe is classified `"hanging"`, which `waitForServer` refuses to count toward readiness
(the #6800 guard). That puts a hard 2s ceiling on how slow a *healthy* first response is allowed to
be, and the poll cannot recover once it is crossed:

- the abort tears the socket down before the route finishes, so all of its work is discarded and
  the route's own 1s payload cache is never populated;
- 500ms later the next probe restarts the same work into the same 2s ceiling;
- repeat for the whole 60s budget.

A cold Windows boot crosses that ceiling easily: this route resolves ~10 dynamic imports and reads
the DB before it can answer. On an idle machine the first response measures ~2.5-4s.

Same failure family as #10508, which fixed it by taking a DNS lookup *out* of the 2s budget rather
than by widening the budget.

## Fix

- `bin/cli/utils/pid.mjs`: `pollHealthOnce` accepts a `probeTimeoutMs`, and `waitForServer`
  escalates it after each hang (2s, 4s, 8s, 15s), clamped to the time left in the budget so the
  caller's total timeout still holds. **Only a hang escalates**, so #6800's guarantee is unchanged:
  a socket that accepts TCP and never answers still resolves `false`.
- `waitForServer` reports each probe outcome to an optional `onOutcome` callback.
- `bin/cli/commands/serve.mjs`: the readiness-timeout diagnostic uses that outcome to say whether
  the port was accepting connections, separating "up and still warming up" from "never bound the
  port". That is the line that makes this failure diagnosable instead of alarming.

## Tests

New `tests/unit/waitForServer-slow-first-response.test.mjs`:

1. a health route answering 200 in 3.2s is reported ready (**fails on `main`**: the old poller ran
   12 probes over 30s and returned `ready=false` every time);
2. escalation stays clamped to the caller's budget (a never-answering socket with an 8s budget
   returns `false` in ~8.5s, not ~10s+);
3. the timeout diagnostic distinguishes a listening port from a dead one.

Existing guards all still pass (`cli-waitForServer.test.mjs`, `waitForServer-tcp-fallback-6800.test.mjs`):
#2460, #6800 and #11766, 9/9 green. The #10508 source-text guard is unaffected (host list and fetch
template unchanged).

End to end against a real install, the patched poller reports ready in 3.9s with the probe trace
`not-listening -> hanging -> ready`; the escalated second probe is what catches it.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The CLI polls the **heavy** `/api/monitoring/health` every 500ms, whose own docstring points
high-frequency pollers at `/api/health/ping` instead, and that is exactly what the Electron
readiness poller (`electron/lib/serverReadiness.js`) already uses. Switching the CLI probe route
would remove the cost that creates this ceiling, but it changes the readiness contract and the
#10508 guard, so it is left as a separate change.

Add filtering support to `GET /models` (and `/api/models`) so clients do not need to fetch the full catalog and filter locally.

- `prefix` — filter by model prefix/alias (e.g. `?prefix=kr` or `?prefix=kr,bai` comma-separated)

title: fix(backend): effort-suffixed combo targets don't inherit model context overrides
body:
## Summary

Since **v3.8.49**, a `priority` combo whose members use **effort-suffixed model ids** (e.g. `GLM-5.3-high`, `GLM-5.3-Flash-xhigh`, `GLM-5.2-high`) routes almost every large request to the *wrong* priority position: positions 1–2 are rejected by the context-aware compatibility filter, so the combo always falls through to a lower-priority member.

Root cause: **effort-suffixed variant ids never inherit the base model's `model_context_overrides` row**, so the compat filter falls back to static catalog windows that contradict the provider-advertised windows the rest of the pipeline uses.

## Setup

- OmniRoute **v3.8.49** (Docker), custom OpenAI-compatible provider (Openference), models discovered from the provider's own `/v1/models`.
- Combo `orchestrator`, strategy `priority`, members (in order):
  1. `openai-compatible-chat-…/GLM-5.3-high` (pinned connection `main`)
  2. `openai-compatible-chat-…/GLM-5.3-Flash-xhigh` (pinned connection `main`)
  3. `openai-compatible-chat-…/GLM-5.2-high`
  4. `qwen-cloud-token-plan/glm-5.2`
  5. `qwen-cloud-token-plan/deepseek-v4-pro`
  6. `cx/gpt-5.6-sol`
- `model_context_overrides` contains `auto:discovery` rows for the **base** ids, matching the provider's live `/v1/models`:
  - `GLM-5.3` = 385351, `GLM-5.3-Flash` = 899153, `GLM-5.2` = 128450
  - No rows for the suffixed variants (`GLM-5.3-high`, `GLM-5.2-high`, …).

## Actual behavior

For a ~500k-token raw request (plus 48k output reserve) every dispatch logs:

```
CHAT: Combo "orchestrator" [priority] with 6 models
COMBO: Context-aware fallback: kept 1/6 targets for request requirements
COMBO: Trying model 1/3: openai-compatible-chat-…/GLM-5.2-high
ROUTING: openai-compatible-chat-…/GLM-5.2-high → openai-compatible-chat-…/GLM-5.2
CONTEXT: Combo context limit: 128450 (source=target)
```

So the combo always lands on member #3 (`GLM-5.2-high`) even though the provider advertises a *larger* window for members #1/#2 than for #3.

Why:

1. `evaluateContextLimit()` (`open-sse/services/combo/contextOverrideGate.ts`) resolves the override via `getModelContextOverride(parsed.provider, parsed.model)` with the **exact** parsed id. For `GLM-5.3-high` there is no override row → verdict falls through to the static catalog → `contextWindow = 200000` → rejected for a 550k requirement. The base override (385351) is never consulted.
2. `GLM-5.2-high` *passes* because `MODEL_SPECS` deliberately ships effort-tier ids (`glm-5.2-high`: `contextWindow: 1000000`) which shadow the base override in the filter path — even though the same request is then compressed to the **base** override (`Combo context limit: 128450 (source=target)`). The filter and the compression pipeline disagree about the same target's window.

Net effect: the filter inverts the real capacity order (believes GLM-5.2-high = 1M > GLM-5.3-high = 200k, while the provider advertises 385351 vs 128450) and destroys the priority ordering.

Evidence that variant ids are meant to resolve to the base model: the dispatcher itself logs `ROUTING: …/GLM-5.2-high → …/GLM-5.2` (effort is sent separately, `effort=high`), and proactive compression uses the base override. Only the compat filter's override lookup keeps the suffix.

Related inconsistency in `/v1/models`: `of/GLM-5.2-low` reports 128450 (no spec entry for `-low` → falls through to the override) while `of/GLM-5.2-high` reports 1000000 (spec entry wins) — the same model advertises different windows depending on the effort tier.

## Expected behavior

- `resolveContextOverrideVerdict()` should strip the effort suffix (e.g. via `splitSyncedEffortSuffix()` with the base model's declared `supportedThinkingEfforts`, or by canonicalizing the variant to the base the same way the dispatcher does) before the override lookup, so `GLM-5.3-high` inherits `GLM-5.3`'s override.
- A deliberate static spec entry for a variant id (`glm-5.2-high`) should not silently shadow a persisted base-model override.
- Ideally the filter, the `/v1/models` catalog, and proactive compression should resolve the same target to the same window.

## Workaround (verified working)

Adding manual `model_context_overrides` rows for each suffixed variant, mirroring the base values:

```
GLM-5.3-high|-low|-medium|-xhigh|-max = 385351
GLM-5.3-Flash-high|-low|-medium|-xhigh|-max = 899153
GLM-5.2-high|-low|-medium|-xhigh|-max = 128450
```

immediately restores correct routing (no restart needed — the override read path is cacheless):

```
COMBO: Context-aware fallback: kept 4/6 targets for request requirements
COMBO: Trying model 1/6: openai-compatible-chat-…/GLM-5.3-high
ROUTING: …/GLM-5.3-high → …/GLM-5.3
CONTEXT: Combo context limit: 385351 (source=target)
COMBO: Model …/GLM-5.3-high succeeded
```

## Related observations

**1. The compat filter evaluates the pre-compression estimate.** `requiredContextTokens` comes from the raw body (`estimatedInputTokens` + requested output). A 500k raw request that proactive compression would reduce to ~74k still rejects every target whose window is below ~550k — e.g. a 385k-window priority-1 member is skipped even though the *compressed* request would fit comfortably. That may be intentional (prefer targets that fit without lossy compression), but combined with the suffix bug it makes priority combos collapse to a single member far more often than necessary.

**2. Catalog `capabilities.effort_tiers` shows the generic canonical ladder, not the provider-advertised set.** The same provider's `/v1/models` declares `reasoning.supported_efforts: ["max", "high", "low"]` for GLM-5.3 / GLM-5.3-Flash. Discovery normalizes these onto the canonical vocabulary (`max` → `xhigh` alias) and the variant entries correctly reflect the mapped set (`of/GLM-5.3-{low,high,xhigh}` — no `-medium`, no `-none`). However, the `capabilities.effort_tiers` field served by `/v1/models` and `/models` reports the full generic ladder `["none","low","medium","high","xhigh"]` for these entries:

- `medium` is advertised although the provider does not support it,
- `max` is not advertised although the provider does,
- requesting `of/GLM-5.3-Flash-max` works only by accident: `resolveSyncedModelIdAndEffort` cannot strip `-max` (not a canonical tier of the synced candidate), so the raw id `GLM-5.3-Flash-max` is passed through and the *provider's own* suffix mechanism resolves it.

A catalog client reading `effort_tiers` cannot tell which tiers the upstream actually accepts.

## Environment

- OmniRoute: **v3.8.49** (`ghcr.io/diegosouzapw/omniroute:3.8.49`, Docker on Windows)
- Provider: custom OpenAI-compatible chat provider with effort-suffixed combo targets and `auto:discovery` context overrides
- Strategy: `priority` (also affects any strategy that runs `filterTargetsByRequestCompatibility`)

## Impact

High for priority combos with effort-suffixed members: priority order is silently inverted for large requests, and the "winning" member is then lossily compressed to a much smaller window than the filter believed (history loss for the client).

> No account details, credentials, API keys, OAuth tokens, or other secrets are included.

title: fix(vertex): discover and route partner models correctly
body:
## Summary

- support both Vertex API keys and Service Account JSON credentials without mixing their capabilities
- infer and persist the Google Cloud consumer project for project-scoped API-key partner inference
- use API-key model discovery only for Gemini and fall back intentionally to a curated project-scoped catalog because Google rejects API keys for publishers.models.list
- fetch the live Model Garden catalog for Google, xAI, Anthropic, Mistral, and open-MaaS publishers with OAuth or Service Account credentials using Google's maximum page size of 300
- treat the authenticated Google publisher catalog as the live source for current Gemini chat models, including Gemini 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, and 3.8 Flash
- retain successful publisher results when the separate Gemini Developer API rejects Service Accounts
- accept requestAccess-backed MaaS model cards while excluding image, TTS, live, transcription, embedding, OCR-only, and retired Gemini entries from the chat catalog
- replace invalid speculative Vertex IDs with documented MaaS IDs such as deepseek-ai/deepseek-v3.2-maas, qwen/qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct-maas, and zai-org/glm-5-maas
- route Gemini, Anthropic, Mistral, xAI, and generic OpenAI-compatible MaaS publishers through their correct transports
- label the dashboard credential field accurately and explain that Service Account JSON enables live Model Garden discovery
- reject OAuth client configuration JSON with a specific explanation instead of reporting missing Service Account fields

## Authentication behavior

A project-bound API key can execute partner models, but Google does not allow it to call Model Garden publishers.models.list. OmniRoute extracts the bound project from structured Google error metadata and uses the curated project-scoped catalog.

A Service Account JSON credential is exchanged for an OAuth access token. That bearer token can list publishers/google/models and the partner publisher catalogs, so successful discovery now returns catalogMode=live_vertex_catalog without supplementing the result with a stale static Gemini baseline.

Google separately rejects Service Accounts on generativelanguage.googleapis.com. That expected rejection no longer marks the entire Vertex discovery as failed.

An OAuth web-client JSON file is only client configuration and is not itself an access credential. It requires a complete authorization-code and refresh-token flow and is now rejected with a clear message.

## Reproduction covered

The live Publisher Model list request used pageSize=1000 although Google enforces a maximum of 300. Every publisher returned HTTP 400, leaving an empty discovery result and causing Sync Models to report:

Vertex model catalogs unavailable — using local catalog

The corrected request returns the live Google and partner catalogs. Gemini chat filtering is capability-oriented: current Flash/Flash Lite/Pro variants from Gemini 2.5 onward are imported, while non-chat and retired entries are excluded.

## Verification

- focused Vertex Node tests on the release branch: 24 passed
- focused provider-dialog tests from the credential UI change: 20 passed
- npm run typecheck:core
- live Service Account token exchange: HTTP 200
- deployed fork image revision fed218ecf5a627b329acbc8b6b42e30c46dc7bf1
- deployed live discovery: source=api, catalogMode=live_vertex_catalog, 29 synchronized models, no warning
- deployed live catalog includes gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.7-flash, gemini-3.8-flash, claude-opus-4-1, and mistral-medium-3
- deployed catalog excludes image, TTS, retired Gemini 1.5, and the former speculative partner IDs
- deployed vertex/gemini-3.7-flash model test: HTTP 200

title: feat(sse): add LLM Gateway DevPass quota tracking
body:
## Summary

Adds DevPass quota tracking for the **`llmgateway`** provider, so the LLM Gateway subscription allowance shows up in OmniRoute's quota telemetry (Dashboard → Limits, quota-aware preflight/monitor) alongside OpenRouter, OpenCode, etc.

LLM Gateway exposes a single documented endpoint — [`GET /v1/key`](https://docs.llmgateway.io/developers/devpass-usage) — authenticated with the connection's own gateway API key (`llmgtwy_…`). It returns the DevPass allowance as decimal-string USD values. This PR mirrors the existing `openrouterQuotaFetcher.ts` API-key pattern.

## What it surfaces

Two independent DevPass windows:
- **Monthly plan credits** — `devPlanCreditsUsed` / `devPlanCreditsLimit` / `devPlanCreditsRemaining` (the recurring DevPass allowance).
- **Weekly premium-model window** — `devPlanPremiumWeeklyLimit` / `devPlanPremiumCreditsUsed` / `devPlanPremiumWeekResetsAt` (7-day rolling; resets to full allowance when the window expires).

Edge cases handled (per the upstream docs):
- All USD values are decimal **strings** → parsed before math.
- Pay-as-you-go keys (`devPlan: "none"`) return no quota (treated as unlimited).
- `401` (invalid/inactive key) and `403` (publishable/session key) fail open — quota tracking never blocks routing.
- 45s TTL cache keyed by connectionId, so combo preflight/monitor polling doesn't hammer the endpoint.

## Changes

- **`open-sse/services/llmgatewayQuotaFetcher.ts`** (new) — fetch + parse `/v1/key`, build a `QuotaInfo` with monthly + weekly premium windows, cache, and `registerLlmgatewayQuotaFetcher()`.
- **`open-sse/services/usage/llmgateway.ts`** (new) — dashboard usage leaf returning the two `UsageQuota` rows.
- **`src/sse/handlers/chat.ts`** — register the bespoke fetcher before `registerGenericQuotaFetchers()` (so it wins over the generic path) + its named windows.
- **`open-sse/services/usage.ts`** + **`usage/fetcherProviders.ts`** — dispatch case + registration list entry.
- **`open-sse/services/usage/supportedProviders.ts`** + **`src/lib/usage/providerLimits.ts`** — add `llmgateway` to `USAGE_SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS` and `PROVIDER_LIMITS_APIKEY_PROVIDERS` (otherwise `/api/usage/[connectionId]` rejects the connection).
- **`ProviderLimits/constants.ts`** — dashboard label + order.
- **`tests/unit/llmgateway-quota-fetcher.test.ts`** (new) — 21 cases.

## Testing

- `tests/unit/llmgateway-quota-fetcher.test.ts` — **21/21 pass** (parser incl. decimal strings + expired premium window; 401/403/network fail-open; pay-as-you-go → null; cache TTL; monthly & weekly exhaustion → `limitReached`; registration wires preflight/monitor/windows; preflight proceed vs block; usage leaf rows).
- Regression: `generic-quota-fetcher` (10/10), `provider-limits-ui` (25/25), `free-tier-providers-wave1-c` (2/2) still green — bespoke registration doesn't disturb the generic ordering.

title: fix(backend): conversation_turn_nodes / agentic_conversations have no retention — unbounded storage.sqlite growth
body:
## Problem

`conversation_turn_nodes` and `agentic_conversations` (added in #10263, migrations 155/156) have **no retention path at all**: they are not in `src/lib/db/cleanup.ts`, have no dashboard retention setting, no env knob, no cascade FK, and nothing else ever deletes from them. Verified against `v3.8.50` and current `main` (`cleanup.ts` contains zero references to either table).

#10263 resolved the storage-architecture concern for *content* — turn text is resolved on demand from `call_logs`, which is "already covered by the existing retention/cleanup lifecycle". But the **identity rows themselves are not covered**, so they outlive the content they point to: once `call_logs` retention (default 3 days, ours too) purges the artifacts, the surviving nodes' `last_correlation_id` points at nothing, and the rows are dead weight that can never render a transcript again.

## Production numbers (4 days after upgrading to this feature)

Single-instance deployment, one busy coding-agent workload (Claude Code with MCP tools), `CALL_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS=3`:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| `conversation_turn_nodes` rows | **1,155,364** (4 days after migration 156 ran) |
| `agentic_conversations` rows | 44,004 |
| Table + 4 indexes on-disk (dbstat) | **~775 MB** of a 1.1 GB `storage.sqlite` |
| Growth rate | **~190 MB/day and accelerating** (618k of the 1.15M rows are from the last 24h) |
| Rows already older than call-log retention | 63k and growing — permanently unrenderable, never deleted |

At this rate the table alone reaches multiple GB within weeks. This is the same failure class as #6848 / #4354 / #10421 (unbounded telemetry growth in `storage.sqlite`), which the cleanup job was built to prevent — the two newest tables just never joined it.

## Proposed fix

Add both tables to the existing cleanup lifecycle in `src/lib/db/cleanup.ts`, following the established per-table pattern:

1. `DELETE FROM conversation_turn_nodes WHERE last_seen_at < cutoff` — cutoff derived from the **call-log retention setting** (reuse `retention.callLogs` rather than introducing a new knob): a node older than call-log retention cannot resolve its display content anyway, so keeping identity rows longer than content is pure cost. If a separate knob is preferred, default it to the callLogs value.
2. Sweep orphaned `agentic_conversations` (no remaining turn nodes) in the same pass.
3. Register both in the startup/scheduled cleanup runner (#9624) and in the "Clear all" paths where appropriate.
4. Document the lifecycle in `docs/reference/ENVIRONMENT.md` next to the other retention rows.

Semantics note: deleting old nodes only affects *reconnect anchors* — a conversation resumed after the retention window mints a new conversation id instead of extending the old chain. That is already the documented behavior for any anchor miss (see `resolveConversationId`), so retention introduces no new failure mode, only makes an existing one time-bounded.

## Workaround we run today

Manual `DELETE FROM conversation_turn_nodes WHERE last_seen_at < datetime('now','-3 day')` plus an orphan sweep of `agentic_conversations`, scheduled outside the app. Works, but every self-hosted install that upgraded past migration 156 is silently accumulating this table until they discover it the hard way (ours was ~70% of the whole database after 4 days).

## Environment

- OmniRoute 3.8.50 (standalone Docker, `node dev/run-standalone.mjs`)
- SQLite storage on a 3.9 GB volume, WAL mode
- Traffic: parallel agentic coding sessions (large tool-heavy bodies), ~75k `call_logs` rows per 3 days

title: fix(perplexity-web): preserve system contract on follow-up requests
body:
**Summary**
This PR addresses the OmniRoute-side bug described in #12104 where follow-up messages on the `perplexity-web` provider drop the system instructions containing the injected tool-use contract, causing subsequent conversational turns to fail at using tools.

**Root Cause**
When formatting a follow-up request, `buildQuery()` historically hit an early return if a `followUpUuid` was present, returning only `parsed.currentMsg` and explicitly discarding the `systemMsg` instruction block.

**Proposed Solution**
Updated `buildQuery` to correctly prepend `parsed.systemMsg` (and the `SEARCH_HINT`, if enabled) to `parsed.currentMsg` when formatting follow-up requests. This preserves the injected instructions for the lifetime of the session without interfering with the existing UI abstraction.

**Important Clarification**
This PR **only** fixes OmniRoute's explicit dropping of instructions for follow-up turns. It **does not** claim to fix upstream limitations in Perplexity's own backend where their model might refuse or mangle structured JSON during its first response. This ensures the contract is successfully sent; how the backend handles it remains upstream behavior.

**Notes for Reviewers**
- A regression test (`tests/unit/12104-perplexity-web-followup-contract.test.ts`) is included to verify that `buildQuery` correctly includes the system contract strings on Turn 2+ follow-ups.

title: fix(perplexity-web): declare tool-calling params unsupported
body:
**Summary**
This PR fixes an issue where providing tool schemas to a combo/auto route that falls back to `perplexity-web` results in an immediate 400 error. 

**Root Cause**
The `perplexity-web` registry configuration lacked the explicit `unsupportedParams` metadata array. As a result, OmniRoute's `chatCore` failed to recognize that the provider cannot process tool parameters.

**Proposed Solution**
Added `unsupportedParams: ["tools", "tool_choice", "parallel_tool_calls"]` to the `perplexity-web` registry entry. 
- On direct requests, this triggers `stripUnsupportedParams`, correctly sanitizing the payload before execution.
- On auto/combo fallback, it triggers `filterTargetsByRequestCompatibility`, ensuring requests requiring tool calling don't route to this unsupported backend.

**Notes for Reviewers**
- This aligns `perplexity-web` with the standard API `pplx-*` models which already declare tool calling as unsupported.
- This change strictly affects capability routing and sanitization prior to execution. It does not modify the `perplexity-web` executor protocol itself.
- A regression test (`tests/unit/12104-perplexity-web-tools-unsupported.test.ts`) is included to verify the compatibility logic integration.

title: feat(backend): video-bridge #12150 P2 — remaining transcript-retention surfaces (raw snapshot, continuation, derived-prompt dispatches, response/semantic-cache)
body:
Surface map for #12150 **P2**, compiled from the P1 whole-branch review (PR #12427). P1 closed the two main-path surfaces (flattened description in the persisted request body via structured content-match redaction + durable Memory suppression). Remaining, all raw/response-class or opt-in×opt-in:

**From the original design (P2 scope):**
1. Raw pre-guardrail client-request snapshot in the detailed-log artifact (`clientRawRequest.body`, captured before guardrails).
2. `previous_response_id` continuation fail-closed when a continuation would rehydrate removed video-derived content (needs a `call_logs` marker column + migration + `resolvePreviousResponseState` refusal).

**Newly surfaced by the P1 review (add to P2):**
3. **Guardrail-ordering fail-open (Important):** video-bridge runs at priority 7; PII masker (10) and credential masker (95) rewrite the SAME chained payload afterward. With `PII_REDACTION_ENABLED`/`CREDENTIAL_REDACTION_ENABLED` on, the flattened description text changes, so the P1 log-redaction content-match (`text === fullText`) misses and the transcript persists (only PII-masked). Fix: re-anchor each redaction entry's `fullText` from the FINAL `preCallGuardrails.payload` (advisory `(container,messageIndex,partIndex)` indices are valid inside the guardrail chain — chain guardrails rewrite text in place, never splice arrays) in `deriveVideoBridgeLog` (src/sse/handlers/chat.ts). NOTE: opt-in×opt-in (PII masking is off by default, Hard Rule #20) — default path is unaffected.
4. Derived-prompt internal dispatches embed the transcript in synthesized STRING-content prompts, which the array-part content-match can't reach: pipeline-strategy stages (`src/domain/pipeline.ts` `original_request`; `pipelineRouter.ts`) and context-handoff (`open-sse/services/contextHandoff.ts` `{HISTORY}`). Memory suppression already holds for these; only their persisted request bodies retain text. Both opt-in. Fix: exact-literal substring replacement at the sink (`indexOf(fullText)`→`redactedText`, still parse-free since fullText is a trusted literal) or suppress request-body persistence for observed derived calls.
5. Residuals: call-log `responseBody` and disk `semantic_cache.response` retain the model's transcript-quoting reply; unreplaced raw video parts (failed describe with `supportsVideo !== false`, or parts beyond `maxVideos`) keep raw `transcript.cues` JSON in the logged body.

Refs #12150, PR #12427 (P1). Design: `_tasks/superpowers/specs/2026-09-01-video-transcript-retention-design.md`.

title: feat(backend): pay the documented streak_bonus and badge_unlock XP rewards

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Tracked for future work; not blocking

body:
### Problem / Use Case

`XP_REWARDS` in `src/lib/gamification/xp.ts:155-158` defines two rewards that users can read about but never receive:

```ts
/** Per consecutive streak day (multiplied by streak length) */
streak_bonus: 2,
/** Unlocking a badge */
badge_unlock: 10,
```

The award pipeline does not read `XP_REWARDS`. `emitGamificationEvent` uses a private table, `getXpForAction()` at `src/lib/gamification/events.ts:108-120`, which stops at `daily_login` and returns 0 for anything else. The streak step (`events.ts:64-78`) calls `updateStreak()` (`src/lib/gamification/streaks.ts:127-164`), which returns only the count and cannot tell the caller whether the streak just extended, and then only checks streak badges. `checkAndUnlockBadge()` (`events.ts:125-156`) inserts into `user_badges` and records a toast, with no XP. `evaluateBadges()` (`src/lib/gamification/badges.ts:414`) has no callers anywhere in the repository and awards no XP either.

The docs promise both rewards. `docs/frameworks/GAMIFICATION.md:237-252` lists `badge_earned` 25 "Earning any badge" and `streak_milestone` 15 "Reaching a streak milestone (7, 14, 30, 60, 90, 180, 365)", and lines 401-414 say `updateStreak()` returns `milestone: boolean` and the "caller awards XP and checks badges". So a user maintaining a 30-day streak and unlocking `monthly-master` sees the badge and the streak on the profile (#12377) but their XP, level and leaderboard position never move for either.

### Proposed Solution

Pay the two rewards inside the existing pipeline, using the amounts the code defines in `XP_REWARDS`:

- On the one request per UTC day that extends a streak, award `streak_bonus × currentStreak` once, guarded by an `xp_audit_log` same-day check so restarts or duplicate events cannot double-pay. Expose the "just extended" signal from the streak tracker (`advanceStreak()` returning `{ currentStreak, extended }`, with `updateStreak()` delegating so existing callers are unchanged).
- On every badge unlocked by the pipeline, award `badge_unlock` once per badge, keyed on whether `unlockBadge()` actually inserted the `(api_key_id, badge_id)` row.
- Route bonus XP through the same `addXp` + level sync + global/weekly/monthly leaderboard path as action XP, so levels and rankings stay consistent with the audit log. Keep the Radar supporter recognition unlock XP-free.

A PR demonstrating this live, with red/green unit tests, accompanies this issue.

### Alternatives Considered

- Wiring `evaluateBadges()` into `emitGamificationEvent` as the docs' flow diagram shows. Not proposed here: it has no callers, its `first`/`rank`/`hidden` criteria would change which badges unlock, and it depends on `badge_definitions`, which is only seeded lazily by `GET /api/gamification/badges` (`src/app/api/gamification/badges/route.ts:23`, see #3472).
- Paying the docs' amounts (25 / 15 at milestones) instead of the code's (10 / 2 × n). The docs and code already disagree on names too; which table is authoritative is a maintainer call and can be settled separately.
- Retroactive bonus for streaks already in progress and paying on day 1 of a streak are left out deliberately; happy to add either if wanted.

### Acceptance Criteria

- A request that extends a streak from n-1 to n writes one `xp_audit_log` row `streak_bonus` with `xp_earned = XP_REWARDS.streak_bonus × n` and `{ "streak": n }` metadata; further requests the same UTC day add none.
- No `streak_bonus` on the first day of a streak or after a broken streak.
- A badge unlocked by the pipeline writes exactly one `badge_unlock` row (`xp_earned = XP_REWARDS.badge_unlock`, `{ "badgeId": ... }`); repeated requests do not add another.
- `user_levels.total_xp` and the global/weekly/monthly leaderboard scores equal the sum of the key's audit log, and the level is recomputed after bonus XP.
- `radar_supporter` unlocks still produce no XP, no `user_levels` row and no leaderboard entry.
- Existing `tests/unit/gamification/*` stay green.

### Area

Analytics / Usage Tracking, Other (gamification)

### Related Provider(s)

None

### Additional Context

Spec: #2403. Related open PRs on the same area: #12390 (per-key XP rate limit on the award path; the change leaves that call site untouched so both apply), #12385 (leaderboard names), #12377 (profile streak). Base `release/v3.8.51`.

### Expected Test Plan

- Add `tests/unit/gamification/streak-badge-xp.test.ts` covering the acceptance criteria above (streak extension signal, amount, once-per-day, day-1/broken negatives, badge paid once, streak badge + bonus in one request, level sync after bonus, radar path).
- Run `tests/unit/gamification/*.test.ts`, `typecheck:core`, `check:db-rules`, `check-complexity-ratchets`.

title: fix(backend): background degradation map — removed default rows reappear after restart

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Tracked for future work; not blocking

body:
### OmniRoute Version

3.8.51 — traced on `release/v3.8.51` at `530096a3be465a763fb7f649f145f41238275d85`

### Installation Method

Built from source

### Operating System

Linux

### OS Version

n/a (code-path finding; applies to every platform)

### Node.js Version

n/a

### Provider(s) Involved

None in particular — Settings › Background Task Degradation

### Model(s) Involved

Any key of `DEFAULT_DEGRADATION_MAP` in `open-sse/services/backgroundTaskDetector.ts:48-63` (e.g. `claude-opus-4-5-20251101`, `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, `gpt-4o`)

### Client Tool

Dashboard (Settings › Background Task Degradation tab)

### Description

Removing one of the built-in rows of the degradation map in the dashboard does not stick. The stored map correctly omits the key, but the runtime loader merges the built-in defaults *underneath* the stored map, so every default key that is absent from the stored map is treated as "not overridden" rather than "removed", and comes back.

`src/lib/config/runtimeSettings.ts:324-329`:

```ts
  setBackgroundDegradationConfig({
    enabled: backgroundDegradation.enabled === true,
    degradationMap: {
      ...getDefaultDegradationMap(),
      ...normalizeStringRecord(backgroundDegradation.degradationMap),
    },
```

There is no way for the persisted map to express "this default key was deleted": the UI deletes the key (`BackgroundDegradationTab.tsx:67-71`, `delete map[key]`) and the PUT handler persists whatever the runtime store holds (`src/app/api/settings/background-degradation/route.ts:88-92`), so the DB simply lacks the key, and the loader fills it back in from the defaults.

Because `updateSettings()` awaits `applyRuntimeSettings()` before returning (`src/lib/db/settings.ts:346-349`), the re-merge also runs inside the PUT itself, and the response built at `route.ts:94` from `getBackgroundDegradationConfig()` already contains the row again. So the loop is: click remove → row reappears on save; click remove a second time → stored value is unchanged so `hasChanged()` is false at `runtimeSettings.ts:505-511` and the runtime store keeps the deletion → row is gone until the next restart, where `src/instrumentation-node.ts:453` calls `applyRuntimeSettings(settings, { force: true })` and the merge brings it back again.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Settings › Background Task Degradation, enable the feature (the map is only shown while enabled).
2. Do not add anything. Remove a built-in row, e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-20250514 → gemini-3-flash`.
3. Observe the list right after "Saved" (row is back), or remove it once more so the list looks right.
4. Restart OmniRoute.
5. Open the tab again.

### Expected Behavior

The removed default row stays removed after save and after restart. Removing a row in the UI is an explicit operator decision and should be persisted as such.

### Actual Behavior

The default row is back after restart (and, on the first removal, already in the PUT response). Only rows the operator *added* or *changed* survive; deletions of default rows are silently reverted.

Side effect: defaults that reference retired model ids (`claude-opus-4-5-20251101`, `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, `gemini-3-pro-preview`, …) can never be purged from an existing configuration, and neither can a default `to` target the operator's providers do not serve.

### Test Impact

Needs a new unit test

### Error Logs / Output

```shell
n/a — no error is raised; the deletion is overwritten by the merge.
```

### Screenshots

n/a

### Additional Context

- `normalizeBackgroundDegradation()` (`runtimeSettings.ts:189-210`) keeps only the keys that are present in the stored record; it does not carry any "removed" marker, so the loader cannot distinguish "never touched" from "deleted".
- Existing tests do not pin the current behaviour: `tests/unit/config-hot-reload.test.ts:89-109` only asserts that a stored key is applied (passes with either merge order), and `tests/unit/background-task-detector.test.ts:141` only asserts that the default map is non-empty.
- Not the same as #1212 (closed, needs-info, 3.6.4): there nothing was saved at all; here the save works and the loader overwrites it.
- Detection patterns have a different rule on the same function (`runtimeSettings.ts:330-333`: stored list wins entirely if non-empty, defaults only when empty), so the two halves of the same settings object already behave differently.

Possible directions, in no particular order — happy to send a PR for whichever you prefer:

1. **Stored map is authoritative when present.** Merge `getDefaultDegradationMap()` only when the stored record has no `degradationMap` (mirrors what is already done for `detectionPatterns`). Simplest change; existing configs that were saved from the UI already contain the full merged map, so nothing is lost for them.
2. **Explicit tombstones.** Keep the merge, but let the UI persist removed default keys (e.g. `degradationMap[key] = ""` or a separate `removedDefaults: string[]`), and have the loader drop those keys after merging. Keeps new defaults flowing into old configs on upgrade.
3. **An "overrides defaults" flag** on the stored record (`useDefaults: boolean`), exposed in the tab, that switches between the two behaviours above.

### Validation Plan

- New unit test on `applyRuntimeSettings()` / `getBackgroundDegradationConfig()`: store a map that omits one default key, apply with `force: true`, assert the key is absent.
- `node --import tsx --test tests/unit/config-hot-reload.test.ts tests/unit/background-task-detector.test.ts`

title: fix(claude): Fable 5.1 rejected on the native OAuth path — pinned claude-cli version is below Anthropic's 2.1.251 gate

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Tracked for future work; not blocking

body:
## Summary

Claude Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`, GA 2026-09-01) cannot be served through the native `claude` OAuth provider. Anthropic rejects the request on the Claude Code client version OmniRoute advertises, and that version is a bare constant with no environment override.

## Reproduce

`POST /api/v1/messages` through the gateway, on a Claude Max OAuth connection:

```json
{"model":"claude/claude-fable-5-1","max_tokens":16,
 "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: PONG"}]}
```

Response:

```json
{"error":{"message":"[400]: Claude Code 2.1.219 does not support this model; version 2.1.251 or newer is required. Run 'claude update', or update the Claude desktop app, then try again.","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"bad_request"}}
```

Control, same API key, same connection, seconds later — a combo targeting `claude/claude-fable-5` returns `200` with `"model":"claude-fable-5"` and the expected completion.

So the model id reaches Anthropic intact and the OAuth rail is healthy. What is refused is the advertised client version.

## Root cause

`src/shared/constants/claudeCodeClient.ts` on `main`:

```ts
export const CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_VERSION = "2.1.220";
export const CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_BUILD_REVISION = "1f2";
```

The published 3.8.49 build carries `2.1.219` / `250`. Anthropic's gate for this model is `>= 2.1.251`, so both the released build and the current `main` are below it.

There is no escape hatch on the Claude path. `CLAUDE_USER_AGENT` overrides only the User-Agent string in `buildHeaders()`, while the constant additionally feeds `open-sse/config/anthropicHeaders.ts`, `open-sse/executors/claudeIdentity.ts`, `open-sse/config/claudeCodeCompatibleIdentity.ts` and `open-sse/services/ccBridgeTransforms.ts`. Codex has `CODEX_CLIENT_VERSION` for exactly this situation; Claude has no equivalent.

Consequence: every Claude Max / Claude Pro user is locked out of Fable 5.1 through OmniRoute until a release re-captures the CLI, with no configuration workaround.

## Suggested fix

1. Capture a `claude-cli` release `>= 2.1.251` and bump the constants in lockstep — `tests/unit/claude-codex-identity-version-sync.test.ts` already guards the 4 sources.
2. Optionally add a `CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_VERSION` environment override mirroring `CODEX_CLIENT_VERSION`, so the next model gated on a client version can be unblocked without waiting for a release. This is the part that turns a recurring outage into a config change.

## Environment

- OmniRoute 3.8.49, installed globally via npm
- macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64
- Native `claude` provider, Claude Max OAuth connection, combo strategy `headroom`
- No `CLI_COMPAT_*` flags set

title: fix(auth): antigravity oauth advertises redirect_uri=http://localhost:8080/callback but never binds the port

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Tracked for future work; not blocking

body:
## Summary

`omniroute oauth start --provider antigravity` builds its Google authorize URL with

```
redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A8080%2Fcallback
```

but nothing ever listens on port 8080. After the user consents, Google redirects the browser to `http://localhost:8080/callback?state=…&code=…` and they land on **ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED**.

The flow does in fact work — it wants the callback URL pasted back at its `Callback URL or code:` prompt — but nothing on the error page says so. It reads as a failed authorization.

## Environment

- OmniRoute v3.8.50 (npm global install)
- Windows 11
- Provider: `antigravity` (flow type `browser` per `omniroute oauth providers`)

## Repro

1. `omniroute oauth start --provider antigravity`
2. Complete Google consent in the browser.
3. Browser redirects to `localhost:8080/callback?...` → **ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED**.

Port 8080 was verified free **before** launching the flow and remained unbound **while the CLI sat at its prompt**:

```
netstat -ano | findstr ":8080 " | findstr LISTENING   ->  0 results
```

So this is not a port conflict — no listener is ever started.

## Expected

Either:

- **(a)** bind a short-lived local server on the advertised port to capture `code` automatically and close the loop, or
- **(b)** don't advertise a `localhost` redirect at all — use an out-of-band redirect that renders the code for copying.

**(b) is already implemented correctly for `claude-code`**, which uses

```
redirect_uri=https://platform.claude.com/oauth/code/callback
```

and lands the user on a page that *displays* the code to paste. That flow is not confusing. The antigravity flow promises a loopback capture it never performs.

## Actual

Every user of the antigravity browser flow hits a browser error page mid-authorization and has to know, without being told, to copy the URL out of the address bar and paste it back into the terminal.

## Workaround

Copy the full `localhost:8080/callback?...` URL from the address bar and paste it at the `Callback URL or code:` prompt. The connection then completes normally — confirmed working with a live call afterwards:

```
omniroute chat --model "antigravity/gemini-3.1-flash-lite" "Reply with the single word: ok"
ok
[gemini-3.1-flash-lite · 1670ms · 243 tok]
```

## Minor, possibly related

The model ids reported by `omniroute models antigravity` are display names (`Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Thinking)`, `Gemini 3.7 Flash (High)`), and passing them verbatim to `chat` fails — silently, with no output and no error. Only slug forms such as `antigravity/gemini-3.1-flash-lite` work. Same for `ds`: the table prints `DeepSeek V4 Flash` while the API wants `deepseek-v4-flash`. Whatever the intended contract, the column heading "Model ID" is misleading if the value cannot be used as one.

title: fix(chatCore): stop executeWithUpstreamStartTimeout leaking its abortPromise listener (hedge-cancelled process exit)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the `Error [AbortError]: hedge-cancelled` process exit (exit code 7) seen on a production instance on 2026-08-31, and hardens the process crash guard around it.

**Root cause** (mapped from the built chunks back to source and reproduced): `executeWithUpstreamStartTimeout` in `open-sse/handlers/chatCore/upstreamTimeouts.ts` registered a `{ once: true }` abort listener for `abortPromise` on the long-lived client/stream signal and never removed it in `finally`, so every executor attempt (and every retry) leaked one listener. `Promise.race` only subscribes once the array literal has been evaluated; when `execute()` threw synchronously the race never ran, `abortPromise` was orphaned, and the next hedge cancellation / client disconnect aborted the signal with the string reason that `streamHandler.ts` forwards. `createAbortError()` rebuilt it as an `AbortError`-named Error and rejected a promise nothing awaited. That `unhandledRejection` reached `src/shared/utils/httpClientAbortGuard.mjs`, whose handler re-threw it as an `uncaughtException`, and the process exited.

## Commits

1. `fix(sse): stop mergeAbortSignals from leaking abort listeners` - the listener-hygiene change from #12391 (`open-sse/executors/base.ts`), included so this branch is self-contained. Note: that change is correct but is **not** on the crash path above.
2. `fix(server): stop the crash guard re-throwing combo abort reasons` - `isClientAbortError()` now absorbs `AbortError`s and the combo abort reasons from `comboAbortReasons.ts` (`hedge-cancelled`, `combo-per-model-timeout`). Ports the upstream guard tests and makes the child-process tests Windows-portable (a `file://` URL instead of a bare path in dynamic `import()`).
3. `fix(chatCore): stop executeWithUpstreamStartTimeout leaking its abortPromise listener` - the root-cause fix: keep a handle to the listener and remove it with the others in `finally`; mark the two race-loser promises as handled so a synchronous throw from `execute()` can never orphan them. Race semantics are unchanged.
4. `fix(server): absorb raw string abort reasons in the crash guard; document the verified crash path` - `streamHandler.ts` aborts with raw string reasons and undici rejects with `signal.reason` verbatim, so a cancellation can reach process level as a bare string; the guard now absorbs those too. Comments corrected to describe the verified mechanism.

## Tests

- New regression tests in `tests/unit/chatcore-upstream-timeouts.test.ts` (+2; both fail against the previous implementation: one asserts no listener growth after a resolving `execute`, one asserts that a synchronously throwing `execute` followed by a late `hedge-cancelled` abort produces no `unhandledRejection`).
- `tests/unit/httpClientAbortGuard.test.mjs` (+9), including a real child-process replay of the production shape on both the `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` routes, and a genuine-error case that must still crash.
- Results: `httpClientAbortGuard` 18/18, `chatcore-upstream-timeouts` 7/7, `executor-base-utils` 23/23; 127 related unit test files 968/970 (the 2 failures reproduce identically on the base commit: a stale G13 golden and a Windows temp-dir EPERM on cleanup).
- `tsc --noEmit -p open-sse/tsconfig.json` clean; eslint clean on the changed files.

## Related

- Extends #12391, which on its own does not fix the exit.
- Separately observed on Windows and not addressed here: `scripts/build/bootstrap-env.mjs` resolves `DATA_DIR` to `%APPDATA%\omniroute` while `src/lib/dataPaths.ts` prefers a legacy `~/.omniroute` when it exists, so the first `npm start` of a source checkout can auto-generate a new `STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and orphan every previously encrypted credential. Happy to file it as an issue.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(providers): Devin Claude Bridge fails on Windows — DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME sandbox check rejects all Windows paths
body:
## Summary

The Devin Claude Bridge executor rejects `DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME` on Windows, so Devin bridge models
(e.g. `dva/swe-1-7-lightning`) fail on Windows with:

```
[500]: DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME must be an absolute path inside the bridge sandbox
```

## Root cause

`open-sse/executors/devin-cli-agentic.ts:118-119`:

```ts
function isIsolatedHome(value: string): boolean {
  return value === "/home/bridge" || value.includes("/.sandbox/");
}
```

`buildDevinChildEnv` (same file, line 127) throws unless `DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME` is absolute AND
passes `isIsolatedHome()`. The check only recognizes Linux-style sandbox paths
(`/home/bridge`, anything containing `/.sandbox/`). A Windows path such as `C:\Users\...\devin-sandbox`
is `path.isAbsolute()`-true but never matches `isIsolatedHome()`, so the bridge always fails
closed on Windows regardless of what `DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME` is set to.

## Expected behavior

`isIsolatedHome()` (or its caller) should recognize a valid isolated home on Windows too — e.g.
accept a configured Windows sandbox directory the same way `/home/bridge`/`/.sandbox/` are
accepted on Linux — instead of unconditionally rejecting every Windows absolute path.

## Reported via

OmniRoute Discord support channel (support-mesh @-mention triage).

title: feat(deploy): Kubernetes support for k3s and k8s
body:
## Summary

The repo ships `docker-compose.yml` and `fly.toml`, and `DOCKER_GUIDE.md` already warns that "stock Docker / Kubernetes OmniRoute is one Node process + one SQLite writer" — but there are no manifests. Anyone running this on k3s or k8s writes them from scratch, against a topology whose constraints are invisible until they bite:

- a second replica against the same volume corrupts the database;
- an ingress that buffers responses withholds the SSE stream until the provider turn ends, which reads as a hung request, not as broken streaming;
- a liveness probe pointed at `/api/monitoring/health` does real DB work on every kubelet tick and restarts the only pod under load.

So the topology is **encoded, not documented**. `replicas: 1`, `Recreate` and `ReadWriteOnce` are fixed in the base, in the chart and in the generator — not exposed as options anywhere. And the chart and the spec schema refuse to render a configuration that fails at runtime, naming the field rather than emitting something that breaks later:

| Rejected | Because |
| --- | --- |
| `replicaCount > 1` | two pods on one volume corrupt the SQLite file |
| access mode ≠ `ReadWriteOnce` | a shared-write volume invites the same second writer |
| heap ceiling ≥ memory limit | the kernel OOM-kills the pod instead of Node raising a recoverable heap error (#7849) |
| `shutdownTimeoutMs` ≥ grace − preStop | the kubelet SIGKILLs mid-drain, so in-flight SSE is cut rather than drained |
| TLS with no Ingress | terminating TLS at something that does not exist |

Four artifacts, one topology:

- **`deploy/kubernetes/`** — Kustomize base plus k3s (Traefik + `local-path`) and generic k8s (ingress-nginx) overlays.
- **`deploy/helm/omniroute/`** — the same topology, values-driven.
- **`omniroute deploy k8s`** — prints manifests built from a running instance's settings, so ports, origins and flags are not transcribed by hand. It writes to stdout and touches nothing, so it composes: `omniroute deploy k8s --target local | kubectl apply -f -`.
- **`docs/ops/KUBERNETES_DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md`** — 416 lines covering deploy, ingress/SSE, probes, upgrades, storage/backups, sizing and troubleshooting.

`local` and `vps` differ only in defaults. `local` assumes k3s on the same machine. `vps` assumes a hostname in front of a cluster other people can reach, so TLS is on, `REQUIRE_API_KEY=true`, the cluster's default StorageClass binds, and `LIVE_WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is derived from the host — without that, the dashboard's live view is rejected by the origin check on the very host it is served from.

Probes follow `docs/ops/MONITORING_GUIDE.md` ("Kubernetes probe recommendations", merged in #10297): `/healthz` for startup and readiness, `/livez` for liveness, never `/api/monitoring/health`. The nginx overlay disables response buffering; the Traefik idle-timeout caveat is documented for k3s, since that one is an entrypoint setting and not an Ingress annotation.

**Provisioning is advisory on purpose.** `omniroute deploy k8s provision` prints the k3s commands and never runs them or connects to a server. Doing it directly would mean shipping an SSH client and holding a private key — a standing surface for a one-off task — so it follows the shape `contrib/vps` already uses for a VPS install. The VPS plan covers the two steps easiest to get wrong by hand: `--tls-san`, without which the cluster is only reachable as `127.0.0.1` and a remote `kubectl` fails TLS verification, and rewriting the `127.0.0.1` server address in the kubeconfig k3s writes. Values rendered into those commands are constrained to hostname, version, username and context shapes, so a printed command cannot mean something other than what it looks like.

**No new API route and no new dashboard surface.** An earlier draft put this behind `/api/deploy/*` with a UI tab; it was dropped before landing. Applying manifests by clicking is at odds with GitOps — the desired state should be versioned, not produced by a form — and the routes existed only to serve the button, spawning `kubectl` with the host kubeconfig, which is a full cluster credential. The CLI reaches the same result without that surface, so `routeGuard.ts` is untouched.

**Two fixes to the manifests themselves**, both surfaced by the test that pins the generator against `deploy/kubernetes/base`:

- Dropped `API_PORT` from the base ConfigMap. Setting it moves the API to a separate port (`src/lib/runtime/ports.ts:27`) that neither the container nor the Service exposes, leaving that listener unreachable. Unset, the API and dashboard share `PORT` — which is what the manifests actually expose.
- Made the container port protocol explicit, so the committed manifest and the generator agree byte for byte.

`deploy` also joins `--mcp` in reserving stdout for data (`bin/omniroute.mjs`). Env-loading notices there made the YAML unparseable — `control characters are not allowed` — which broke the pipe the command exists for.

## Related Issues

- Related to #10297 — the probe recommendations these manifests implement
- Related to #7849 — the V8-heap-vs-cgroup ceiling the spec schema now enforces
- Related to #8075 — multi-writer HA; until it ships, single-replica is the documented ceiling and this PR encodes it

## Validation

- [x] Change type: build-deploy (plus CLI)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR

**Applied to a live cluster, not just a dry run.** Single-node k3s v1.36.4+k3s1:

| Checked | Result |
| --- | --- |
| PVC on `local-path` | `Bound`, 10Gi, RWO |
| Pod | `1/1 Running`, 0 restarts |
| Rollout | completed, `Available=True` |
| `/healthz` and `/livez` through the Service | HTTP 200 both |
| `/v1/models` | answers application JSON, so the app serves — not just the probes |
| Probe failure events | none recorded |
| Helm chart, `--dry-run=server` | accepted by the real API server |

That run corrected two documentation errors a client-side dry run cannot catch: the health check used `wget`, and the published image ships neither `wget` nor `curl` (`node` is the only HTTP client in it); and an Ingress naming an IngressClass the cluster does not run is accepted by the API server and then silently routes nothing. Both are now in the guide, the second as a troubleshooting row.

Red first, per invariant: each manifest guard was verified to fail under a deliberate mutation of the file it protects — flipping `replicas` to 2, the access mode to RWX, `proxy-buffering` to `on`, liveness to `/api/monitoring/health`, or the shutdown budget past the grace period each turns exactly one test red, and only one. The generator/CLI suites found three real defects while being written: a `fail` placed at the top level of a `_*.tpl` file (Helm parses and discards it, so the replica guard was a silent no-op), context-name validation that rejected legitimate EKS contexts, and the stdout pollution above.

The automated review then found four more, fixed in the second commit: an address pattern that accepted a port or a bare IPv6 literal and rendered `https://host:123:6443`; a context pattern that rejected the ARN-shaped contexts managed clusters produce; the context being interpolated into a temp path, which the previous item would have turned into a directory traversal; and a quantity pattern that accepted `K` while rejecting `k`, the lowercase decimal thousand Kubernetes actually uses, so `512k` was refused. Each has a regression case.

Rebased onto `release/v3.8.51` and the full set rerun there: **54 tests passing**, `npm run typecheck:core` clean, both overlays render with zero kustomize warnings, `helm lint` clean, `check:docs-all` / `check:tracked-artifacts` / `check:cli-i18n` passing, and `omniroute deploy k8s | kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f -` still creates all six objects.

`npm run lint` reports **zero errors** but exits 2, on this branch and on an untouched checkout of the base alike — `suppressions left that do not occur anymore`, unrelated to any file here.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/k8s-deploy-manifests.test.ts` — 12 cases over the committed manifests: single replica, Recreate, RWO, probe targets, drain budget, unbuffered SSE, secret hygiene, and that the chart's replica guard is actually reachable rather than discarded.
- `tests/unit/deploy/kubernetes-manifest-generator.test.ts` — 13 cases: generation invariants, target profiles, storage-class semantics, and parity between the generator and `deploy/kubernetes/base`.
- `tests/unit/deploy/kubernetes-provision-plan.test.ts` — 19 cases: the provisioning plan's correctness (including `--tls-san` and the kubeconfig rewrite), the deploy-spec guard rails, and the five review findings below.
- `tests/unit/deploy/kubernetes-cli-command.test.ts` — 10 cases driving the real binary: the stdout contract, exit codes, and argument rejection.

## Coverage Notes

New production code is `src/lib/deploy/kubernetes/` (three pure modules, 830 lines) and `bin/cli/commands/deploy.mjs` (250 lines).

The generator and the spec schema are pure — no cluster, no filesystem, no clock — and are covered directly by the two unit suites. The CLI is covered end to end by a suite that executes `bin/omniroute.mjs` and parses its stdout, which is what pinned the stdout-pollution bug; a mocked test would not have caught it. `bin/omniroute.mjs` gains one condition, exercised by that same suite.

Nothing existing loses coverage. Beyond the new files, the only changes are the two ConfigMap/protocol fixes, that one condition, a `.prettierignore` entry for Helm's Go templates (which Prettier's YAML parser cannot read), and two doc cross-references.

## Reviewer Notes

- **The chart's guard rails live in a `define` that `deployment.yaml` includes.** Helm parses and then discards top-level code in a `_*.tpl` file, so a bare `fail` there is a silent no-op — the first version of this had exactly that bug, and `replicaCount=2` rendered happily. A test now pins the `include`.
- **`storageClassName` is omitted, never set to `""`.** An empty string disables dynamic provisioning entirely; omitting the key binds the cluster default. The two look interchangeable, so a test covers the distinction.
- **The k3s overlay assumes the Traefik that k3s ships by default.** A cluster installed with `--disable=traefik` has no such IngressClass, and the API server accepts the Ingress anyway — it is created and routes nothing. Documented in troubleshooting rather than worked around, since the fix is to name the class the cluster actually runs.
- **Context names accept `:` and `/`.** Managed clusters produce them (an EKS context is `arn:aws:eks:<region>:<account>:cluster/<name>`). Safe because nothing here goes through a shell, the leading-alphanumeric requirement prevents a value being read as an *option*, and — the part that had to change for this to hold — the temp filename in the fetch-kubeconfig step is fixed rather than derived from the context, so a `/` cannot turn it into a path.
- **Recreate means every upgrade is a short full outage** — in-flight SSE and dashboard sessions drop, and the empty-endpoint window returns a controller `502`. That is the SQLite topology, not a probe misconfiguration, and the guide says so where an operator will hit it.
- The `--tls-san` step matters more than it looks: omit it and the cluster works perfectly from the VPS itself while every remote `kubectl` fails TLS verification, which is a confusing way to lose an afternoon.
- No migration, no feature flag, no change to the request path, no new environment variable.

title: fix(claude): claude-fable-5-max returns an empty stream past ~1800 messages when stream=true
body:
Split out of #12334 so that PR #12340 (`Closes #12334`) does not bury a second, unrelated defect.

Reported by @Kizuno18 in #12334, who explicitly offered to separate it — thank you.

## Symptom

`claude-fable-5-max` returns an **empty stream** once the conversation grows beyond roughly 1800 messages. The request does not error; it completes with no content.

## Scope

- Reproduces only with `stream: true`. The same request with `stream: false` is unaffected.
- Unrelated to the combo/priority-advance defect tracked in #12334 (that one is about `hasPerModelQuota()` not listing `claude`, so a model-level failure gets attributed to the connection).

## What is needed

A repro at the message-count boundary, then a root-cause pass on the Claude streaming path — most likely a truncation or buffer limit that silently yields zero events rather than surfacing an upstream error.

Refs #12334
