title: fix(sse): stop mergeAbortSignals from leaking abort listeners
body:
## Summary

`mergeAbortSignals()` in `open-sse/executors/base.ts` attached `"abort"` listeners to its `primary`/`secondary` signals but never removed them once the merged signal settled. Every executor fetch attempt calls this (`fetchWithStartTimeout`, once per URL/retry), so a busy combo request accumulated one live listener per call on the long-lived combo/client signal. A leaked listener still fires when that signal is later aborted (e.g. a hedge cancellation arriving after this merge's own caller already finished), for a merged output nothing is watching anymore.

Fix mirrors the already-correct self-cleaning pattern in `open-sse/utils/directResponseStartTimeout.ts`'s local `mergeAbortSignals`.

Originally investigated from a production crash: `Error [AbortError]: hedge-cancelled` thrown unhandled from deep inside the built Next.js server bundle, killing the whole Node process. This fix addresses one confirmed, measured listener leak on the exact signal-merge path that carries the hedge-cancellation reason through every provider fetch — it removes a real defect regardless, though it was not possible to build a full end-to-end repro of that exact crash through the entire combo-hedging dispatch path.

## Test plan

- [x] TDD: added a regression test (`tests/unit/executor-base-utils.test.ts`) that merges the same long-lived signal 25 times and counts real listener growth via `node:events`' `getEventListeners`.
- [x] Confirmed red on pre-fix code: exactly 25 leaked listeners after 25 merges.
- [x] Confirmed green on fixed code: 0 leaked listeners, 23/23 tests passing in the full file.
- [x] Ran `tests/unit/executor-base-utils.test.ts` on Windows (the platform the original crash was observed on) — 23/23 pass.
- [x] Scoped ESLint on both changed files — 0 new violations (pre-existing violations elsewhere in `base.ts` are outside this diff's hunks).

title: fix(pack): include BUILD_OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH in APP_STAGING_ALLOWED_EXACT_PATHS
body:
## Summary

Sentinel written by `write-build-base-path.mjs` into the standalone dist/ directory. Consumed at container start by `ensure-docker-base-path.mjs` to compare the baked-in `OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH` against the runtime value.

Without this entry, prepublish Step 10.7 (`findUnexpectedArtifactPaths`) prunes `dist/BUILD_OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH` as an unexpected artifact before the tarball is packaged. The Docker container then crashes at startup with a missing sentinel (same class as the `BUILD_SHA` / #7065 incident).

## Fix

Added `"BUILD_OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH"` to `APP_STAGING_ALLOWED_EXACT_PATHS` in `scripts/build/pack-artifact-policy.ts`.

## Verification

- `git diff scripts/build/pack-artifact-policy.ts` confirms the single-line addition
- No test file changes required: the fix is a pure allowlist addition
- Pre-existing typecheck errors in `tray.ts`, `responsesTransformer.ts` etc. are unrelated to this change

## Regression testing

After merging, verify the standalone `npm pack` output contains `BUILD_OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH`:
```bash
npm run build:release
npm pack
tar -tf omniroute-*.tgz | grep BUILD_OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH
```
Expected: `package/dist/BUILD_OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH`

title: fix(memory): word/sentence-boundary aware fact truncation
body:
## Bug

`src/lib/memory/extraction.ts` truncates extracted memory facts with raw
character-offset slicing and no boundary awareness:

- `sanitizeMatch()` did `raw.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').slice(0, MAX_FACT_LENGTH)`
  — a hard cut that can land mid-word.
- `capExtractionText()` did `text.slice(-MAX_EXTRACTION_TEXT_LENGTH)` on the
  front edge when input exceeds `MAX_EXTRACTION_TEXT_LENGTH` (64KB) — same
  problem, opposite edge.

These facts later get injected into LLM context as `<system-reminder>`
memory blocks, so a mid-word/mid-clause cut produces garbled fragments
(e.g. text starting with a stray closing parenthesis, or ending with no
punctuation and a half word).

## Fix

- `sanitizeMatch()` now backs the cut index off to the nearest clean
  boundary within a lookback window: prefers a sentence-ending mark
  (`.`/`!`/`?`) so the fact reads as a complete clause, falls back to a
  plain whitespace/word boundary, and only falls back to the original hard
  cut when no boundary exists in the window (e.g. one long unbroken run of
  characters).
- `capExtractionText()` applies the equivalent boundary-aware trim on the
  front edge of the kept tail (extends the cut forward to the next
  whitespace boundary rather than slicing mid-word).

This mirrors the boundary-aware truncation already used by
`open-sse/services/compression/lite.ts` (issue #8169) for tool-result
truncation, so the codebase now has one consistent pattern for this class
of problem.

## Testing

- New: `tests/unit/memory-extraction-boundary-truncation.test.ts` — covers
  a long match cut at a word boundary, a match cut preferentially at
  sentence-ending punctuation, short strings passing through untouched,
  the no-boundary-in-window fallback, and `capExtractionText`'s
  boundary-aware tail behavior (both under and over the 64KB cap).
- Ran existing `tests/unit/memory-extraction.test.ts` alongside the new
  file — all 28 tests pass, no regressions:
  ```
  ℹ tests 28
  ℹ pass 28
  ℹ fail 0
  ```
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — no new type errors introduced by
  this change.

No unrelated files were touched.

title: fix(sse): stop CircuitBreaker.execute() from counting a resolved upstream failure as a success
body:
⚠️ base-red inherited: #12335

## Summary

Fixes #12254. `CircuitBreaker.execute()` calls `_onSuccess()` for any non-throwing resolution of
`fn()`, but `handleChatCore()` returns `{success:false, status:5xx}` for ordinary upstream failures
without throwing. `executeChatWithBreaker`'s `breaker.execute(chatFn)` therefore called
`_onSuccess()` on every dispatch through this call site regardless of outcome — and in CLOSED
state `_onSuccess()` does `failureCount = Math.max(0, failureCount - 1)`, which silently cancelled
the very next explicit `_onFailure()` call in `chat.ts` / `accountFallback.ts` for the same
attempt. `failureCount` could never climb past ~1, so the provider breaker could never open under
sustained genuine failures — on both the direct dispatch path and the combo path (same
per-provider breaker singleton via `getCircuitBreaker(provider)`).

## Fix

Adds `CircuitBreaker.executeTrackingFailureOnly()`: identical `OPEN`/`HALF_OPEN` gating and
identical `isFailure`/`classifyError`-based failure accounting on an actual throw, but it never
calls `_onSuccess()` just because `fn()` resolved. Success/failure accounting for a *resolved*
result stays exactly where it already lives — the explicit `_onSuccess()`/`_onFailure()` call
sites in `chat.ts` and `recordProviderSuccess()`/`recordProviderFailure()` in
`accountFallback.ts` (the combo path already uses these explicitly, per `combo.ts:2358/1870/3587`
gated by `shouldRecordProviderBreakerFailure()`). `executeChatWithBreaker`'s two
`breaker.execute()` call sites are switched to the new method. `CircuitBreaker.execute()` itself
is untouched — it has no other callers in the codebase.

This is the direction discussed in #12254: a shared classification
(`PROVIDER_BREAKER_FAILURE_STATUSES` / `shouldRecordProviderBreakerFailure`) already exists on the
combo side and the single-model side already does explicit `_onFailure()`/`_onSuccess()` calls —
the one remaining gap was this single `execute()` call site quietly fighting all of that explicit
accounting.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/circuit-breaker-provider-accounting-12254.test.ts` — unit tests on `CircuitBreaker`
  directly: no implicit accounting on a resolved (non-throwing) call; failure accounting on an
  actual throw still honors `classifyError`; consecutive genuine failures escalate to `OPEN`
  without being cancelled by interleaved non-throwing calls (the exact reported bug shape); `OPEN`
  and `HALF_OPEN` gating unchanged.
- `tests/unit/execute-chat-with-breaker-accounting-12254.test.ts` — end-to-end reproduction at the
  actual regressed call site: drives 6 real upstream 502s through `executeChatWithBreaker` (mocked
  `global.fetch`, same harness pattern as `execute-chat-resource-pressure-breaker.test.ts`) and
  asserts the breaker accumulates zero implicit accounting.

Ran locally: `npm run typecheck:core` (clean), `npm run lint` (clean), `npm run check:cycles`
(clean), plus the full existing circuit-breaker/combo-provider-cooldown/account-fallback test
files (174 tests, all passing) to confirm no regression from the new method or the two swapped
call sites.

## Changelog

Fragment to follow in this same branch once the PR number is known (`changelog.d/README.md`
convention).

title: fix(providers): Codex Responses + Gemini 3 Flash loops on narrated tool intent instead of emitting function_call
body:
### OmniRoute Version

3.8.50

### Installation Method

npm (global)

### Operating System

Windows

### OS Version

Windows 11

### Node.js Version

v24.7.0

### Provider(s) Involved

Gemini (direct Gemini provider)

### Model(s) Involved

`gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview`

### Client Tool

OpenAI Codex CLI

### Description

When Codex CLI uses `gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview` through OmniRoute's `/v1/responses` endpoint, agentic tool use can get stuck in a loop.

Gemini appears to understand that a local tool should be used, but instead of returning a structured function/tool call to Codex, it repeatedly outputs plain text describing the action it intends to perform.

Example:

> I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
>
> I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
>
> I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.

No local filesystem/tool action is executed, and Codex continues repeating the same intention until the request is manually aborted.

Gemini 3 Flash supports native function calling, so this appears to be an interoperability issue in the **Codex Responses API → OmniRoute → Gemini tool-calling path**, rather than a missing model capability.

This may be related to PR #8211, which already documents Gemini Flash models sometimes narrating an intended tool call as text instead of emitting a real `functionCall`.

However, #8211 mainly added support for mapping `tool_choice: "required"` to Gemini `ANY`. Normal Codex agent requests use `tool_choice: "auto"`, which OmniRoute maps to Gemini `VALIDATED`, so the problem can still occur during normal Codex usage.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Codex CLI to use OmniRoute via the Responses API:

```toml
wire_api = "responses"
base_url = "http://localhost:20128/v1"
```

2. Configure a model or combo whose selected target is:

```text
gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview
```

3. Open Codex in a normal coding workspace where local tools such as filesystem and shell access are available.

4. Use a project containing instructions that cause Codex to inspect the workspace, for example an `AGENTS.md` file or similar project instructions.

5. Send a simple request such as:

```text
ping
```

6. Codex decides that it should inspect the workspace, for example the `memory-bank/` directory.

7. Observe that instead of executing the filesystem tool, the assistant repeatedly prints statements such as:

> I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.

8. The loop continues until the request is manually aborted.

### Expected Behavior

When Gemini decides that a local Codex tool is required, OmniRoute should preserve the structured tool-call round trip:

```text
Codex /v1/responses
  → OmniRoute
  → Gemini functionCall
  → OmniRoute
  → OpenAI Responses function_call
  → Codex executes local tool
  → function_call_output
  → model continues
```

Codex should execute the requested filesystem/shell operation and continue the task normally.

### Actual Behavior

Instead of emitting an executable tool call, the model repeatedly narrates the action it intends to perform:

```text
I'll start by exploring the workspace and checking the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the current state of the project.
I'll start by exploring the workspace and checking the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the current state of the project.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
```

No local tool execution occurred, and the request had to be manually aborted.

### Test Impact

Needs a new integration test

### Error Logs / Output

There was no HTTP error. OmniRoute reported a successful Gemini request.

Relevant OmniRoute call-log information:

```text
POST /v1/responses
status: 200
provider: gemini
model: gemini-3-flash-preview
requestedModel: gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview
sourceFormat: openai-responses
targetFormat: gemini
duration: ~28s
error: null
```

Codex output before manually aborting:

```text
I'll start by exploring the workspace and checking the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the current state of the project.
I'll start by exploring the workspace and checking the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the current state of the project.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
```

The exported OmniRoute call log omitted the complete request and response bodies due to the payload size limit. Therefore, I cannot currently confirm whether Gemini emitted no `functionCall` at all, or whether a structured call was lost during translation back to the OpenAI Responses format.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional Context

OmniRoute is running locally on Windows:

```text
http://localhost:20128
```

Codex uses the OpenAI Responses API through OmniRoute:

```toml
wire_api = "responses"
```

The request was routed through a small priority combo. Gemini was the first target and was selected immediately, so this reproduction did not involve cascading through multiple providers.

Relevant routing order:

```text
1. gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview
2. groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b
3. openrouter/qwen/qwen3-coder
```

No fallback occurred because the Gemini request itself returned HTTP 200.

This appears related to PR #8211:

> `fix(sse): Gemini malformed function-call handling + tool_choice translation`

That PR documents a Gemini Flash model being observed to:

> narrate an intended tool call in plain text instead of actually emitting one

The current OmniRoute Gemini translator maps:

```text
tool_choice unset/auto    → VALIDATED
tool_choice required/any  → ANY
tool_choice none          → NONE
specific function         → ANY + allowedFunctionNames
```

Codex normally sends:

```text
tool_choice: "auto"
```

Therefore, the `required → ANY` fix does not cover the normal Codex agent path.

I do not think simply changing all `auto` requests to Gemini `ANY` would be correct, because that would change the semantics of `auto` and force a tool call even when one is unnecessary.

The suspected path is therefore:

```text
Codex /v1/responses
  tool_choice: auto
        ↓
OmniRoute Responses → Chat normalization
        ↓
OpenAI → Gemini translation
  auto → VALIDATED
        ↓
Gemini may narrate intended tool usage as prose
        ↓
Codex receives no executable tool call
        ↓
Agent can repeat the same intended action
```

This is only a suspected explanation. The raw upstream Gemini response was not available in the exported call log, so it is not yet proven whether the `functionCall` is missing at the Gemini side or lost later during response translation.

### Validation Plan

At minimum, a targeted integration test should verify the complete **Codex/OpenAI Responses → Gemini → OpenAI Responses** tool-call round trip.

Existing tests around PR #8211 should remain green, especially:

```bash
node --import tsx --test tests/unit/gemini-tool-choice.test.ts
```

A new regression test should be added for the Codex Responses API path, for example:

```bash
node --import tsx --test tests/integration/gemini-codex-responses-tool-call.test.ts
```

The new test should exercise:

```text
/v1/responses
tool_choice = auto
function tools present
Gemini native functionCall
Responses function_call returned to client
function_call_output accepted
successful continuation
```

The test should verify that:

1. Responses API function tools survive the Responses → Chat → Gemini translation.
2. Gemini receives valid `functionDeclarations`.
3. A native Gemini `functionCall` is translated back into an OpenAI Responses `function_call`.
4. The function name, call ID, and arguments are preserved.
5. A subsequent `function_call_output` can be sent back successfully.
6. The model continues after the tool result instead of repeatedly narrating the intended action.

It is important that the regression test uses:

```text
tool_choice: "auto"
```

and not only:

```text
tool_choice: "required"
```

because `auto` represents the normal Codex agent path involved in this reproduction.

The general project checks should also remain green:

```bash
npm run test:unit
npm run test:integration
npm run check
```

For live verification, running Codex CLI through OmniRoute with `gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview` and repeating the reproduction above should result in a real local tool execution instead of repeated prose describing the intended action.

title: fix(backend): API-key budget enforcement can compute $0 for routing alias auto
body:
### OmniRoute Version

16.3.1

### Installation Method

npm (global)

### Operating System

Linux

### OS Version

Ubuntu

### Node.js Version

24.20.0

### Provider(s) Involved

Kiro, Qoder, Antigravity

### Model(s) Involved

auto

### Client Tool

Claude Code

### Description

API-key budget enforcement is structurally wired before execution, but the accumulated cost can become $0 for requests routed through the `auto` alias even when the underlying execution has a known billable model.

Environment: OmniRoute v16.3.1, Node.js v24.20.0, npm global installation, Ubuntu.

Observed data:
- `usage_history`: 2163 records
- `kiro/auto`: 1422 records (~66%)
- `qoder`: 16 records
- `antigravity`: pricing resolves correctly through the `ag` alias
- `pricing_synced`: 0 keys
- `models_dev_pricing`: 0 keys

Causal chain:
`usage_history` → `apiKeyUsageLimits.ts:406` → `costCalculator.ts:176` → `db/settings/pricing.ts:123`

`usage_history.model` stores the routing alias `auto`, while `call_logs.model` stores the resolved model.

`normalizeModelName("auto")` returns `"auto"` unchanged because normalization only removes a `provider/` prefix.

For `kiro/auto`, the provider resolves, but the model lookup fails because `DEFAULT_PRICING` has no `auto` entry. `costCalculator.ts:207` then executes:

`if (!pricing) return 0`

Therefore billable executions can contribute $0 to API-key accumulated cost.

This is separate from:
1. recommendation vs authorization/execution mismatch; and
2. `aggregateHistory.ts` hardcoding `daily_usage_summary.total_cost` to `0.0`, which affects cost reporting but not this enforcement path.

The suggested direction is to calculate cost using the resolved model (already available in `call_logs.model`) or otherwise resolve `auto` before pricing lookup. The preferred implementation should be determined upstream.

Additionally, missing pricing should be represented as UNKNOWN/error rather than silently becoming $0.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run OmniRoute v16.3.1 with a request routed through the `kiro` provider using the `auto` routing alias.
2. Allow the request to execute against a billable resolved model.
3. Inspect the resulting `usage_history` record and observe `model = "auto"`.
4. Inspect the corresponding `call_logs` record and observe that it contains the resolved model.
5. Trace API-key budget calculation through `apiKeyUsageLimits.ts:406`.
6. Observe that cost calculation reaches `costCalculator.ts:176`.
7. Observe that pricing lookup receives `auto`.
8. `normalizeModelName("auto")` remains `auto`.
9. Pricing lookup fails to find a price for `auto`.
10. `costCalculator.ts:207` returns `0`.
11. Observe that the API-key accumulated cost does not consume the actual cost of the execution.

### Expected Behavior

API-key budget enforcement should calculate the cost of a billable execution using the resolved model/provider pricing.

A known-priced execution routed through `auto` should produce a cost greater than $0, and that cost should be included in the API-key budget accumulation.

If pricing cannot be determined, the result should be represented as UNKNOWN or an explicit error rather than silently treated as $0.

### Actual Behavior

For `kiro/auto`, `usage_history.model` contains the routing alias `auto` instead of the resolved model.

The pricing lookup therefore fails to find a model price and `costCalculator.ts:207` silently returns `0`.

As a result, billable executions can contribute $0 to API-key budget accumulation.

In the inspected installation, 1422 of 2163 usage_history records (~66%) were `kiro/auto`.

The enforcement call itself is present and occurs before execution (`chat.ts:603` → `enforceApiKeyPolicy`), so the issue is not absence of enforcement wiring; it is incorrect/unknown cost accounting upstream of the budget calculation.

### Test Impact

Needs a new unit test

### Error Logs / Output

```shell
Observed behavior:

usage_history.model = "auto"
call_logs.model = <resolved model>

costCalculator.ts:207:
if (!pricing) return 0

Observed dataset:
2163 usage_history records
1422 kiro/auto records (~66%)
qoder: 16 records without pricing entries
antigravity: pricing resolves through alias ag

pricing_synced: 0 keys
models_dev_pricing: 0 keys
```

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional Context

This report is based on a local OmniRoute v16.3.1 installation.

Important clarification: Antigravity was investigated as a possible pricing issue but is NOT the defect. Its provider alias resolution works through `PROVIDER_ID_TO_ALIAS` (`antigravity` → `ag`).

The relevant discrepancy is that usage_history records the routing alias (`auto`) while call_logs records the resolved model.

No Eco IA code, routing, pricing, database, or configuration was modified while reproducing this finding.

The related Eco IA investigation is recorded as D-124 / FINDING-003. Separate findings concerning recommendation-vs-execution enforcement and daily cost aggregation are intentionally distinguished from this issue.

### Validation Plan

The fix should be validated with an automated regression test covering:

1. A `kiro/auto` request whose resolved model has known pricing.
2. Verify calculated cost > 0.
3. Verify the calculated cost is included in API-key budget accumulation.
4. Verify `auto` does not silently produce $0 when the resolved model is billable.
5. Verify missing pricing produces UNKNOWN/error rather than zero.
6. Run the relevant OmniRoute unit/integration test suite.

title: fix(combo): scope Claude model failures to the model, not the account
body:
## Summary

A priority combo whose steps are five different models on one Claude OAuth connection stops at step 1: whatever kills the first step is recorded against the connection, and the pre-dispatch cooldown gate then skips every later step because they share that connection. The drop order is silently a single-model route.

`hasPerModelQuota()` returns false for `claude`, so in `markAccountUnavailable()` the model-lockout branch never runs and the failure lands on the connection row instead. `getPersistedConnectionCooldownSkipReason()` takes it from there.

To keep the model-specific bug in #12334 out of the picture, I reproduced it with a first step naming a model that cannot exist. The 404 lands and step 2 is never dispatched; point step 2 at a different account and the same combo works:

```
COMBO: Trying model 1/2: claude/claude-bogus-model-x
COMBO: All models failed | claude/claude-bogus-model-x: model — model: claude-bogus-model-x (HTTP 404)
COMBO: Trying model 2/2: agy/claude-sonnet-4-6      ← only when step 2 is another account
```

A Claude OAuth connection multiplexes Fable 5, Opus 5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet and Haiku behind one credential — the multiplexing the doc comment on `hasPerModelQuota` already describes. Its quota is a different question, though: a 429 on a Max subscription is account-wide, and `shouldMarkAccountExhaustedFrom429("claude", …)` pins that in `account-fallback-service.test.ts`. Adding `claude` to `hasPerModelQuota` breaks that test, and rightly so.

So this splits the two: a new `hasPerModelFailureScope()` covers the non-quota statuses (404, 5xx, a stream that ended with no content), `auth.ts` uses it only when `status !== 429`, and quota scope stays exactly as it was. `targetExhaustion` gets the same treatment for 404, which names one model the account cannot serve rather than a bad connection — the empty-content 502 was already exempt through `isEmptyContentFailure`.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12334

## Validation

- [x] Change type: routing
- [x] Focused tests: `tests/unit/combo-claude-per-model-scope.test.ts` plus every existing test touching `hasPerModelQuota` or `targetExhaustion` — 17 files, 226 passing, 0 failing
- [x] `npx eslint` on the four touched files: same 3 pre-existing `no-unused-vars` errors in `accountFallback.ts` before and after (line 2413 shifts to 2437), no new ones
- [x] Reconciled with `release/v3.8.51`
- [x] Production-code changes come with a new test

Full unit suite on this branch: 47 failures. On the same checkout with the patch stashed: 46. The one extra is `Vietnamese locale has no internal missing markers or empty fallbacks`, which fails on a clean tree when run on its own:

```
not ok 1 - Vietnamese locale has complete key parity with English
not ok 2 - Vietnamese locale has no internal missing markers or empty fallbacks
```

so it is suite variance, not this change.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/combo-claude-per-model-scope.test.ts` (new) — mirrors `combo-provider-cooldown-sibling.test.ts`: failure scope for `claude`, quota scope unchanged, the connection-level override still winning, and the two sides of the pre-dispatch gate (a real cooldown still protects siblings; no cooldown lets step 2 dispatch).

## Coverage Notes

`hasPerModelFailureScope()` is covered by the new file. The `auth.ts` and `targetExhaustion.ts` call sites are covered indirectly by the existing lockout tests for gemini, github, nvidia, ollama, openrouter, vertex and agentrouter, which all still pass — they pin that nothing outside `claude` changed scope.

## Reviewer Notes

The risk worth looking at is the 429 split. I deliberately left quota scope alone so a Max rate limit keeps retiring the account, since dropping to another model there would just burn a second upstream call. If you would rather have per-model quota for `claude` too, that is a one-line change to `hasPerModelQuota` plus an update to the `shouldMarkAccountExhaustedFrom429` expectation — happy to do it either way.

Reproduced against `diegosouzapw/omniroute:main` @ `sha256:88996a83` and the previous `sha256:611c555b`, on a single `claude_max` OAuth connection.

title: fix(api): X-OmniRoute-Fallback-Attempts always 0 on chat completions (streaming and non-streaming)
body:
### Summary

On streaming (`stream: true`) `/v1/chat/completions` responses, `X-OmniRoute-Fallback-Attempts` is absent (defaults to `0`) on the initial SSE header set, even when a combo failover to a non-primary target actually happened before the stream opened. The same request with `stream: false` reports the correct attempt count. `X-OmniRoute-Provider`/`X-OmniRoute-Model` **do** update correctly to whoever actually answered on the streaming path — only the fallback-attempts counter is missing.

### Root cause (confirmed in code)

`assembleStreamingResponseHeaders()` (`open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingResponseHeaders.ts:14`) builds the streaming meta headers by calling `buildStreamingResponseHeaders()` with an explicit object literal that only passes `provider`, `model`, `cacheHit: false`, `latencyMs: 0`, `usage: null`, `costUsd: 0`, `strategy` — it never forwards `fallbackAttempts`. The sole call site, `chatCore.ts:5523`, doesn't pass it either. `buildOmniRouteResponseMetaHeaders()` (`src/domain/omnirouteResponseMeta.ts`) defaults `fallbackAttempts` to `0` when omitted, so the header comes out `0`/absent on every streaming response regardless of what actually happened upstream.

The non-streaming path (`nonStreamingResponseHeaders.ts`) threads the real `fallbackAttempts` value through, which is why `stream: false` reports it correctly.

### Repro

1. Configure a combo where the primary target fails (bad key / unreachable) and a fallback target succeeds.
2. `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `stream: false` → `X-OmniRoute-Fallback-Attempts: 1` (correct).
3. Same request with `stream: true` → header absent/`0`, despite `X-OmniRoute-Provider` correctly showing the fallback provider.

### Impact

A client that only reads response headers can tell which provider answered a streaming call, but cannot tell whether that was the first-choice target or a failover — any "answered via fallback" UI signal is dead on the streaming path.

### Expected

Streaming and non-streaming responses expose the same routing-outcome headers; `X-OmniRoute-Fallback-Attempts` should be >= 1 on the streaming response whenever a failover occurred.

### Note on `X-OmniRoute-Fallback-Reason`

There is no `X-OmniRoute-Fallback-Reason` header anywhere on the `/v1/chat/completions` path (streaming or non-streaming) — that's not a regression, it never existed there. A similarly-named `X-Routing-Fallback-Reason` exists, but only on the separate `/api/v1/relay/chat/completions` relay-routing endpoint (`src/app/api/v1/relay/chat/completions/route.ts`), which is a different backend. Worth a follow-up feature request if a reason code on the main chat path is wanted, but it's out of scope for this bug.

---
Found and independently reproduced while building [OmniHarness](https://github.com/shipking-ai/omniharness) — reported by @shipking-ai in discussion #12303, code root-caused there by @diegosouzapw.

**OS:** Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 host)
**Provider:** `claude` (OAuth, `organizationType: claude_max`)
**Models:** `claude-fable-5-max`, `claude-opus-5-max`, `claude-opus-4-8-max`, `claude-opus-4-7-max`, `claude-opus-4-6`
**Client:** cURL (also reproduced through Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness)

## Description

A `priority` combo whose steps are five different models on a **single** Claude OAuth connection never advances past step 1. Whatever kills step 1 is recorded against the connection, and the pre-dispatch cooldown gate then skips every remaining step because they share that connection — so a per-model drop chain silently behaves like a single-model route.

The chain I wanted is the same shape as Claude Code's own fallback: stay on Fable 5 until it errors, then continue on Opus 5, then 4.8, then 4.7, then 4.6, all on one Max subscription.

I also hit a second, unrelated bug on the way in (`claude-fable-5-max` returning an empty stream on long histories) — details at the end, happy to split it into its own issue if you prefer.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Connect one `claude` OAuth account.
2. Create a `priority` combo whose steps all pin that same `connectionId`, with a deliberately invalid model first so the model-specific bug below isn't part of the picture:

```json
{"name":"zz-failover-test","strategy":"priority","models":[
  {"id":"m1","kind":"model","model":"claude/claude-bogus-model-x","providerId":"claude","connectionId":"<A>"},
  {"id":"m2","kind":"model","model":"claude/claude-opus-5-max","providerId":"claude","connectionId":"<A>"}
]}
```

3. `POST /v1/messages` with `"model": "zz-failover-test"`.
4. Change only step 2 to a different account (`agy`) and repeat.

## Expected Behavior

Step 1 fails, step 2 is dispatched. A 404 on one model says nothing about the other models on that connection.

## Actual Behavior

Same account — step 2 is never dispatched:

```
COMBO: Trying model 1/2: claude/claude-bogus-model-x
COMBO: All models failed | claude/claude-bogus-model-x: model — model: claude-bogus-model-x (HTTP 404)
```

Different account on step 2 — works:

```
COMBO: Trying model 1/2: claude/claude-bogus-model-x
COMBO: All models failed | claude/claude-bogus-model-x: model — model: claude-bogus-model-x (HTTP 404)
COMBO: Trying model 2/2: agy/claude-sonnet-4-6      ← dispatched, answers 200
```

With the real chain the connection gets marked and all four remaining steps report the skip:

```
COMBO: Model claude/claude-fable-5-max returned 200 but failed quality check: streaming upstream error
AUTH:  claude | all 1 active accounts rate limited (reset after 5s) | lastErrorCode=502.0, lastError=Claude returned an empty response (no content bloc
AUTH:  (×4 — one per remaining step)
COMBO: All models failed | Upstream response failed quality validation: streaming upstream error
```

Things I tried that don't change it:

- `config.failoverBeforeRetry: true` with `maxSetRetries: 1`, `setRetryDelayMs: 0` — the `AUTH … rate limited` lines disappear, step 2 is still never tried.
- Leaving `connectionId` off step 2 — the request then ends with `all targets were skipped by pre-dispatch filters`.

## Where it comes from

`hasPerModelQuota()` in `open-sse/services/accountFallback.ts` decides whether a failure is scoped to the model or to the whole connection. It returns true for `antigravity`/`agy`, `codex`, `gemini`, `github`, passthrough and compatible providers — and false for `claude`. So in `src/sse/services/auth.ts` the model-lockout branch (`isPerModelQuotaProvider && … (status === 404 || status === 429 || status >= 500)`) never runs for a Claude OAuth connection, the failure lands on the connection row instead, and `getPersistedConnectionCooldownSkipReason()` in `open-sse/services/combo/comboPredicates.ts` then skips every sibling target before dispatch.

A Claude OAuth connection multiplexes Fable 5, Opus 5, 4.8, 4.7, 4.6, Sonnet and Haiku behind one credential, which is exactly the multiplexing the doc comment on `hasPerModelQuota` describes. That also matches how the subscription actually meters: Opus has its own weekly cap on Max, so an Opus 429 doesn't mean Sonnet is unavailable — dropping to another model is the documented behaviour of Anthropic's own client.

I'm opening a PR that adds `claude` to `hasPerModelQuota()` with a regression test mirroring `tests/unit/combo-provider-cooldown-sibling.test.ts`.

## Second bug: `claude-fable-5-max` empty stream above ~1800 messages, streaming only

Minimal repro — no tools, no system prompt, alternating `ping N` / `pong N` messages of ~4 tokens each, ending with a `say OK` user turn:

| messages | `stream: true` | `stream: false` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1400 | ok | ok |
| 1521 | ok | ok |
| 1801 | **502 empty response** | ok |

```
[STREAM] Empty Claude stream at flush - emitting error (claude:claude-fable-5-max)
🌊 [STREAM] CLAUDE | claude-fable-5-max | 14490ms | error: Claude returned an empty response (no content block)
❌ claude [502]: Claude returned an empty response (no content block)
```

Same account, same betas, same payload: `claude-opus-5-max`, `claude-opus-4-8-max` and `claude-opus-4-7-max` all answer fine at 1801 messages. Size isn't the trigger — a single 275 KB / 125k-token message streams fine, it's the message count, and the boundary moved from ~1350 on the 2026-08-13 build to ~1800 on the current one. The 14.5 s before the flush suggests the upstream connection is held open and then closed with nothing on it, so a retry-on-empty-stream inside the Claude SSE handler may be worth it independently of the combo behaviour.

## Test Impact

Needs a new unit test.

title: feat(perf): lazy-boot quota auto-ping scheduler + build heap floor guard
body:
## Summary

Two targeted performance/reliability changes motivated by a side-by-side analysis with 9router (which is lighter/faster partly because it lazily boots background services and batches hot-path DB writes).

### 1. Lazy-boot the quota auto-ping scheduler (9router 27b37705 parity)

- `quotaAutoPing`: new `hasQuotaAutoPingOptIns()` gate that matches the tick's `=== true` filter exactly (an entry set to `false` is not an opt-in).
- `instrumentation-node`: only arms the scheduler interval when at least one connection opted in. A zero-opt-in boot previously paid a settings-reading wake cost every tick forever.
- `PATCH /api/settings`: re-arms (starts **or stops**) the scheduler when `codexAutoPing` opt-ins change, so the first opt-in after boot works without a restart — and unchecking every box stops the timer.

### 2. Build heap floor guard in `build-next-isolated.mjs`

An operator shell that exports `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=1024"` (a common dotfile leftover) was silently **respected** by the previous `\!/--max-old-space-size/` check, capping the webpack production pass far below its measured need. Measured on 2026-09-01 (16 GB macOS host):

| Scenario | Heap ceiling | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| inherited 1024 (dotfile case) | ~1 GB | OOM (SIGABRT) 12 s into compile |
| direct 2048 | ~2 GB | OOM at 2 GB heap, peak RSS 2469 MB |
| backend-only + 3072 | ~3 GB | OOM, heap fully consumed (Scavenge at 3021 MB) |
| full build | 4 GB floor (new behavior) | passes (validated below) |

The guard now **replaces in place** any inherited ceiling below the 4096 MB floor (no duplicate flags, unrelated NODE_OPTIONS entries preserved). `OMNIROUTE_BUILD_MEMORY_MB` overrides and inherited values ≥ floor remain respected, and Turbopack-native memory behavior is unchanged (see #6409).

## Tests

- `tests/unit/build-next-isolated.test.ts`: 12/12 pass (2 new: floor-replace semantics + unrelated-flag preservation)
- `tests/unit/quota-auto-ping.test.ts`: 20/20 pass (1 new: opt-in gate shapes incl. absent/empty/false entries)

title: fix(providers): Vertex Express-key discovery failure is an intentional local-catalog fallback, not degraded (#12328)
body:
## What

Fixes #12328.

Vertex model discovery with a **Vertex AI Express API key** (`?key=` on `generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models`) always fails with `400 API_KEY_INVALID` — the Generative Language API is a different service and does not accept Vertex-scoped keys. Today that failure falls back to the generic `API unavailable — using local catalog`, which reads as a transient/auth problem and sends users chasing key/permission ghosts, while the connection test and inference both succeed.

## Change

On discovery failure with `400/403` **and** an Express key (`queryKey` path, non-JSON credential):

- the fallback warning now names the real cause (`Vertex Express API key cannot list models on the Generative Language API (API_KEY_INVALID) — …`);
- the local catalog is served as an **intentional** source (`localIntentional`, #5460/#5465) so model-sync imports it instead of treating the response as a degraded remote fetch.

Everything else is untouched:

- SA-JSON (Bearer) discovery unchanged — live listing still parsed when it succeeds;
- transient errors (500, network, redirect-block) keep the existing generic fallback;
- the fetch attempt itself still happens (best effort; no capability removed for keys that *do* work on that endpoint).

## Test plan

New regression suite `tests/unit/vertex-express-discovery-12328.test.ts` (4 tests, real tmpdir DB + mocked `fetch`, same pattern as `7993-noauth-proxy-routing`):

1. Express key + 400 → 200, `source: local_catalog`, `intentional: true`, warning matches `API_KEY_INVALID`; exactly one call to the GL endpoint with `key=` in query;
2. Express key + 403 → same intentional fallback;
3. Express key + 500 → generic fallback, **not** intentional, no `API_KEY_INVALID` in warning (no behavior change);
4. SA-JSON (real RSA key generated in-test; `importPKCS8` rejects placeholders) → OAuth token mocked, live GL list parsed, `source: api`, no `?key=` on the wire.

Local verification on `release/v3.8.51`:

```
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/vertex-express-discovery-12328.test.ts   # 4/4 pass
npm run typecheck:core                                                            # clean
npx eslint <touched files>                                                        # 0 new errors (9 pre-existing in route.ts)
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/integration/model-catalog-responsiveness-9199.test.ts  # 2/2
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/integration/provider-journey.contract.test.ts          # 14 tests / 0 fail
```

title: fix(combos): clear LKGP pins when a combo is deleted
body:
Closes #12326.

## Problem

`deleteCombo()` deleted the `combos` row but left the combo's LKGP pins in `key_value`. Pins are keyed by `${comboName}:${modelId}`, so once the combo is gone those rows become unreachable:

- the combo itself 404s, so no API or UI path addresses them
- `clearLKGP()` needs a `modelId` the caller no longer knows
- `clearAllLKGP()` wipes the namespace for *every* combo, which is not a targeted cleanup

On an instance with 26 live combos the `lkgp` namespace held 54 rows — 52 for live combos plus 2 orphans from a combo deleted earlier that day. Roughly 2 rows leak per deleted combo, so the table grows without bound for anyone who creates and deletes combos regularly.

## Fix

Provider-connection deletion already handles this via `deleteLKGPByConnectionIds()` (#8887), and `providers/deletion.ts` wraps it in try/catch so cleanup failures never block the delete. This applies the same pattern to combo deletion:

- **`deleteLKGPByComboName(comboName)`** in `settings/lkgp.ts` — deletes every pin under the `${comboName}:` prefix and calls `invalidateCachedLKGP()` for each, so a stale pin cannot be served from the 5s read cache for the rest of its TTL.
- **`deleteCombo()`** resolves the combo name before deleting the row, then clears its pins inside try/catch — a cleanup failure is logged, never fatal to the delete.

The `:` delimiter in the prefix keeps sibling combos safe (`prod` does not match `prod-canary`), and `LIKE` wildcards in combo names are escaped so a name like `temp_a` cannot match `tempXa`.

## Tests

New `tests/unit/combo-delete-lkgp-cleanup-12326.test.ts`, structured after the #8887 suite:

| Test | Covers |
|---|---|
| deleting a combo removes its LKGP pins | core fix, survivor pins untouched |
| invalidates warmed read-cache entries | the `invalidateCachedLKGP()` path |
| prefix-sharing sibling keeps its pins | `prod` vs `prod-canary` |
| `LIKE` wildcards do not widen cleanup | `temp_a` vs `tempXa` |
| unknown combo id leaves state untouched | early-return branch |
| combo without pins deletes cleanly | no-op path |

Verified the tests actually exercise the fix — with the cleanup block removed, 4 of 6 fail; with it restored, all 6 pass.

```
$ npx tsx --test tests/unit/combo-delete-lkgp-cleanup-12326.test.ts
# tests 6
# pass 6
# fail 0
```

No regressions in the existing LKGP suites:

```
$ npx tsx --test tests/unit/delete-provider-connection-invalidates-lkgp-8887.test.ts \
    tests/unit/lkgp-enabled-context-11181.test.ts \
    tests/unit/lkgp-stale-pin-exhaustion-11911.test.ts \
    tests/unit/combo-delete-lkgp-cleanup-12326.test.ts
# tests 18
# pass 18
# fail 0
```

`eslint` and `prettier --check` are clean on the touched files; `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in them (the repo's existing baseline errors are unrelated and untouched).

## Notes

- Changelog fragment added at `changelog.d/fixes/12330-combo-delete-lkgp-cleanup.md`.
- No behaviour change for combos that are never deleted; the new query only runs on the delete path.

title: fix(providers): Vertex model discovery sends Express API key to generativelanguage.googleapis.com — always fails (400 API_KEY_INVALID), UI masks it as 'API unavailable'
body:
## Summary

Model discovery for the **Vertex** provider with a **Vertex AI Express API key** (`auth_type=apikey`, opaque string) always fails, because the discovery branch sends the key to the **Generative Language API** — a different Google service that does not accept Vertex keys. The UI then silently falls back to the local catalog with a generic "API unavailable" message, which makes it look like a key/permission problem on the user's side. It isn't: the same key works perfectly for inference through OmniRoute's own Vertex executor.

## Environment

- OmniRoute `3.8.50` (docker image digest `dbf98ed1efcf…`, digest-pinned)
- Provider: `vertex`, auth type: API key (Vertex AI Express mode, created in Cloud Console)
- Region: `us-central1`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add a Vertex connection with a **Vertex AI Express API key** (not a Service Account JSON, not an AI Studio key).
2. Connection test passes: `POST /api/providers/{id}/test` → `{"valid":true,…}`.
3. Trigger model discovery / "Importar Modelos" (`GET /api/providers/{id}/models`).
4. Observe: the import modal reports `API unavailable – using local catalog` / "no new models to import", and the container logs:

```
[models] Vertex model discovery failed { provider: 'vertex', status: 403 }
```

## Root cause

`src/app/api/providers/[id]/models/route.ts` (line ~1856 on current `main`), vertex branch:

```ts
// Vertex AI lists models from the Generative Language `v1beta/models` endpoint, which both
// Express-mode API keys (via ?key=) and Service Account JSON ... can reach.
...
const baseUrl = "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models?pageSize=1000";
...
let pageUrl = queryKey ? `${baseUrl}&key=${encodeURIComponent(queryKey)}` : baseUrl;
```

The comment's assumption is inverted for Express keys: a Vertex Express key is **not** valid on `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`. Reproduced with a plain curl using exactly the request the discovery branch builds (`?key=<vertex express key>`):

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": 400,
    "message": "API key not valid. Please pass a valid API key.",
    "status": "INVALID_ARGUMENT",
    "details": [
      {
        "@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo",
        "reason": "API_KEY_INVALID",
        "domain": "googleapis.com",
        "metadata": { "service": "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The SA-JSON path (OAuth bearer) is unaffected; only the Express-key (`queryKey`) path is broken.

## Why this is misleading (the actual UX bug)

- The connection test says the key is **valid** (it is — for `aiplatform.googleapis.com`).
- Inference through the executor works for **any** model id, including ones absent from the local catalog (verified live E2E with `gemini-3.7-flash` / `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, which the static registry doesn't list yet).
- Discovery then fails with a generic "API unavailable – using local catalog", so users chase key permissions/regional IAM ghosts while the real cause is the endpoint choice.

Net effect: the live catalog is never fetched, and the local catalog lags behind what the key can actually serve.

## Suggested fix

For the Express-key (`queryKey`) case, at minimum:

1. **Don't route Vertex Express keys to `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`.** Since Vertex has no public list-all endpoint for Express keys, discovery could instead probe a curated candidate list via the publisher inference endpoint (`…/v1/publishers/google/models/{id}` with `x-goog-api-key`), or simply skip the remote fetch.
2. **Surface the real upstream error** (status + `reason: API_KEY_INVALID`, service `generativelanguage`) instead of the generic `API unavailable` warning, so the modal distinguishes "endpoint not applicable to this credential type" from "network/auth failure".

## Workaround (verified on 3.8.50)

Register the models as custom models — they're merged into every catalog read (#6247) and route normally in combos:

```
POST /api/provider-models {"provider":"vertex","modelId":"gemini-3.7-flash","modelName":"Gemini 3.7 Flash (Vertex)","source":"manual"}
```

After that, `{"model":"gemini-3.7-flash","providerId":"vertex",…}` in a combo serves traffic end-to-end (verified with text and multimodal probes).

title: feat(backend): video frame-contract follow-ups — clamp negative estimate, unify encode-site prefixes, broker-client 4th site
body:
Follow-ups bundled from the whole-branch review of PR #12322 (shared JPEG frame data-URI contract). None are defects in that PR; all ride safely today.

1. **Clamp negative estimates**: `estimateJpegFrameBytes` (src/lib/guardrails/videoBridgeFrameContract.ts) can return -1 for degenerate inputs the charset-only pattern admits (e.g. `data:image/jpeg;base64,=`). Consequence-free in the current upper-bound usage, but a documented byte-estimate should never go negative: `return Math.max(0, ...)`.
2. **Encode-side prefix unification**: three encode sites still hardcode the `data:image/jpeg;base64,` template literal instead of `JPEG_FRAME_DATA_URI_PREFIX`: videoBridgeContactSheet.ts:123, videoBridgeRuntime.ts:1000, videoBridgeDrilldownLifecycle.ts:173.
3. **Fourth validation site (behavior decision, not mechanical)**: videoBridgeBrokerClient.ts:104 keeps its own deliberately case-SENSITIVE regex validating the broker's own output. Unifying it onto the (case-insensitive) shared contract changes acceptance semantics — decide, don't just swap.
4. **Optional behavior change**: structural base64 validation (misplaced padding currently passes the charset-only pattern; the internet-facing drill-down path keeps its own canonical round-trip check, so no exposure today).

Refs PR #12322.

title: fix(antigravity): surface image quotas in Provider Limits
body:
## Summary

- keep Antigravity image-only models excluded from chat discovery
- add a quota-specific visibility predicate for user-facing image quota buckets
- use that predicate when parsing both `fetchAvailableModels` and `retrieveUserQuota`
- add regression coverage proving `gemini-3.1-flash-image` is visible in Provider Limits while TTS/tab buckets remain hidden

## Problem

Antigravity quota parsing currently reuses `isDiscoverableAntigravityModelId()`. That predicate is intentionally chat-specific and excludes `gemini-3.1-flash-image`, so Google can return a valid image quota bucket from `retrieveUserQuota` / `fetchAvailableModels` and OmniRoute silently drops it before the Provider Limits UI sees it.

The image model should remain absent from the chat catalog, but its quota is user-facing because the model is callable through `/v1/images/generations`.

## Implementation

Introduce `isUserVisibleAntigravityQuotaModelId()` as a separate concern from chat discovery. It accepts normal discoverable chat models plus the known user-facing Antigravity image quota IDs, while continuing to reject TTS, tab-completion, retired, and other non-chat buckets.

`getAntigravityUsage()` now uses this quota predicate in both quota passes, including the `retrieveUserQuota`-only path.

## Related work

#9231 already fixed OAuth refresh / quota-aware credential selection and 401 account rotation for the image-generation route. This PR does not duplicate that work; it only fixes quota visibility in Provider Limits.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- regression test added for live `retrieveUserQuota` precedence (`25%` image quota) and non-chat filtering

title: fix(gemini): preserve response-schema nullability across union flattening
body:
## Summary

- `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` flattens every union spelling of "nullable" before a schema reaches Gemini: `flattenTypeArrays` turns `["string","null"]` into `"string"`, and `flattenAnyOfOneOf` drops the `{"type":"null"}` branch. That is correct for **tool parameters** and wrong for **response schemas**, where the union is the only thing telling the model that "nothing" is a legal answer. Stripped of it, a model with nothing to say returns the *string* `"null"` — or fabricates a value (live repro in #12308: an empty `{}` payload produced a fully-adjectived invented product). Pydantic emits the `anyOf` spelling for `Optional[str]`, so the fabricating path is the common one for Python consumers.
- A new `preserveNullable` walk runs as **Phase 1b**, before the Phase 2 flattening destroys the union: it records Gemini's sibling-key spelling, `nullable: true`, on any node whose `type` array contains `"null"` or whose `anyOf`/`oneOf` carries a `{"type":"null"}` branch.
- The key survives the rest of the pipeline for free: `nullable` is absent from `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS`, and `flattenAnyOfOneOf` merges the surviving branch with `Object.assign`, which cannot clobber a key the branch lacks. No existing pass changes.
- **Opt-in**: `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` gains `options: { preserveNullable?: boolean }` defaulting to off. Only the `responseSchema` call site in `openai-to-gemini.ts` passes it; the three tool-parameter call sites in `geminiToolsSanitizer.ts` keep today's behaviour exactly.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12308
- Related to #12307 (fix that one first — it corrupts the repro for this one)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: provider (Gemini/Antigravity translator path)
- [x] Focused tests from the golden path (commands below)
- [ ] `npm run lint` — targeted `npx eslint` run on the three touched files instead; full lint left to CI
      (every reported error reproduces identically on the untouched `release/v3.8.51` base — pre-existing, none introduced by this diff; the new/changed files themselves lint clean)
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (branched from `release/v3.8.51` HEAD `d920e64`)
- [x] Production-code changes include a new automated test in this PR

Commands run locally:

```bash
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/12308-gemini-response-schema-nullable.test.ts
npx eslint open-sse/translator/helpers/geminiHelper.ts \
  open-sse/translator/request/openai-to-gemini.ts \
  tests/unit/12308-gemini-response-schema-nullable.test.ts
```

Verified end-to-end against a live gateway carrying this change (unique nonce per request so nothing was served from cache):

```
type: ["string","null"]        -> {"value": null}     upstream 1685ms
anyOf: [{string},{null}]       -> {"value": null}     upstream 1697ms
oneOf: [{string},{null}]       -> {"value": null}     upstream 1674ms
anyOf: [{string},{number}]     -> {"value": "null"}   upstream 2242ms   <- negative control: no null branch, nothing marked
```

A/B on the same gateway, same prompts: with the fix, 5/5 real JSON nulls; without it, the string `"null"` and two fabricated descriptions.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/12308-gemini-response-schema-nullable.test.ts` (new): all three union spellings survive as `nullable: true`; nested fields are marked; a union **without** a null branch is left untouched; a caller-supplied `nullable: true` passes through; **the default (tool-parameter) call is byte-unchanged**; and a guard pins `nullable` out of `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS` so a future keyword-list edit cannot silently kill the fix.

## Coverage Notes

- `geminiHelper.ts`: the new walk + options parameter are covered by all eight tests, including the negative control and the default-path test.
- `openai-to-gemini.ts`: a one-argument change at the `responseSchema` call site; visible in the diff, exercised by the live verification above. (Importing that module in a unit test drags in the executor/registry graph, so the call-site is deliberately not unit-tested — the helper-level flag semantics are.)

## Reviewer Notes

- **Tool-calling behaviour is deliberately untouched.** Flattening to a concrete type is correct for `functionDeclarations.parameters` (and `VALIDATED` mode depends on today's shapes); the flag exists so the fix cannot leak there. The default-path test locks this.
- Known limitation, pre-existing: `hasNullBranch` matches `type === "null"` exactly, mirroring the filter `flattenAnyOfOneOf` already uses — a branch written as `{"type": ["null"]}` is matched by neither. Rare; can be handled separately if it ever turns up.
- `claude-to-gemini.ts` imports this helper but never calls it (dead import, line 5); left alone here to keep the diff minimal.

title: fix(cache): fold the response output contract into the semantic cache signature
body:
## Summary

- The semantic-cache signature hashed only `{model, messages, temperature, top_p}`. Two temp=0 requests with identical messages but **different `response_format`** therefore shared a cache key, and the second was served the first's stored body under a 200 — a response that violates the schema it asked for. `tools`/`tool_choice` had the same exposure. (Live repro in #12307: a request for `{color, wheels}` was served a stored `{"value": "A vibrant red bicycle…"}`.)
- `generateSignature` now accepts an optional **output contract** — `response_format`, `text.format` (Responses API spelling), `tools`, `tool_choice`, collected by a new exported `outputContractOf(body)` — and folds it into the hashed payload **only when present**. Plain-chat signatures are byte-identical to before, so every existing plain-chat cache entry survives the upgrade; only structured-output/tool requests get new keys (their old entries age out within the 30-minute TTL).
- All three call sites pass it: the read path (`chatCore/semanticCache.ts`) and both write paths (`semanticCacheStore.ts`, `streamingSemanticCacheStore.ts`). Read/write key symmetry is preserved automatically because `bodyForCacheWrite` snapshots the same body object the read path hashed (the existing `#cache-signature-asymmetry` guard).

## Related Issues

- Closes #12307
- Related to #12308 (this cache defect corrupts the experiment used to investigate that one)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: other — semantic cache (`src/lib` + chatCore decomposition modules)
- [x] Focused tests from the golden path (commands below)
- [ ] `npm run lint` — targeted `npx eslint` run on the five touched files instead; full lint left to CI
      (every reported error reproduces identically on the untouched `release/v3.8.51` base — pre-existing, none introduced by this diff; the new/changed files themselves lint clean)
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (branched from `release/v3.8.51` HEAD `d920e64`)
- [x] Production-code changes include a new automated test in this PR

Commands run locally:

```bash
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/12307-semantic-cache-output-contract.test.ts
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/cache-signature-roundtrip.test.ts     # existing guard, still green
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/11559-semantic-cache-ttl-expiry.test.ts  # existing guard, still green
npx eslint src/lib/semanticCache.ts open-sse/handlers/chatCore/semanticCache.ts \
  open-sse/handlers/chatCore/semanticCacheStore.ts \
  open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingSemanticCacheStore.ts \
  tests/unit/12307-semantic-cache-output-contract.test.ts
```

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/12307-semantic-cache-output-contract.test.ts` (new): different schemas ⇒ different signatures; identical schemas ⇒ shared signature; tools split the key; **plain chat keeps the legacy signature byte-for-byte** (backward compat); `outputContractOf` returns `null` for plain chat and collects the `text.format` spelling; both store paths forward the contract to `generateSignature` (via injected deps, mirroring the existing DI seams).

## Coverage Notes

- `src/lib/semanticCache.ts`: new exported helper + one parameter — covered by the six signature tests.
- The three chatCore modules: one-argument change each — covered by the two deps-injection forwarding tests.
- Existing guards `cache-signature-roundtrip` and `11559-semantic-cache-ttl-expiry` rerun green, so read/write symmetry and TTL behaviour are unchanged.

## Reviewer Notes

- **Key stability:** the `output` field is spread into the payload only when the contract is non-null, so plain-chat keys (the overwhelming majority — on the instance where this was found, the cache served 13 hits against 5390 upstream calls over three days) are unchanged and their entries stay valid. Structured-output entries written by the old code become unreachable and expire via TTL; that is the point of the fix.
- **Key-order caveat:** `response_format`/`tools` are folded in as sent, so two clients serialising the same schema with different key order will miss each other's entries. That is a miss, not a collision — and it mirrors how `messages` content objects are already treated.
- **Alternative considered:** refusing to cache schema-carrying requests entirely (measured cost ≈ 0.24 % hit-rate loss). Folding the contract into the key was chosen because it keeps those hits and covers `tools` uniformly.
