title: fix(providers): response schemas lose nullability on the Gemini hop — model returns "null" or fabricates values
body:
# Response schemas lose nullability on the Gemini hop — the model answers `"null"` or invents a value

**OmniRoute Version:** 3.8.50 (reproduced live); defect verified unchanged at `release/v3.8.51` HEAD `d920e64`
**Installation Method:** Docker / Docker Compose
**Operating System:** Linux (Ubuntu 26.04)
**Component:** `open-sse/translator/helpers/geminiHelper.ts` → `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity`
**Severity:** silently fabricated data in structured output

## Summary

`cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` flattens every union spelling of "nullable" before the schema reaches Gemini. That is correct for a **tool parameter** — Gemini wants a concrete type there and the caller decides what an absent argument means. It is wrong for a **response schema**, where the union is the only thing telling the model that "nothing" is a legal answer.

Stripped of it, a model with nothing to say cannot answer `null`. It answers with the *string* `"null"`, or it invents a plausible value. Both reach the client as schema-conformant data.

## Reproduction

Empty payload, a prompt that explicitly asks for null, one nullable field:

```bash
curl -s $BASE/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-omniroute-no-cache: true' \
  -d '{
  "model":"<antigravity-gemini-model>","temperature":0,
  "messages":[
    {"role":"system","content":"Write a description of the product. If the payload carries nothing to describe, the value must be null."},
    {"role":"user","content":"{}"}
  ],
  "response_format":{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"d","strict":true,"schema":{
    "type":"object","properties":{"value":{"type":["string","null"]}},
    "required":["value"],"additionalProperties":false}}}}'
```

> Send the bypass header. Without it this request is a strong candidate for a stale cache entry — see #12307 — the cache signature omits `response_format`.

Observed across all three spellings:

```
type: ["string","null"]              -> {"value": "null"}      (the 4 characters, as a string)
anyOf: [{string}, {null}]            -> a fabricated description
oneOf: [{string}, {null}]            -> a fabricated description
```

Expected: `{"value": null}` in all three.

### The fabrication case is the serious one

Asked to describe an **empty** payload through an `anyOf` schema, the model did not return `"null"`. It invented a product, with adjectives:

```json
{"value": "این محصول یک پوشاک مردانه شیک و باکیفیت است که..."}
```
> *"This product is an elegant, high-quality piece of men's clothing that…"* — from an input of `{}`.

A fabricated value is indistinguishable from a real one downstream. `"null"` at least looks wrong to a human scanning a column; this does not. Anything that matches, deduplicates or bills on such a field gets a confident wrong answer.

### This is not an edge case

**Pydantic emits `anyOf` for `Optional[str]`**, and so does `zod-to-json-schema`. Any consumer generating response schemas from Pydantic models — which is the common case in Python — has been on the fabricating path, not the `"null"` path. One downstream team found their memory service had been extracting through `Optional[str]` fields this whole time.

## Root cause

`geminiHelper.ts`, Phase 2 of `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity`:

```ts
  // Phase 2: Flatten complex structures
  mergeAllOf(cleaned);
  flattenAnyOfOneOf(cleaned);   // drops the {"type":"null"} branch, keeps the rest
  flattenTypeArrays(cleaned);   // ["string","null"] -> "string"
```

```ts
function flattenTypeArrays(obj: unknown): void {
  ...
  if (record.type && Array.isArray(record.type)) {
    const nonNullTypes = record.type.filter((t) => t !== "null");
    record.type = nonNullTypes.length > 0 ? nonNullTypes[0] : "string";
  }
  ...
}
```

Both passes are right about Gemini's constraint — its `Schema` proto has no union types — and both throw away the one bit that mattered.

## Why `nullable: true` is the right fix

Gemini spells nullability as a sibling key rather than a type. Two properties make this a clean fix rather than a workaround:

1. **`nullable` is not in `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS`.** The word does not appear anywhere in `geminiHelper.ts`. A schema that already carries it survives Phase 4's keyword removal untouched. Verified by injecting it ahead of the sanitizer and observing real JSON nulls end to end.

2. **`flattenAnyOfOneOf` merges with `Object.assign(record, toRecord(selected))`.** The surviving branch has no `nullable` key of its own, so a flag set beforehand is not clobbered. The existing passes need no changes at all — only ordering.

Ordering is the whole trick: the flag has to be recorded *before* Phase 2, because afterwards there is no union left to detect.

## Proposed fix

Deliberately **opt-in**, so tool parameters keep their current (correct) behaviour.
`cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` is shared: `geminiToolsSanitizer.ts` calls it at three sites
for `functionDeclarations.parameters` — all keep the default — and
`openai-to-gemini.ts` calls it once for `responseSchema`, which alone opts in.

- A `preserveNullable` walk runs as Phase 1b, **before** the Phase 2 flattening destroys the
  union: it records `nullable: true` on any node whose `type` array contains `"null"` or whose
  `anyOf`/`oneOf` carries a `{"type":"null"}` branch.
- `nullable` survives the rest of the pipeline for free: it is absent from
  `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS`, and `flattenAnyOfOneOf` merges the surviving branch with
  `Object.assign`, which cannot clobber a key the branch does not have.
- `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` gains an options argument (`{ preserveNullable?: boolean }`)
  defaulting to off; the `responseSchema` call site passes `{ preserveNullable: true }`.

No other call site needs the flag. (`claude-to-gemini.ts` imports the helper at line 5 but
never calls it — that import is dead and could be dropped separately.)

**An accompanying PR implements this, with tests.**

### Known limitation of this patch

`hasNullBranch` matches `type === "null"` exactly, mirroring the filter `flattenAnyOfOneOf` already uses. A branch written as `{"type": ["null"]}` is matched by neither. That is pre-existing and rare, and can be handled separately if it turns up.

## Verification

Deployed ahead of an instance and measured with cache-busting nonces, so nothing was served from the cache:

| repair | result |
|---|---|
| ON, 5 runs | `null` × 5 — real JSON null |
| OFF, 3 runs | `"null"`, then two fabricated descriptions |

Per spelling, end to end through a live gateway:

```
type: ["string","null"]        -> {"value": null}     upstream 1685ms
anyOf: [{string},{null}]       -> {"value": null}     upstream 1697ms
oneOf: [{string},{null}]       -> {"value": null}     upstream 1674ms
anyOf: [{string},{number}]     -> {"value": "null"}   upstream 2242ms   <- correct: no null branch, nothing marked
```

The last row is the negative control: a union with no `null` member must not be marked nullable, and is not.

## Related

#12307 (semantic cache signature omits `response_format`/`tools`) is worth fixing first. Its signature omits `response_format`, so the natural way to investigate *this* bug — hold the prompt fixed, vary only the schema — pins the cache key and returns a stale body. It corrupts the experiment you would run to confirm this fix landed.

title: fix(backend): semantic cache signature omits response_format/tools — structured-output requests are served each other's bodies
body:
# Semantic cache key omits `response_format` — structured-output requests return each other's bodies

**OmniRoute Version:** 3.8.50 (reproduced live); defect verified unchanged at `release/v3.8.51` HEAD `d920e64`
**Installation Method:** Docker / Docker Compose
**Operating System:** Linux (Ubuntu 26.04)
**Component:** `src/lib/semanticCache.ts` → `generateSignature`
**Severity:** returns HTTP 200 with a body that violates the caller's schema

## Summary

The cache signature is computed from `{model, messages, temperature, top_p}`. `response_format` is not part of it — nor are `tools`, `tool_choice`, `max_tokens`, `seed` or `stop`. Two requests with identical messages and **different response schemas** therefore share a cache key, and the second is served the first's stored body under a 200.

## Reproduction

Both requests below have byte-identical `messages`; only the schema differs.

```bash
# A — schema {value}
curl -s $BASE/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model":"<gemini-model>","temperature":0,
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Describe a red bicycle."}],
  "response_format":{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"d","strict":true,"schema":{
    "type":"object","properties":{"value":{"type":"string"}},
    "required":["value"],"additionalProperties":false}}}}'

# B — same messages, schema {color, wheels}
curl -s $BASE/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model":"<gemini-model>","temperature":0,
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Describe a red bicycle."}],
  "response_format":{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"d","strict":true,"schema":{
    "type":"object","properties":{"color":{"type":"string"},"wheels":{"type":"integer"}},
    "required":["color","wheels"],"additionalProperties":false}}}}'
```

Observed:

```
A -> {"value":"A vibrant red bicycle featuring a glossy crimson frame..."}
B -> {"value":"A vibrant red bicycle featuring a glossy crimson frame..."}   <- A's body
```

Expected for B: `{"color":"red","wheels":2}` — which is exactly what it returns with `-H 'x-omniroute-no-cache: true'`.

`call_logs` confirms the mechanism:

```
B without bypass ->  cache_source=semantic   duration=2ms
B with    bypass ->  cache_source=upstream   duration=1768ms
```

B receives a 200 whose body has neither `color` nor `wheels`. A client validating the response sees required fields missing; a client that does not validate consumes the wrong object silently.

## Root cause

`src/lib/semanticCache.ts:135`

```ts
export function generateSignature(
  model,
  conversation,
  temperature = 0,
  topP = 1,
  apiKeyId?: string
) {
  const payload = JSON.stringify({
    model,
    messages: normalizeConversation(conversation),
    temperature,
    top_p: topP,
  });
  const digest = crypto.createHash("sha256").update(payload).digest("hex");
  return apiKeyId ? `${apiKeyId}.${digest}` : digest;
}
```

`normalizeConversation` compares role/content as exact strings, so despite the `semantic` label this is an exact-match cache, not an embedding one. That is not the problem — the problem is that everything determining the *shape* of a valid response is absent from the key.

`tools` / `tool_choice` have the same exposure: `isCacheableForWrite` does not exclude tool-calling, so a request with tools can be served the body of one without.

## Why this deserves priority over the schema-nullability bug

It is not the larger defect, but it is the one that hides the others.

It returns 200s silently, and it corrupts precisely the experiment an engineer runs to investigate anything else. Isolating one variable means holding the prompt fixed — and holding the prompt fixed is what pins the cache key. A correct methodology walks straight into it.

Concretely: while diagnosing the nullability bug (filed separately), this cost three rounds of back-and-forth between a gateway operator and a downstream consumer. Both parties independently concluded "the fix is not deployed" from what were stale cache reads. The only tell was latency — 5 ms versus 2 s — which neither was recording.

## What is already correct

- Keys are namespaced per `apiKeyId`, so there is **no cross-tenant leakage**. That was the first thing checked.
- The 30-minute TTL and the `temperature === 0` gate are reasonable.
- `x-omniroute-no-cache` works on both the read and write paths.

## Proposed fix

Fold the output contract into the digest. Concretely:

- A helper `outputContractOf(body)` collects the fields that decide the *shape* of a valid
  response — `response_format`, `text.format`, `tools`, `tool_choice` — and returns `null`
  when none are present, so plain-chat signatures (and their existing cache entries) are
  unchanged.
- `generateSignature` accepts it as an optional final argument and folds it into the hashed
  payload only when non-null.
- The three call sites pass it: the read path in `open-sse/handlers/chatCore/semanticCache.ts`
  and the two write paths (`semanticCacheStore.ts`, `streamingSemanticCacheStore.ts`). Since
  `bodyForCacheWrite` snapshots the same body object used at read time (#cache-signature-asymmetry
  guard), read/write key symmetry is preserved automatically.

**An accompanying PR implements this, with tests.**

### Cheaper alternative

If changing the key is undesirable, refusing to cache any request that carries a response schema also closes it. We deployed exactly that as a stopgap in front of our own instance and measured the cost: over three days the cache served **13 hits against 5390 upstream calls (0.24 %)**, because real agent traffic carries unique conversations. Skipping the cache for structured output is close to free. Fixing the key is still better, because it keeps the hits and covers `tools` too.

title: question: should universal handoff be suppressed or de-duplicated on same-request fallback cascades?
body:
## Context

PR #12227 (by @hartmark) originally shipped two changes:

1. Translating the universal-handoff fallback note from Spanish to English — merged as the surviving scope of that PR.
2. An `i === 0` gate suppressing universal handoff on **same-request fallback cascades** — trimmed out before merge because it contradicts the contract pinned by `tests/unit/combo-context-relay.test.ts` (a fallback landing on a model different from the session's last turn injects exactly one retargeted handoff message).

This issue tracks the substantive question behind change 2, which deserves a deliberate decision rather than a silent contract flip.

## The cost argument (from @hartmark)

- When a combo's primary target fails and a fallback step (i > 0) lands on a different model than the previous *turn*, today's code both injects the existing handoff summary **and generates a new one in the background** — one extra LLM call per affected request.
- On an unstable primary, this happens on *every* request; the reporter measured **1200+ failures/week** in their environment, each paying the extra background call.
- The injected "you are being handed off" system message describes internal routing the client never observed fail, adding prompt noise.

## The current contract's rationale

- The session's continuity anchor is `getLastSessionModel()` (last successful turn). If the previous turn ran on model A and this request ends up served by model B — even via internal fallback — the *model actually answering* changed, and the summary keeps context coherent.
- `tests/unit/combo-context-relay.test.ts` deliberately encodes this: fallback with model ≠ last-turn model ⇒ exactly one handoff injected (no accumulation across cascade steps).

## Options

1. Keep the current contract (status quo; cost stays).
2. Gate generation (not injection) on `i === 0` — inject the existing summary but skip generating a *new* one from a fallback step.
3. Full `i === 0` gate as proposed in #12227 (requires changing the pinned contract test with an explicit rationale).
4. Make it configurable (the `UNIVERSAL_CONTEXT_HANDOFF_ENABLED` flag from #12167 already gives a global kill-switch; a narrower per-combo knob could target just the fallback path).

Owner call. Credit to @hartmark for surfacing the measurement and the proposal.

title: fix(nodejs): connection delete takes 4–12s when the DB falls back to the sql.js WASM driver

labels.name: needs-info
labels.description: Issue needs more information from reporter

body:
## Environment
- Branch: **`release/v3.8.51`** (latest) @ `073b98462`
- OS: Windows 11, Node **v24.18.0**, **`npm run dev`** (Turbopack), DB **101 MB** (`~/.omniroute/storage.sqlite`)
- Reported from fork `chirag127/OmniRoute`

## Symptom
Deleting a provider connection from the dashboard (Delete → confirm) takes **4–12+ seconds** before the row disappears. Users on `npm run dev` experience this on every delete; the UI feels hung.

## Measured evidence (live dev-server request log)
```
DELETE /api/providers/<id>   200 in 12.5s   (next.js: 7.9s, proxy.ts: 4.6s, application-code: 28ms)
DELETE /api/provider-nodes/… 200 in  4.4s   (first call for this route)
DELETE /api/provider-nodes/… 200 in   70ms  (same route, already compiled)
```
- `next.js:` time = **Turbopack on-demand route compilation** (first use of each route per server run).
- `proxy.ts:` time = **real handler work** (4.6s for a connection delete) — this happens on every delete, compiled or not.

## Root-cause breakdown
1. **Dev: Turbopack first-compile** — the DELETE route compiles on first use (~3–8s). One-time per server start, but it's the first thing a user hits when testing deletes.
2. **Dev: better-sqlite3 fails to load** — `[DB] Sync driver 'better-sqlite3' failed to open: Cannot find module as expression is too dynamic`; the app falls back to **sql.js WASM**, where every write re-serializes the **entire in-memory DB (101 MB)** to disk via `sqljsAdapter.persist()`. A connection delete triggers several writes (transaction + model cleanup + reorder + backup) → seconds each.
3. **Prod-agnostic: `backupDbFile("pre-write")`** runs synchronously in `deleteProviderConnection` (`src/lib/db/providers/deletion.ts`) — a full-file backup on every delete (throttled, but still a full copy when it fires), plus `cleanupProviderModelsAfterConnectionDelete`, `reorderConnections`, and `syncToCloudIfEnabled` all run inside the request before the response is sent.

## Suggested fixes
- Fix/route-around the dev-only `better-sqlite3` "too dynamic" failure so dev uses the native driver (this alone removes the per-write full-DB serialization).
- Defer or offload `backupDbFile("pre-write")` and model cleanup so the DELETE response isn't blocked on them (respond first, clean up in background).
- The `.build/next` dev cache purge (see #12297) also avoids recompiling routes on stale caches.

title: fix(providers): dashboard shows stale data after deleting custom providers/models until a full page reload
body:
## Environment
- Branch: **`release/v3.8.51`** (latest release branch) @ `073b98462`
- OS: Windows 11, Node **v24.18.0**, dev mode (Turbopack); reported from fork `chirag127/OmniRoute`

## Symptom
After deleting a **custom (OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible) provider** or its models from the dashboard, the UI does not refresh — the deleted provider/model keeps showing until a **manual full page reload**.

Repro (provider level):
1. Add a custom OpenAI-compatible provider, open its detail page (`/dashboard/providers/<id>`).
2. Click **Delete** (header action) → `DELETE /api/provider-nodes/<id>`.
3. The app calls `router.push("/dashboard/providers")`.
4. The Providers list still shows the deleted provider until F5.

## What I verified
- Server-side deletion is correct: I live-tested model delete on a running instance — `POST /api/provider-models` → `GET` shows the model → `DELETE` returns `{"removed":true,...}` → subsequent `GET` no longer contains it. So the stale data is a **client-side refresh gap**, not a broken delete API.

## Suspected root cause (client-side)
1. **Providers list page** — `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/providers/page.tsx` loads all data exactly once in `useEffect(..., [])` via `loadProviderPageData()` and has **no refetch-on-focus, no polling, no `router.refresh`** hook. Deleting a provider from the detail page (`components/CompatibleNodeCard.tsx`) does `router.push("/dashboard/providers")` **without `router.refresh()`**, so a soft navigation back to the previously-cached list can render the deleted provider.
2. **Provider detail models list** — `ProviderModelsSection` renders from a `models` `useMemo` over `syncedAvailableModels` + `modelMeta.customModels`; after model deletes, `onModelsChanged` → `fetchProviderModelMeta()` refetches both, but the refresh is skipped if any step in the delete chain fails silently (e.g. the alias-delete path in `useProviderModels.handleDeleteAlias`), leaving rows visible.

## Suggested fix
- Call `router.refresh()` after provider-node deletion, and/or make the Providers list page re-fetch on window focus / route refocus (or use a shared invalidation signal).
- In the model-delete chain, always run the list refetch in a `finally`-style path so a failed alias delete can't suppress the models refresh.

title: feat(startup): purge stale Turbopack dev cache when known app routes 404 after a dev-server restart

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Tracked for future work; not blocking

body:
## Environment
- Branch: **`release/v3.8.51`** (latest release branch, fully synced with upstream) @ `073b98462`
- OS: Windows 11, Node **v24.18.0**, `npm run dev` (Turbopack dev mode)
- Reported from fork `chirag127/OmniRoute`

## Symptom
After the dev server has run once, is stopped, and a new instance is started, a **subset of dashboard routes 404** — while other routes keep working. In our case every `/dashboard/settings/*` sub-route returned 404:

| Route | Result |
|---|---|
| `/dashboard/settings/general` | **404** |
| `/dashboard/settings/security` | **404** |
| `/dashboard/settings/appearance` | **404** |
| `/dashboard/settings/advanced` | **404** |
| `/dashboard/settings` | 200 |
| `/dashboard/providers`, `/dashboard/logs`, `/dashboard` | 200 |

Note: unauthenticated requests to the 404-ing routes **307-redirect to `/login`** (so the route is matched by the auth layout), but after a successful login the same URL returns **404**.

## Root cause
The Turbopack **persistent dev cache** at `.build/next/dev/cache/turbopack` (4.1 GB) was last written at 12:25, while the dev server serving the 404s had started at 17:45 — i.e. a newer server instance read a **stale/corrupted persistent cache**. The main `app-paths-manifest.json` (also from 12:25) *did* contain the settings routes, but per-route compiled artifacts were inconsistent, so route matching partially failed.

**Purging `.build/next/dev/cache/turbopack` and restarting the dev server resolves it completely** — every route returns 200.

## Relation to #6289
This is the same Turbopack persistent-cache corruption class as #6289, but a **different manifestation**: instead of the startup crash (`os error 1455` / misleading "Module not found"), it surfaces as **silent 404s on a subset of routes**. `scripts/dev/turbopackCacheHeal.mjs` only purges on the startup crash signature, so this mode is not detected.

## Repro
1. `npm run dev` (Turbopack), visit several dashboard routes.
2. Stop the server.
3. Start `npm run dev` again.
4. Visit `/dashboard/settings/general` → 404 (even with a valid session).

## Suggested fix
In the dev launcher, detect "known app routes returning 404 at startup" (e.g. compare requested route against the compiled app-paths manifest + source tree) and purge the Turbopack cache, or invalidate the persistent cache when the route manifest is older than the source files it maps.

title: fix(startup): "Invalid regular expression flags" crash right after STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY generation on first run
body:
### Description
A user on the Discord (EN) support channel reported a crash right after first-run bootstrap generates the storage encryption key:

```
omniroute
  📋 Loaded env from /usr/lib/node_modules/omniroute/.env
  ✨ Generated STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY in /root/.omniroute/.env
✖ Invalid regular expression flags
❯ ✖ Invalid regular expression flags
```

`"Invalid regular expression flags"` is a native V8/`SyntaxError` thrown by `new RegExp(pattern, flags)` when constructing a regex with an unsupported/invalid flags string — not a string that exists literally anywhere in this codebase (checked `src/`, `open-sse/`, `bin/`), so this is likely either a transitive dependency behavior triggered by an environment value, or a Node/V8 version mismatch (other reports in the same channel around the same time also involved unsupported Node versions, e.g. v23.7.0 outside the `>=22.22.2 <23 || >=24.0.0 <27` supported range — see `AGENTS.md` → Environment).

### Missing info (needed before this can be worked)
- `node -v` output
- Operating System + OS version
- Full command that was run (npm global install? npx? which package manager?)
- Whether it happens on a fresh `DATA_DIR` every time, or only once

### Status
This is a tracking issue opened from the support mesh pending the reporter's environment details — not yet reproduced locally.

title: fix(resilience): ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED 503 on round-robin combos returns no per-target diagnostics
body:
Title: [BUG] `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` 503 hides pre-dispatch rejection reasons after local queue-expiration failures

## Summary

OmniRoute intermittently returns HTTP 503 for a configured combo with the message:

```text
Service temporarily unavailable: all targets were skipped by pre-dispatch filters
```

The request reaches OmniRoute successfully through Traefik. The failure occurs inside combo routing. Server-side evidence shows that the 503s frequently follow a 504 caused by OmniRoute's local rate-limit execution expiration for the same combo target. However, the final 503 does not identify which targets were filtered, which filters rejected them, or whether the preceding 504/cooldown state caused the remaining targets to be skipped.

This report is based on a live Docker deployment and redacts credentials, API keys, email addresses, request bodies, and sensitive identifiers.

## Environment

- Repository: https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute
- OmniRoute package version inside the running container: `3.8.50`
- Docker image: `diegosouzapw/omniroute:latest`
- Image digest: `sha256:085c57adf499a8aaa9f35ccde95c0df9c11bd9ecd18d6c9edbf3b68b8079ba9d`
- Image build timestamp reported by Docker: `2026-08-27T03:51:02.735635887Z`
- Container command: `node dev/run-standalone.mjs`
- Entrypoint: `/app/check-permissions.sh`
- Node.js: `v26.7.0`
- Next.js: `16.3.1`
- Host OS: Linux kernel `6.8.0-138-generic`
- Storage: SQLite at `/app/data/storage.sqlite`
- Redis: `redis:8.10.1-alpine`
- OmniRoute container status during collection: healthy
- Container restart count: `0`
- Container OOM-killed: `false`
- Container memory limit: unlimited; observed usage was approximately `893 MiB`

## Client configuration

Hermes uses an OpenAI-compatible custom provider:

```yaml
model:
  default: devops-good
  provider: custom
  base_url: https://omniroute.w.k8sforfun.com/v1
```

The API key is supplied through an environment variable and is omitted here.

The failing request is sent to:

```text
POST https://omniroute.w.k8sforfun.com/v1/chat/completions
model: devops-good
```

The reported client context was approximately `239,580` tokens, while Hermes displayed approximately `294K/872K` (`34%`).

## Deployment configuration

The OmniRoute Compose project is `/opt/services/omniroute`.

Services:

- `omniroute`: `diegosouzapw/omniroute:latest`, internal port `20128`
- `omniroute_redis`: `redis:8.10.1-alpine`, internal port `6379`
- `omniroute_export_proxy`: `nginx:1.27-alpine`, internal port `8080`

The OmniRoute service uses:

```yaml
PORT=20128
DASHBOARD_PORT=20128
API_PORT=20129
LIVE_WS_PORT=20132
NODE_ENV=production
REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
BASE_URL=https://omniroute.w.k8sforfun.com
NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://omniroute.w.k8sforfun.com
CLOUD_URL=https://cloud.omniroute.online
NEXT_PUBLIC_CLOUD_URL=https://cloud.omniroute.online
AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE=true
REQUIRE_API_KEY=false
DATA_DIR=/app/data
OMNIROUTE_MEMORY_MB=1024
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=1024
```

Secret-bearing variables were present but are redacted from this report, including the storage encryption key, JWT secret, API-key secret, initial password, and authentication-related values.

The service is attached to external Docker networks `web_net` and `app_net`. Redis is attached only to `app_net`. The application has a named volume `omniroute_data` mounted at `/app/data`.

The Compose file passed:

```text
docker compose -f /opt/services/omniroute/docker-compose.yml config --no-interpolate
```

## Traefik configuration

Traefik routes the public hostname to the OmniRoute container using the Docker provider:

```text
Host(`omniroute.w.k8sforfun.com`)
entrypoint: web-secure
TLS: enabled
service: omniroute
backend port: 20128
Docker network: web_net
```

Traefik is configured with:

```text
--log.level=INFO
--providers.docker=true
--providers.docker.exposedbydefault=false
--providers.docker.network=web_net
--providers.file.directory=/etc/traefik/dynamic
--providers.file.watch=true
--entryPoints.web.address=:80
--entryPoints.web-secure.address=:443
--entryPoints.web-secure.http.tls=true
```

The application endpoint is reachable and returns an OmniRoute application response. No Traefik `502` or backend connectivity failure was observed for the failing requests. Traefik logs contained unrelated ACME TLS-ALPN errors for other domains, but no OmniRoute backend error corresponding to these 503s.

The Nginx sidecar only handles `/api/db-backups/exportAll` and is not involved in `/v1/chat/completions`.

## `devops-good` combo configuration

The active SQLite configuration contains this combo:

```json
{
  "name": "devops-good",
  "strategy": "round-robin",
  "models": [
    {
      "model": "codex/gpt-5.6-sol",
      "providerId": "codex",
      "connectionId": "<redacted>",
      "label": "<redacted>"
    },
    {
      "model": "codex/gpt-5.6-sol-high",
      "providerId": "codex",
      "connectionId": "<redacted>",
      "label": "<redacted>"
    },
    {
      "model": "antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high",
      "providerId": "antigravity",
      "connectionId": "<redacted>",
      "label": "<redacted>"
    }
  ],
  "config": {
    "maxRetries": 1,
    "retryDelayMs": 750,
    "concurrencyPerModel": 3,
    "handoffThreshold": 0.85,
    "handoffModel": "",
    "maxMessagesForSummary": 30,
    "trackMetrics": true,
    "reasoningTokenBufferEnabled": true,
    "compressionMode": "standard",
    "zeroLatencyOptimizationsEnabled": false
  }
}
```

At collection time, provider connection state was:

- `antigravity`: active, OAuth, `test_status=active`
- `codex`: inactive, OAuth, `test_status=expired`, `error_code=unrecoverable_refresh_error`
- Other active connections existed for providers including OpenRouter, NVIDIA, Nara, Bluesky/Bluesminds, AgentRouter, and AGY; they are not members of `devops-good`.

## Observed successful and failed requests

The same combo successfully dispatched to Antigravity before and after failures:

```text
2026-09-01T10:17:06Z  HTTP 200  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high  tokens_in=285471
2026-09-01T10:17:20Z  HTTP 200  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high  tokens_in=289092
2026-09-01T10:17:44Z  HTTP 200  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high  tokens_in=290815
2026-09-01T10:25:14Z  HTTP 200  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high  tokens_in=293896
2026-09-01T11:54:58Z  HTTP 200  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high  tokens_in=1736
```

This demonstrates that a context around 290K tokens can succeed through the configured Antigravity target. It does not prove every target accepts that context, but it makes a simple global context-limit explanation insufficient.

The failing requests were recorded by OmniRoute's SQLite `call_logs` table:

```text
2026-09-01T10:18:50.684Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:18:53.997Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:18:58.634Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:19:02.411Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:19:05.602Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:19:11.784Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:23:25.826Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:23:29.716Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:23:35.444Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:25:38.935Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:25:41.016Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:30:43.190Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:30:46.311Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:30:51.870Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
```

For these 503 records, OmniRoute stored:

```text
error_summary=[503] Service temporarily unavailable: all targets were skipped by pre-dispatch filters
tokens_in=0
tokens_out=0
detail_state=ready
has_request_body=1
has_response_body=0
```

Representative correlation IDs:

```text
bdf1e572-9139-4526-b466-cfa778a9b010
0d26d3d4-f457-4d32-8e32-d1b079326e1e
c6f4aa2e-a004-4fce-a2a7-32973699db6d
3f22b982-772a-4f86-9aec-7aa5bdf16362
```

## Important preceding errors

Several 503s were preceded by a target-level 504 for the same combo. OmniRoute recorded:

```text
Request exceeded OmniRoute's local rate-limit execution expiration
(legacy resilienceSettings.requestQueue.maxWaitMs=15000ms)
for antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high.
Bottleneck applies this deadline only after dispatch; it does not bound queue wait
and is not an upstream-generated timeout.
```

Examples:

```text
2026-09-01T10:15:21.189Z  HTTP 504  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high
2026-09-01T10:15:21.219Z  HTTP 503  devops-good

2026-09-01T10:25:37.765Z  HTTP 504  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high
2026-09-01T10:25:37.796Z  HTTP 504  devops-good
2026-09-01T10:25:38.935Z  HTTP 503  devops-good
2026-09-01T10:25:41.016Z  HTTP 503  devops-good
```

The container logs also show the following routing state immediately before a later successful request:

```text
Combo "devops-good" [round-robin] with 3 models
antigravity selection candidates model=gemini-3.1-pro-high: active=1, excluded=0, modelLocked=0, familyLocked=0, eligible=1
Combo context limit: 1048576 (source=target)
antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high succeeded
```

This indicates that OmniRoute can resolve a 1,048,576-token target context limit for this combo and that the target is normally eligible. The failure therefore appears state-dependent, rather than a permanent invalid model mapping.

## Relevant container log excerpts

Normal successful dispatch:

```text
[HTTP] POST /v1/chat/completions | devops-good | 2 msgs
[CHAT] Combo "devops-good" [round-robin] with 3 models
[AUTH] antigravity selection candidates model=gemini-3.1-pro-high: active=1, excluded=0, modelLocked=0, familyLocked=0, eligible=1
[CONTEXT] Combo context limit: 1048576 (source=target)
[ProxyEgress] antigravity status=success
[COMBO-RR] antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high succeeded
```

Other traffic demonstrated the relevant resilience behavior:

```text
[OPENCODE] Rate limited (429) ... rotating to next
[AUTH] Egress-bucketed cooldown ... cooled ... for 3s
[COMBO] All models failed ...
```

The logs do not emit an equivalent per-target diagnostic for the `devops-good` 503 path. In particular, they do not show the candidate list, filter name, filter result, or rejection reason for each target at the point where the final `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` response is generated.

## Reproduction pattern

1. Configure a combo with multiple targets, including at least one target whose provider connection is expired/inactive and one active target.
2. Send a large OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` request through the combo.
3. Generate enough concurrent traffic or queue pressure for the active target to hit the local `requestQueue.maxWaitMs=15000ms` execution expiration.
4. Retry the same combo request while the target/cooldown/resilience state is active.
5. Observe that OmniRoute may return:

```text
HTTP 503
Service temporarily unavailable: all targets were skipped by pre-dispatch filters
```

The exact filter responsible is not visible in the response or ordinary INFO logs.

## Expected behavior

When no target survives pre-dispatch filtering, OmniRoute should either:

- return structured diagnostic metadata containing every candidate and the rejection reason; or
- emit a correlated log entry containing the candidate, provider, model, connection ID (redacted), filter name, reason, cooldown/expiry time, and context estimate.

For example:

```text
Pre-dispatch candidate evaluation:

Target: codex/gpt-5.6-sol
Result: rejected
Filter: connection_state
Reason: connection inactive; test_status=expired

Target: antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high
Result: rejected
Filter: cooldown_or_queue
Reason: local execution expiration or active cooldown

Final result: ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED
```

## Questions

1. What exact pre-dispatch filters can produce `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` in v3.8.50?
2. Does a prior local queue-expiration 504 place a target into a state that causes subsequent requests to be skipped before dispatch?
3. Can an inactive/expired connection remain in a combo and contribute to an `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` result without being logged as a candidate rejection?
4. How are `connectionId`, provider ID, model ID, cooldown state, and target context limits used when evaluating combo targets?
5. Does the final 503 intentionally collapse target-level 504, inactive-connection, cooldown, rate-limit, and context-limit reasons into the same error?
6. Is there a debug setting, API endpoint, trace ID, or database record that exposes the per-target pre-dispatch decisions?
7. Can the response include a safe redacted `recovery` object with filter names and retry timing?
8. Is this behavior fixed in a release after `3.8.50`?
9. Are there known interactions between `maxRetries`, `concurrencyPerModel`, local queue expiration, and pre-dispatch cooldowns for large requests?

## Additional implementation suggestion

When the final candidate pool is empty, preserve the existing generic message for compatibility but add structured diagnostics in debug mode and a correlation ID in the response. For example:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED",
    "message": "Service temporarily unavailable: all targets were skipped by pre-dispatch filters",
    "correlation_id": "...",
    "targets": [
      {
        "provider": "codex",
        "model": "gpt-5.6-sol",
        "filter": "connection_state",
        "reason": "connection inactive or expired"
      },
      {
        "provider": "antigravity",
        "model": "gemini-3.1-pro-high",
        "filter": "cooldown_or_queue",
        "reason": "local queue execution expiration/cooldown active",
        "retry_after_ms": 0
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Sensitive credentials, request bodies, API keys, account emails, and full connection identifiers should remain excluded or hashed.

## Conclusion

Traefik and Docker reachability do not appear to be the cause. OmniRoute is healthy, accepts the request, and can successfully dispatch the same `devops-good` combo and approximately 290K-token requests to `antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high`.

The live evidence instead shows repeated final `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` responses with zero dispatched input tokens, often following a local queue-expiration 504. The main defect is the absence of target-level diagnostics, which prevents determining whether the final empty pool is caused by cooldown, queue state, inactive combo members, context filtering, rate limiting, or another pre-dispatch condition.

Please advise how to obtain the exact per-target filter decisions and whether the current behavior is expected or fixed in a newer release.

title: feat(backend): baseline the restored circular-deps gate (154) and untangle the db/settings spine

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Tracked for future work; not blocking

labels.name: quality-gate-finding
labels.description: Surfaced by the new quality gates (PR #3471), frozen in an allowlist pending fix

body:
## Context

`npm run check:circular-deps` was crashing instead of running. `scripts/check/check-circular-deps.mjs` invoked `node node_modules/.bin/dpdm`, but that path is an **npm shell wrapper**, not a JS entrypoint:

```
$ npm run check:circular-deps
basedir=$(dirname "$(echo "$0" | sed -e 's,\\,/,g')")
          ^^^^^^^
SyntaxError: missing ) after argument list
[circular-deps] ERROR running dpdm: Command failed: node .../node_modules/.bin/dpdm ...
exit 1
```

Fixed in #11615 (`f5e70950d38f`) by pointing `DPDM_BIN` at `node_modules/dpdm/lib/bin/dpdm.js`. Thanks @benzntech for spotting it.

## Why nobody noticed

Two reasons stacked:

1. The gate is **advisory in CI** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `quality-extended`, step `Circular deps (dpdm; advisory)` carries `continue-on-error: true`. The crash never turned a run red.
2. The script itself **exits 0** regardless of the count — it only prints a baseline suggestion. So even a working run is non-blocking.

The sibling gate `npm run check:cycles` (`scripts/check/check-cycles.mjs`) has always been green, which made the area look healthy. It isn't a contradiction — it's a different scope. `check-cycles` walks a fixed set of directory roots (`src/shared/components`, `src/lib/db`, `src/lib/compliance`, `open-sse/translator`, `open-sse/mcp-server`) with its own Tarjan SCC pass, so it only sees edges whose endpoints are both inside those roots. `check-circular-deps` runs dpdm transitively from 4 pipeline entrypoints (`open-sse/handlers/chatCore.ts`, `open-sse/services/combo.ts`, `open-sse/mcp-server/index.ts`, `src/lib/db/core.ts`) across the whole graph. Most of the cycles below route through `src/lib/config/runtimeSettings.ts` and `src/lib/tokenHealthCheck.ts`, which sit outside `check-cycles`' roots — invisible to it by construction.

## What the gate reports now

On `release/v3.8.51` with the fix applied:

```
[circular-deps] circularDeps=154
[circular-deps] Advisory — add to quality-baseline.json: { "value": 154, "direction": "down" }
```

Modules appearing most often as a node in a cycle (occurrences across the 154 chains):

| count | module |
|---:|---|
| 119 | `src/lib/db/settings.ts` |
| 115 | `src/lib/db/providers.ts` |
| 107 | `src/lib/config/runtimeSettings.ts` |
| 103 | `src/lib/tokenHealthCheck.ts` |
| 103 | `src/lib/db/readCache.ts` |
| 103 | `src/lib/db/providers/deletion.ts` |
| 91 | `open-sse/services/combo/nativeCodexTurnPin.ts` |
| 85 | `open-sse/services/combo/quotaExhaustionCutoff.ts` |
| 83 | `open-sse/services/combo/quotaStrategies.ts` |
| 80 | `src/domain/quotaCache.ts` |
| 75 | `src/lib/db/models/modelCatalogWriteSignals.ts` |
| 73 | `src/shared/utils/featureFlags.ts` |
| 73 | `src/lib/db/featureFlags.ts` |
| 73 | `open-sse/services/usage.ts` |
| 65 | `src/lib/piiSanitizer.ts` |

The dominant cluster is one spine repeated in ~100 of the 154 chains:

```
src/lib/db/readCache.ts
  -> src/lib/db/settings.ts
  -> src/lib/config/runtimeSettings.ts
  -> src/lib/tokenHealthCheck.ts
  -> src/lib/db/providers.ts
  -> src/lib/db/providers/{deletion,codexAccountState,migrations,nodes,rateLimit}.ts
```

with a second, shorter feeder through `src/lib/piiSanitizer.ts -> src/shared/utils/featureFlags.ts -> src/lib/db/featureFlags.ts -> src/lib/db/models/modelCatalogWriteSignals.ts -> src/lib/db/readCache.ts`. Breaking the `settings.ts <-> runtimeSettings.ts <-> tokenHealthCheck.ts <-> providers.ts` knot would collapse the large majority of the count at once.

Smaller independent clusters worth separate passes:

- `open-sse/services/alibabaFreeTier.ts -> alibabaFreeTierDiscovery.ts -> alibabaFreeTierQuotaFetcher.ts -> alibabaFreeTierQuotaClassify.ts`
- `open-sse/mcp-server/server.ts <-> catalog.ts` and `server.ts <-> radarCatalog.ts`
- `src/lib/db/quotaPools.ts <-> src/lib/quota/quotaCombos.ts <-> quotaKey.ts`
- `src/lib/plugins/hooks.ts <-> src/lib/plugins/manager.ts`
- `src/lib/kimi/tokenRefresh.ts <-> open-sse/executors/kimi-web.ts`

## Proposed next steps

1. **Freeze 154 as a down-ratchet** in `config/quality/quality-baseline.json` (`{ "value": 154, "direction": "down" }`, exactly what the script suggests) so the number can only improve. This is the cheap, immediate win: it stops the count from silently growing again now that the gate can actually see it.
2. **Decide whether the step should stay `continue-on-error: true`.** Once a baseline exists, the ratchet is what would block, not the raw count — the current double non-blocking (step-level `continue-on-error` **and** the script's unconditional exit 0) means a regression still can't fail CI.
3. Chip at the `db/settings <-> config/runtimeSettings <-> tokenHealthCheck <-> db/providers` spine first — it is the single highest-leverage target.

Reproduce with:

```bash
npm run check:circular-deps
```

Not urgent and not a runtime defect — ESM tolerates these cycles at import time. Filing it so the newly-restored signal doesn't get lost.

title: fix(resilience): auto/coding collapses to the 200k-context target and fails with context_length_exceeded instead of the 1M model

labels.name: keep-open
labels.description: Ongoing community thread — exclude from stale auto-close

body:
## Summary
When a session routed through `auto/coding` exceeds ~200k input tokens, OmniRoute's request-compatibility filter collapses the model pool to a **single target: `oc/mimo-v2.5-free` (200k window)**. The request then fails with `context_length_exceeded` because the input (200,685–200,833 tokens) exceeds the model's 200k limit. Meanwhile, `oc/nemotron-3-ultra-free` (1M context) exists in the same provider and would handle the request, but it's dropped by the filter.

## Root Cause (from log analysis)
1. Request arrives: `POST /v1/messages | auto/coding | 340 msgs | 30 tools` (~200,724 estimated input tokens)
2. `Virtual auto-combo created: auto/coding (1 candidates)` → `Combo "auto/coding" [auto] with 8 models`
3. `Auto selection: oc/big-pickle | intent=medium task=default | strategy=lkgp | LKGP: using last known good provider opencode`
4. **`Context-aware fallback: kept 1/8 targets for request requirements`** ← filter output
5. `Trying model 1/1: oc/mimo-v2.5-free`
6. `Combo context limit: 200000 (source=target)`
7. `Input exceeds maximum input tokens for opencode/mimo-v2.5-free: estimated 200724 input tokens, max input 200000`
8. `Input-bound request failure from oc/mimo-v2.5-free — aborting combo (same input will fail identically on every account)`
9. Claude Code retries: `auto/coding:reliable` (same single target, same failure) → `auto/best-coding` (Invalid auto prefix format) → `auto/best-coding-fast` (Invalid auto prefix format) → surfaces raw `context_length_exceeded`

## Key Evidence
- **`oc/nemotron-3-ultra-free` has a 1M context window** (advertised by `/v1/models`)
- The filter kept only 1 of 8 targets. `context_window` is NOT in `HARD_COMPAT_REASONS`, so context-rejected models should stay in `compatible`. The fact that `compatible.length === 1` means **7 targets had a hard failure** (`tools`, `vision`, `structured_output`, or `output_tokens`).
- The same 8 models work fine for smaller requests (no "kept" log line → pool returned unchanged).
- Uncovered path adjacent to PR #12189 (liveness-aware readiness + auto model echo).

## Failing Log Excerpt
\`\`\`
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:58:59.857Z","tag":"COMBO","msg":"auto with nested resolution: 8 total targets"}
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:58:59.885Z","tag":"COMBO","msg":"Auto selection: oc/big-pickle | intent=medium task=default | strategy=lkgp | LKGP: using last known good provider opencode"}
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:58:59.894Z","tag":"COMBO","msg":"Context-aware fallback: kept 1/8 targets for request requirements"}
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:58:59.895Z","tag":"COMBO","msg":"Trying model 1/1: oc/mimo-v2.5-free"}
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:59:00.044Z","tag":"CONTEXT","msg":"Combo context limit: 200000 (source=target)"}
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:59:00.061Z","tag":"CONTEXT","msg":"Input exceeds maximum input tokens for opencode/mimo-v2.5-free: estimated 200685 input tokens, max input 200000"}
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:59:00.063Z","tag":"COMBO","msg":"Input-bound request failure from oc/mimo-v2.5-free — aborting combo (same input will fail identically on every account)"}
\`\`\`

## Expected Behavior
For inputs >200k tokens, `auto/coding` should retain `oc/nemotron-3-ultra-free` (or any model with adequate context) in the fallback pool, not collapse to the smallest-context model.

## Affected Areas (likely)
- `open-sse/services/combo/comboStructure.ts` — `filterTargetsByRequestCompatibility`, `getTargetCompatibilityFailures`
- `open-sse/services/combo/contextOverrideGate.ts` — context-limit evaluation
- `open-sse/services/autoCombo/virtualFactory.ts` / `engine.ts` — candidate pool assembly

## Possible Solutions
1. **Investigate the hard-reject reason**: surface per-target reject reasons (currently only the kept count is logged at info level; reject reasons only at debug) to identify why 7/8 targets are hard-rejected on large requests.
2. **Fix the filter** so a `context_window`-only rejection never removes the last fallback, and so the largest-context compatible model is retained for oversized inputs.
3. **Add `context_length_exceeded` as a soft (fallback-eligible) reason** for heterogeneous pools, so a bigger-context sibling can catch the request (the code comment in `combo.ts` says this path exists for heterogeneous combos — it's just not being reached because the pool has already collapsed to 1).

## Reproduction
Run a long-running Claude Code session (300+ messages, ~200k+ tokens) through OmniRoute with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:20128` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=auto/coding`. Session dies with `context_length_exceeded` instead of routing to the 1M-context model.

## Related
- PR #12189 (merged) — fixed liveness and model echo.
- Workspace: `opensource-elearning/omniroute-fixes`

title: feat(memory): integrate turbovec vector store backend
body:
## Summary & Abstract

This pull request introduces a highly optimized, research-backed vector store tier into the OmniRoute memory system: **Turbovec** (based on Google Research's TurboQuant algorithm). 

Currently, OmniRoute's context retention relies on `sqlite-vec` (local) or Qdrant (remote/container). While `sqlite-vec` is highly portable, embedding heavy project files and long-lived agent memories locally scales linearly in RAM usage (Float32). To resolve this without forcing operators to host an external Qdrant container, this PR natively bridges Turbovec into the V8 runtime via N-API.

## Architectural Changes & Implementation Details

### 1. Zero-Overhead Native Rust Bridge (`packages/turbovec-node`)
- Scaffolded a zero-overhead Node API (N-API) binding mapping the Node.js execution cycle directly to the Rust `turbovec` crate.
- By binding `IdMapIndex` into JS/TS via `@node-rs/helper`, we allow Node.js to directly dispatch vector operations to underlying processor SIMD intrinsics (NEON on ARM; AVX-512/VNNI on x86) entirely bypassing V8 Garbage Collection latency.

### 2. State Mapping & Synchronization (`src/lib/memory/store.ts`)
- **Deterministic ID Mapping:** Turbovec requires `u64` numeric stable IDs. We structurally mapped SQLite's implicit integer `rowid` (`id` -> `BIGINT rowid`) to map directly to the Turbovec engine.
- Parallelized memory block upserts `upsertTurbovecPoint` and removals `deleteTurbovecPoint`. Data is natively synchronized incrementally to disk (`.tvim` format), ensuring crash safety without continuous block rebuilds.

### 3. Retrieval Engine Integration (`src/lib/memory/retrieval.ts`)
- Substituted the semantic retrieval execution loop to actively resolve queries using Turbovec when the engine is toggled. 
- Integrated the L2-distance / inner-product scoring output from the SIMD module into OmniRoute's standard RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) hybrid pipeline, guaranteeing that FTS5 keyword hits combine perfectly with Turbovec's dense vector ranks.

### 4. Policy Configuration & Schema Expansion (`src/shared/schemas/memory.ts`)
- Extended the `z.enum` bounds structurally for `vectorStore` arrays (`sqlite-vec`, `qdrant`, `turbovec`, `auto`), validating strict type compliance for the UI Engine tab (`MemoryEngineStatusSchema`) and API configuration.

## Projected Achievements (Performance Gains)

Integrating this architecture immediately unlocks several aggressive thresholds for OmniRoute installations:

1. **Extreme Memory Compression (16x RAM Saving):** 
   TurboQuant forces deterministic statistical distribution across hyperspheres, mapping float32 vectors into 4-bit and 2-bit spaces natively. A theoretical corpus of 10M embeddings compresses from ~31 GB down to ~3 GB without accuracy destruction. Resolves Agent `FATAL ERROR` memory limitations out-of-the-box.
2. **Sub-millisecond Search (Zero Network Latency):** 
   Qdrant imposes 15ms-60ms network overhead per recall stage. Turbovec executes purely in-memory via the N-API bounds (sub-1ms execution paths), accelerating contextual injections for auto-combo routers.
3. **Training-Free Online Ingest:**
   Unlike FAISS PQ setups that require explicit batch training or rebuilding as history scales, the implemented `IdMapIndex` operates completely on edge and supports un-batched `addWithIds()` synchronously at near O(1) ingestion times.

## Validation & Reviews

- **Opt-in Only:** The default configuration aggressively maintains fallback bounds. Turbovec requires explicit Opt-in over `sqlite-vec`, avoiding breaking changes for ongoing instances.
- **Data Integrity:** Testing confirms that FFI execution catches errors properly via standard `log.warn(...)` without halting the core Next.js SSE streams.
- Contains no API overrides; relies on standard REST endpoints mapping directly exactly as implemented for Qdrant. 

---
_Ref: Based on "TurboQuant: Online Vector Quantization with Near-optimal Distortion Rate" (ICLR 2026)._

title: fix(sse): classify "N API calls / month" 429 text as quota_exhausted
body:
### Problem

`QUOTA_PATTERNS` in `src/shared/utils/classify429.ts` recognizes `monthly ... limit`, `monthly ... quota` and `per month ... limit`, but not the **reversed phrase order** providers actually use in trial-key messages.

Cohere's trial-key 429 reads:

```
You are using a Trial key, which is limited to 1000 API calls / month.
```

None of the existing patterns match that, so `classify429()` returns `rate_limit` instead of `quota_exhausted`. The caller then applies the generic short transient backoff to an allowance that will not reset until the next billing cycle, and the same key is retried every few seconds for the rest of the month.

### Evidence

Measured on a production instance over 24h against two Cohere trial connections: **481 of 752** 429s carried this exact text, and every one was treated as a short transient rate limit. The connections were never cooled for a meaningful window, so traffic kept being dispatched to a provider with no remaining monthly quota.

### Fix

Three additional patterns covering the reversed order and the `N calls / month` / `N requests/month` spellings:

```ts
/(?:api\s+)?calls?\s*\/\s*month/i,
/requests?\s*\/\s*month/i,
/limited\s+to\s+[\d,]+.*(?:calls?|requests?).*per\s+month/i,
```

They are deliberately narrow — each requires an explicit `month` token adjacent to a call/request noun — so ordinary per-minute or per-day rate-limit text is unaffected.

### Tests

Added `monthly call allowances classify as quota_exhausted regardless of phrase order`, covering both orders plus the verbatim Cohere string.

Verified TDD on this branch:

- **Before the fix** the new test fails: `Limited to 1000 API calls per month` → `actual: 'rate_limit', expected: 'quota_exhausted'`.
- **After the fix** `tests/unit/classify429.test.ts` is 31/31.

No regressions in the neighbouring quota/classification suites:

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `classify429` | 31/31 |
| `circuit-breaker-failure-kind` | 12/12 |
| `antigravity-429-quota-tdd` | 5/5 |
| `antigravity-429-quota-cooldown` | 13/13 |
| `cloudflare-ai-neuron-exhaustion-6980` | 11/11 |
| `egress-ip-lock-10880` | 17/17 |

Prettier clean on both changed files.

### Notes

Branched from `origin/release/v3.8.51` and targets that branch. No open `base-red` issue and no active `release-freeze` at the time of cutting.

The changelog fragment is added in a follow-up commit on this branch once the PR number is known, per `changelog.d/README.md`.

title: fix: extra upstream headers — invalid entry can't be deleted, reverts on blur
body:
## Report

A user reports that after accidentally adding an invalid entry under a provider's "Extra upstream headers" (they entered a full URL as the header *name* instead of a value), the dashboard fails to persist deletion of that entry:

> I accidentally added an invalid entry under "Extra upstream headers" for a provider (entered a full URL as the header name). When I click the delete icon or clear the text boxes, the dashboard fails to save the deletion and the invalid header keeps reverting on blur/close.

## Likely area

`upstreamHeaders` is stored as JSON on the model/provider-compat row (`src/lib/db/models.ts` — `readUpstreamFromJsonRecord` / `sanitizeUpstreamHeadersMap`, surfaced via `ModelCompatPopover.tsx` / `CustomModelsSection.tsx` under `dashboard/providers/[id]/components/`). The report describes a client-side state/sync bug: the delete action does not reach a successful save, or the popover's local draft re-hydrates the invalid value on blur/close before the delete is persisted.

## Ask

Needs reproduction: add a provider, add an "Extra upstream header" entry with an invalid/malformed name (e.g. a full URL), save, then attempt to delete it via the UI (delete icon and/or clearing both text boxes). Confirm whether the deletion is actually rejected server-side (validation blocking the save) or whether it's a pure client-side state bug (the popover keeps re-populating the old draft on blur).

No known workaround via the UI. Editing `storage.sqlite` directly while the server is running is not recommended (risk of corruption/lock contention) and is not something we can respons­ibly instruct a user to do casually.

title: fix(resilience): clear the combo LKGP pin only when it names the failed target
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #12013 (thanks @HouMinXi — the clearing itself is right, this only narrows *which* pin gets cleared).

#12013 clears the persisted LKGP pin from 13 call sites so a dead provider stops being re-pinned. None of them look at **which provider the pin names**, and the combo-level pin records whichever provider last *succeeded* — not necessarily the one failing now.

Under `lkgp` this is harmless: `applyStrategyOrdering` hoists the pinned target to index 0, so the pinned provider is always the first thing tried, and by the time anything else fails the pin either already refreshed or legitimately went stale.

Under **`auto` it is not**. `resolveAutoStrategy` reads the pin into `lastKnownGoodProvider` and feeds it to candidate *scoring* rather than hoisting it, so the pinned provider is not necessarily tried first. Skipping an unrelated target — a connection cooldown, a quota cutoff, an unavailable model — then discards a preference for a provider that never failed.

Measured on `63e4afa32`, same combo and same skip, only the strategy differing:

```
strategy=lkgp   pin after: {"provider":"felo"}   ← survives (felo hoisted first, succeeds)
strategy=auto   pin after: null                  ← destroyed
strategy=round-robin  pin after: null
```

In all three, `felo` is healthy and returns 200; the target that gets skipped is `opencode`.

This clears the combo-level pin only when it names the failed target's provider, and — when both sides carry one — its connection, so a sibling connection failing doesn't invalidate the pinned one. The target-scoped `executionKey` pin is still cleared unconditionally; that one is unambiguously about the target that just failed.

`failed` is optional, so a caller without a target in scope keeps the previous unconditional behaviour.

## Related Issues

- Refs #11911 (fixed by #12013; this narrows the clearing introduced there)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: routing (combo resilience)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint` — 21 problems on `open-sse/services/combo.ts`, **identical count on the base**; this adds none
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base (`63e4afa32`); focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR

The new test failed on `63e4afa32` before the fix.

The three tests #12013 added are the guard against over-narrowing, and they're what makes this safe — they pin the *same* provider that gets skipped, so they must keep passing. Mutation results:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| always clear (the pre-fix behaviour) | 1 fail — the new test |
| never clear the combo-level pin | 3 fail — all of #12013's tests |

So the guard can be neither too loose nor too tight without something going red.

```
tests/unit/lkgp-stale-pin-exhaustion-11911.test.ts
tests/unit/lkgp-enabled-context-11181.test.ts
tests/unit/delete-provider-connection-invalidates-lkgp-8887.test.ts
tests/unit/combo-stream-readiness-fallback.test.ts
tests/unit/combo/*.test.ts (12)
→ 139 tests, 139 pass, 0 fail
```

`npx tsc --noEmit` reports 0 errors for the touched files on the base and 0 with this change.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/lkgp-stale-pin-exhaustion-11911.test.ts` — 1 added: under `auto`, a pin naming healthy `felo` survives `opencode` being skipped. Added to #12013's own file so the LKGP behaviour stays described in one place.

## Coverage Notes

`open-sse/services/combo.ts` is the only production file changed, and both sides of the new branch are covered — the pin naming the failed provider (#12013's three tests) and naming a different one (the new test). Coverage does not move down in any touched file.

## Reviewer Notes

- The 13 call sites all now pass `target`, which they already had in scope; the change at each is one argument.
- Worth a second opinion on the connection-matching rule: I treat a pin as stale when the provider matches and *either* side lacks a `connectionId`. That deliberately errs toward clearing, so it stays closer to #12013's behaviour where the data is ambiguous.
- I reviewed the earlier #11914 and raised this same point there before it was closed; it didn't carry into #12013, and the call-site count went 2 → 13 in the meantime, which is what made it worth chasing down and measuring properly rather than leaving as a review comment.

title: fix(providers): opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna routed to /chat/completions, upstream serves it only on Responses
body:
**Version:** 3.8.50
**Provider:** opencode-go (API key connection)
**Platform:** Windows Server 2022, native install

## Summary

opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna is entitled and listed in /v1/models, but always fails through OmniRoute with [500]: Internal server error. The request is sent to the Go /chat/completions endpoint, but the Go upstream serves GPT-5.6 Luna only on the Responses API.

Same class of bug as #9942 (Copilot GPT-5.6 Terra/Luna), but on the opencode-go provider.

## Reproduction

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{"model":"opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly one word: pong"}],"max_completion_tokens":50}'

Result: {"error":{"message":"[opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna] [500]: Internal server error (reset after 3s)"}}

## Direct upstream verification (bypassing OmniRoute)

From the same server, same key:

# Chat Completions + luna → always 500
curl -s https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $GO_KEY" -d '{"model":"gpt-5.6-luna","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"pong"}],"max_completion_tokens":50}'
# → {"type":"error","error":{"type":"error","message":"Internal server error"}}

# Responses + luna → works
curl -s https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer $GO_KEY" -d '{"model":"gpt-5.6-luna","input":"pong","max_output_tokens":50}'
# → 200

# Control: Chat Completions + deepseek-v4-flash (same key) → 200

## Root cause

open-sse/config/providers/registry/opencode/go/index.ts does not include gpt-5.6-luna. The model is discovered via autoSync (dynamic catalog), so getModelTargetFormat returns null and the executor falls back to "openai" (Chat Completions).

The same repo already has targetFormat: "openai-responses" for:
- github provider: gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna
- opencode-go provider: deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash, muse-spark-1.2-contributor + effort tiers

But opencode-go gpt-5.6-luna is missing.

## DB override does not help

Writing modelCompatOverrides for opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna with targetFormat: "openai-responses" does not work: resolveOpencodeTargetFormat() in open-sse/executors/opencode.ts only consults the static registry, not DB overrides. The request body gets translated to Responses shape but is still sent to /chat/completions, so it still fails with 500.

## Fix

Add to open-sse/config/providers/registry/opencode/go/index.ts:

{
  id: "gpt-5.6-luna",
  name: "GPT-5.6 Luna",
  targetFormat: "openai-responses",
  supportsReasoning: true,
  maxOutputTokens: 128000,
},

Verified locally by patching the compiled dist chunks.

## Verification after local patch

POST /v1/chat/completions { model: "opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna", ... } → 200, content "pong"
Regression: opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash → 200, main/grok-4.6 → 200

## Reasoning effort passthrough (bonus finding)

reasoning_effort is correctly forwarded for both opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash and opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna — reasoning_tokens scales monotonically with effort level. The effort plumbing is healthy; the bug is purely endpoint routing.

## Follow-up: reasoning content blocks rejected by Go upstream

After the registry fix, luna works for simple requests. However, when a client replays conversation history that includes AI SDK-style reasoning content blocks ({type:"reasoning",text:"..."}) in assistant messages, the Go upstream rejects with:

[400]: [array_above_max_length] Invalid 'input[N].content': array too long. Expected an array with maximum length 0, but got an array with length 1 instead.

This is because openaiToOpenAIResponsesRequest passes type:"reasoning" content parts through verbatim into the Responses input[] array, but the Go upstream expects reasoning as standalone {type:"reasoning",content:[{type:"reasoning_text",text:"..."}],summary:[]} items, not as content parts inside a message.

A possible fix is to detect type:"reasoning" content parts in the translator and hoist them into standalone reasoning items, similar to how reasoning_content string fields are already handled.

title: fix(providers): Trae import-token connections fail with 401 from stale Referer/Origin/region defaults
body:
### OmniRoute Version
3.8.50

### Installation Method
Docker / Docker Compose

### Operating System
Linux (self-hosted VPS)

### Provider(s) Involved
Trae

### Client Tool
cURL / dashboard "Test" button

### Description
Trae connections created through the manual token-import flow (`flowType: "import_token"`, as documented in #3034) return `401` on every real request — including chat completions and the dashboard "Test" button — even when the imported `Cloud-IDE-JWT` is fresh and currently valid on the real Trae web client.

Comparing the request the `TraeExecutor` actually sends (`open-sse/executors/trae.ts`, `buildHeaders()`) against a `Copy as cURL` capture of a real authenticated request from the live web client, the executor's hardcoded header defaults no longer match what Trae's backend expects for the current international SOLO edition:

| Header | `buildHeaders()` (current code) | Real client (captured today) |
|---|---|---|
| `x-user-region` | `US` (or `providerSpecificData.userRegion`, which itself defaults to `"US"` on import — see `src/lib/oauth/providers/trae.ts`) | `SG` |
| `Referer` | `https://solo.trae.ai/` | `https://work.trae.ai/` |
| `Origin` | *(not sent at all)* | `https://work.trae.ai` |
| `x-trae-user-timezone` | *(not sent at all)* | `America/Recife` |

It looks like the product's web client moved from `solo.trae.ai` to `work.trae.ai` at some point, and the default `x-user-region` guess of `US` doesn't match this account's actual region (`SG`). Since the `Cloud-IDE-JWT` is session-scoped (decodes to `{"data":{"source":"session","source_id":"...","tenant_id":"...","type":"user"}}`), it's plausible the backend validates the request's `Origin`/`Referer` against the session's real origin and rejects mismatches — which would explain a clean 401 on an otherwise-valid, non-expired token.

This is distinct from #5650 / #6236 (Trae CN / multi-edition support) — this is the **default/current international SOLO edition** failing, not an unsupported edition.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Sign in at `https://work.trae.ai` (current SOLO web client).
2. Open DevTools → Network, send a chat message, find a request to `core-normal.trae.ai`, right-click → Copy as cURL. Note the `Authorization: Cloud-IDE-JWT <token>` value and the other headers (`origin`, `referer`, `x-user-region`, `x-trae-user-timezone`).
3. In OmniRoute, go to Providers → Trae → Import Token, paste the JWT (or import via `providers/claude-auth`-style JSON with `accessToken` set to the JWT).
4. Send a real chat completion through `/v1/chat/completions` with `model: "trae/auto"`, or click "Test" on the connection.

### Expected Behavior
The request authenticates successfully, same as the real web client does with the same token.

### Actual Behavior
```
[trae/auto] [502]: [401] {"code":1001,"message":"We're sorry, but we are not able to authenticate you. If you continue to experience issues, please contact our support team for assistance."}
```
This reproduces consistently across multiple fresh token imports (new JWT each time), so it isn't a one-off stale-token issue.

### Test Impact
Needs a new unit test

### Additional Context
The repo already has `scripts/ad-hoc/diag-trae-auth.mjs`, written to probe several `Authorization` header variants against `core-normal.trae.ai` — its own comments already suspect "the web client likely authenticates via a COOKIE, not a bearer header." From what I captured, the real client *does* use the `Authorization: Cloud-IDE-JWT <token>` header (so that part of `buildHeaders()` is correct) — but it also sends `Origin: https://work.trae.ai`, a matching `Referer`, and the account's real `x-user-region`/`x-trae-user-timezone`, none of which `diag-trae-auth.mjs`'s header variants include either (they only vary the `Authorization` header/scheme, not `Origin`/`Referer`/region). That's likely why every variant in that script fails too.

### Validation Plan

title: feat(providers): select and preserve a connection proxy before starting OAuth

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Tracked for future work; not blocking

body:
## Problem / Use Case

First of all, thank you for the substantial work already done on OmniRoute's proxy system. The Proxy Registry, provider/account assignments, OAuth proxy support, and connection-aware routing already provide a very useful foundation for managing multiple accounts with separate egress routes.

This request is intended as a small UX improvement built on top of that work, not as a complaint about the current implementation.

Today, a user who wants one OAuth account to keep the same proxy throughout its lifetime can already achieve it manually:

1. Temporarily assign the intended proxy at provider level.
2. Configure the browser with the same proxy.
3. Complete the OAuth flow.
4. Assign that proxy to the newly created connection/account.
5. Restore or remove the temporary provider-level assignment.

This works, but it is easy to forget one of the steps when connecting or re-authenticating multiple accounts. A forgotten temporary assignment may also affect the next connection unintentionally.

The goal is simply to make this existing workflow easier, more discoverable, and less error-prone.

## Proposed Solution

When the user clicks **Connect new account**, optionally show a proxy-selection step before OAuth begins:

```text
Connect new Codex account

Connection proxy:
  ○ Use current provider/default routing
  ○ Direct connection
  ● Use saved proxy: [Proxy 54 — US Residential ▼]

[ Test proxy ]  [ Continue ]
```

If a saved proxy is selected:

1. Keep that selection with the pending OAuth session.
2. Use it for the server-side OAuth requests where supported.
3. After authorization succeeds and the connection is created, automatically assign the same saved proxy to that connection.
4. During future re-authentication, preselect the connection's existing account-level proxy.

Users who do not need a dedicated connection proxy could continue using the current provider/global/default behavior without any additional configuration.

For strict configurations, an optional fail-closed behavior would also be helpful: if an explicitly selected connection proxy is unavailable, show a clear error rather than changing the egress route without the user's knowledge.

I understand that this is more than adding a dropdown: the selected proxy needs to be associated with the pending OAuth state before the final connection exists and then transferred safely to the resulting connection. This request is mainly about the desired user experience; the maintainers may have a better implementation approach.

## Alternatives Considered

The current provider-level workaround works, but requires temporary configuration changes before and after every OAuth connection or re-authentication. It is functional, but depends on the user remembering each step correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A user can optionally select a saved proxy before starting a new OAuth connection.
- [ ] Existing provider/global/default behavior remains available and unchanged for users who do not select one.
- [ ] The selected proxy is retained for the pending OAuth flow.
- [ ] After successful authorization, the created connection receives the same account-level proxy assignment automatically.
- [ ] Re-authentication preselects the proxy already assigned to the existing connection.
- [ ] Cancelled, failed, or expired OAuth flows clean up any temporary proxy association.
- [ ] The selected proxy name/scope is visible during the connection flow without exposing credentials.
- [ ] Tests cover successful connection, re-authentication, cancellation, and an unavailable selected proxy.

## Area

- Dashboard / UI
- Proxy / Routing
- OAuth / Authentication

## Related Provider(s)

OAuth providers in general; Codex is the primary use case.

## Additional Context

This proposal is a UX-oriented continuation of the existing proxy work, especially:

- #119 — proxy support for provider authorization and connection tests
- #425 — saved proxy registry and provider/account proxy selection
- #2603 — scoped proxy assignment precedence
- PR #3051 — fail-closed behavior for account-scoped OAuth usage traffic

Thank you to everyone who worked on these features. The current proxy system is already powerful; this would mainly make the safest per-account workflow easier to discover and harder to misconfigure. 😊

The browser remains outside OmniRoute's control, so users who require the browser login and server-side OAuth exchange to share one IP would still configure the same proxy in their browser separately.

## Expected Test Plan

- Add unit coverage for storing a selected proxy with pending OAuth state.
- Add integration coverage for transferring the selected proxy assignment to a newly created connection.
- Add re-auth coverage proving that the existing account proxy is reused by default.
- Add cleanup coverage for cancelled/expired flows.
- Keep existing OAuth flows unchanged when no proxy is explicitly selected.

title: fix(providers): video via /v1/videos/generations — Agnes poll returns 404 task not found (missing model_name in agnes-video-job poll)
body:
## Symptom

Generating a video via `/v1/videos/generations` through a custom OpenAI-compatible video provider node using the `agnes-video-job` preset: the `submit` reaches Agnes Video upstream, but the subsequent poll always fails.

```
POST /v1/videos/generations
{ "model": "agnes/agnes-video-2.5-flash", "mode": "text", "prompt": "..." }
```

Evidence of upstream connectivity: the submit can surface Agnes' own `429 rate limit exceeded: allows 2 requests / 1 minute` error. When it is not rate-limited, the poll always returns:

```
HTTP 404 {"error":{"code":404,"message":"task not found"}}
```

Reproduces consistently and is unrelated to polling timeout (fails immediately even with long waits).

- Environment: self-hosted OmniRoute (release/v3.8.51), custom video provider node configured with `generationConfig.preset: "agnes-video-job"` (+ `providerSpecificData.baseUrl`).
- Verified against `main` too: the preset is unchanged there.

## Root cause

In `open-sse/handlers/videoGeneration/job.ts` the `agnes-video-job` preset does submit→poll:

```ts
submit: { method: "POST", path: "/v1/videos", ... },        // returns video_id
poll:   { pathTemplate: "/agnesapi?video_id={taskId}" },    // <-- missing model_name
```

After `POST /v1/videos` returns a valid `video_id`, the poll does `GET {baseUrl}/agnesapi?video_id={taskId}` **without a `model_name` parameter**. Agnes' `/agnesapi` result endpoint requires `model_name` to locate the task and its result URL; without it the task cannot be found and it answers `task not found`.

Cross-check: a working client (to the same Agnes baseUrl) queries `GET /agnesapi?video_id=<id>&model_name=agnes-video-2.x` and gets `status=completed` with `metadata.url`. Dropping `model_name` yields the 404 above.

## Suggested fix

Make the poll path model-aware. Add a `{model}` substitution to the preset and to the poll URL assembly:

```ts
poll: { pathTemplate: "/agnesapi?video_id={taskId}&model_name={model}" },
```

and replace `{model}` with the effective model name (provider prefix stripped — the same value passed to Agnes upstream in `submit.buildBody`) when building `pollUrl` in `handleVideoJobGeneration()`. `buildBody` already receives `model`, so carrying it into the poll path is low risk.

## Notes

- Affects all self-hosted users of the `agnes-video-job` preset, including the shipped free `agnes-video-2.5-flash`.
